### The light shafts have a pixel shader of their own
2026-09-26

**What.** The additive draw calls of `.TRG` material 2 - the light shafts, lamp cones and
window and candle glows - are drawn with a pixel shader of their own, `hd_glow.hlsl`,
behind the room's own vertex shader. It draws what the room pixel shader draws in the
additive pass and multiplies four fades onto it: near the eye, where a card is seen
edge-on (`|N.V|`), at the card sides of a part cut out of the middle of its page, and at
both ends of an asset cut out of its page along v. Three weight presets of material 2
are raised where the fades would take a glow under 55 per cent of the mean the sum
drew. Every other additive material, material 16 included, is drawn by the room shader
as before.

**Why.** After screen composition the clipping was gone, and what stayed was measured
in the same fixed views (RoomProbe `-glow`, the glow alone over the scene's depth):
- The cards' own edges. Neighbour steps of more than 40 of 255 stood at 2633 in ANDREA2
  room 131's side view, 3488 inside it, 4413 from 4811 -1250 5864, 2097 in RICH1 room
  3's corridor view and 2614 inside the grate shaft, and at 6386 in the sweep view of
  ANDREA2 131. The window shaft takes u 48..206 of page 3038, whose columns there still
  carry 61 to 64 per cent of the brightest one, so every card side is a line.
- The camera inside a shaft: the glow's mean over its pixels was 119.9 of 255 inside
  ANDREA2's shaft and 127.4 inside RICH1's, the additive pass covering 85.6 and 88.1 per
  cent of the frame.
- A card seen in its own plane: TITLE room 6 from 6013 -151 3599 shows its streaks
  converging on the plane's vanishing point.
- RICH1's grate shaft is a cylinder of cards whose vertex light is a flat 1.0, a block
  of equal brightness with the rings of its foot showing, where `|N.V|` gives the chord
  profile of a column.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_glow.hlsl` (new) includes `hd_room.hlsl` and so reads
the same `VS_OUT`, registers and `BulbIntensity`; `GlowPS` is `RoomPS` in the additive
pass - texel, alpha test, vertex and dynamic light, WaterTable term, distance fog, the
ceiling of one, the bulbs' darkening, the caustic, texel alpha, weight and swing - less
the ripple, the gloss and the bulbs' added colour, which are zero on these draw calls,
and times the fades (`:188`-`:212`):
- near: `smoothstep` over `HD_GLOW_NEAR` = 1024 units of `|viewPos|` (`:73`, `:190`);
- facing: `|N.V|` with the interpolated file normal, or with the face normal out of
  `ddx`/`ddy` of the view position (`:202`), chosen per part by a constant;
- edge: `smoothstep` over the outer 15 per cent of the part's used u range (`:205`);
- ends: `smoothstep` over the fade length at both ends of the asset along its page-v
  axis, `dot(roomPos, axis)` against the asset's ends in the drawn room's frame (`:209`).

The fade near the eye and the `|N.V|` term are TROne's rules for its glow material:
TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931, credited in the
shader's header; the file-normal variant, the edge and the end fade are this project's.
The per-draw constants sit in c77 to c79 (`:98`), which no pixel shader of the renderer
reads or holds a literal in; the glow shader's own literals take c0 to c15 outside c4
and c10 and c36 to c39, so gRipple (c36) is written again when the room shader comes
back. `hd_glow_ps.inc` is 479 instruction slots; `bshader.bat` compiles it with the
others (`:53`, stamp `:64`) and `be.bat` guards it (`:56`, `:76`).

`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`:
- `BuildGlowParts` (`:1516`) runs before the build loop (`:3053`) and takes per material
  2 part with additive triangles: the u and v range; the edge fade where u spans less than
  90 per cent of the page (`:1652`); the face normal where `|N.f|` is under 0.9 on more
  than half of the part's corners (`:1653`); the page-v axis as the mean of dP/dv over
  its triangles. Parts of one tuple and one page whose world boxes come within a sector
  (`kGlowTouch`, `:1490`) join one asset (`:1707`); the rooms' origins for that come with
  the room boxes, `HDRoomBox::originX/originZ` (`hd_render.h:210`, filled at
  `hd_level.cpp:1085` and `RoomProbe.cpp:3909`), and without them an asset is one
  group's parts. The asset's axis is the sum of its parts', its ends the extent of all
  their vertices along it; the end fade is 512 units (`kGlowEndFade`, `:1488`), at most a
  quarter of the extent, and only for an asset with a part that uses less than 90 per
  cent of the page's v (`:1756`). `GlowConstants` (`:1818`) turns a part into the three
  registers; a fade that does not apply gets a range the pixel never leaves.
- The glow part is in the additive sort key after the material (`:3650`) and in the range
  merge (`:3722`); the parts are numbered in file order, so the triangle order is the one
  before.
- `draw_pass` switches to the glow shader for a range with a glow part and back to the
  room shader for any other and at the end of the pass (`:4780`-`:4798`, `:4965`), the
  per-part registers written when the part changes.
- `GlowGain` (`:472`) multiplies the weight of a glow part by its preset's gain (`:3277`).
- `HDRenderGlowOverride` takes a third switch, `noShader` (`:2383`), and
  `HDRenderGlowPartCount` / `HDRenderGlowPartInfo` hand the decisions to the tool;
  `HDRenderStats` counts `glowParts`, `glowEdgeParts`, `glowFaceParts`, `glowAssets`.

Tools: `RoomProbe -glowps 0|1` (`RoomProbe.cpp:3480`) draws material 2 with the room
shader (0) or the glow shader (1, the renderer's own), and the additive block prints a
`glow:` line and one `glow part:` line per part (`:4303`, `:4314`).

**Checked.** The fixed list of 46 views of the first half, six pictures each (full,

### The light shafts are as faint as the church mist
2026-09-27

**What.** The glow shader's gain on a `.TRG` material 2 part is set per preset - the
whole parameter tuple - so that every light shaft, ray fan, lamp cone and window glow
shows at the strength of the church mist of ANDY2 room 6: in its brightest view it is
no brighter than that mist, barely visible. The mist itself, the candle halos beside
it, ANDREA1's haze and RICH2 room 78's glow keep a gain of 1.

**Why.** The mist of page 2100, preset (1, 0.2, 2, 1), is the strength that is right
as the game draws it after the fades, and it is the measure here.
- The mist's level. RoomProbe over ANDY2 room 6 from 8150 7000 2100, yaw -94, pitch 2.2,
  fov 86.2 - the view of a recording of that room at 2.1 seconds, matched by the gradient
  correlation of the pictures (0.40 at 320 x 180; window, arch and post within about 20
  pixels at 1280 x 720). Over the pixels the mist's glow lights above 2 of 255 (25.7 per
  cent of the frame) its light is 5.2 on average and 8.0 at the 95th percentile, and its
  share of the frame - the frame with material 2 drawn against the frame with no additive
  material, in luma - is 5.1 on average and 8.0 at the 95th percentile, 20.7 per cent of
  the frame's luma there. Above 8 of 255 lie only 0.84 per cent of the frame - the near
  candle halos (29 per cent of those pixels) and two brighter patches of the mist by the
  far wall: mean 12.6, 95th percentile 23.3, 30.9 per cent of the frame's luma. As a
  picture measurement, the recording shows the mist 4.55 +- 0.54 of 255 above the ring 16
  to 48 pixels around it, over 19 steady frames, with the scene's own contrast taken out
  through RoomProbe's frame without additive material; RoomProbe's own frame gives 4.45
  over the same pixels. The raw lift over the ring is only about 1 of 255; most of the
  4.55 is the background correction taken from RoomProbe's frame, so the agreement rests
  largely on RoomProbe itself.
- The flash that comes now and then in that room is not a gain of material 2. The
  recording shows bursts of 0.8 to 1.3 seconds, three to four seconds apart, that step at
  30 Hz, the logic tick; each lifts the lit surfaces of the room's middle and right (up to
  2.3 times, the left wall not at all, the texture showing in the difference, so light is
  added) and with them the beams of page 2100, because the glow shader multiplies the page
  by the room's light. No file of the HD path reads the storm's `LightningRGB`
  (`game/draw.cpp`), and the source of the burst was not isolated; the bursts' length and
  spacing do match the storm clock there (`LightningCount` runs 16 to 47 ticks, a strike
  starts with a chance of 1 in 128 per tick), so the storm reaches the room by some path
  other than the sky's. It is left as it is.
- The Remaster's picture, measured on recordings of the Remaster and of this build.
  The title flyby is spline sequence 1 of the TITLE `.TRC`'s spot cameras, computed
  as `game/spotcam.cpp` does and drawn by RoomProbe with the roll applied after;
  the matched ticks correlate 0.46 to 0.73 with this build's recording, the
  Remaster's frames 0.40 to 0.72 with it, at a lag of 0.65 seconds. The far ray fan
  of page 2146 seen past the churchyard wall (9.2, 9.8 and 10.4 seconds) stands 20.0
  of 255 above its ring in this build's recording and -5.3 +- 2.0 in the Remaster's:
  no lift at all within the background's own error, a ratio of 0.1 or less. The fans
  over the sky (1.0 to 2.6 seconds) cover 26 to 38 per cent of the frame, their ring
  lies on the church and the ground, and they could not be measured. ANDREA2 room 131
  could not be matched: this build's recording only roughly, the Remaster's not at all
  (it follows another camera), and the Remaster's recording shows no shaft in that
  room in any frame from 4 to 15 seconds. That scene leans on the mist.
- The rule of the entry before - no preset under 55 per cent of its brightness before
  the fades - kept the shafts far above the mist: the 95th percentile of the share of
  the frame, in each preset's brightest view, was 191.8 in ANDREA2 room 131, 223.5 in
  room 225, 42.6 at the title's ray fans (TITLE room 6 from 7000 -400 1500) against
  the mist's 8.0; in the title flyby RoomProbe put the far fan 15.4 above its ring.
- One factor for all does not do: the gains that reach the mist lie from 0.0128
  (ANDREA3 room 36's window glow) to 0.584 (JOBY5 room 115's glow), ANDREA2 room
  131's shaft at 0.0273 and the title's fans at 0.171.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: `GlowGain` (`:454`-`:520`) holds 22 entries keyed
by the four parameters exactly as the file stores them (literals checked bit for bit
against all 26 material 2 tuples of the fifteen files); a tuple the table does not
name draws at 1. The gain multiplies the weight of a draw call that carries a glow
part (`:3311`), which exists only for the glow shader: with `-glowps 0`, as in
`HDRenderGlowOverride`'s `noShader`, no glow part is built and no gain applies. Each
gain was found by drawing: the brightest RoomProbe view of the tuple, `-glow -addmat 2`
against `-addmat 99`, the 95th percentile of the share of the frame over the pixels
the glow of 29c4d45 lit above 2, the gain scaled by 8 over it and the view drawn again,
four rounds at most; an 8-bit frame drops a card's share once it falls under half a
step, so the picture does not follow a gain this small in proportion: the window glow
of ANDREA2 room 225 reads 20.0, 10.9, 3.7 and 7.7 at gains of 0.042, 0.0168, 0.0124
and 0.0146.

### The sky
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-08

**What.** Where a level's `.TRG` carries a sky group, the HD path draws the Remaster's
own sky - a panorama band and one to three cloud discs - in the classic horizon mesh's
place, and the classic horizon mesh and its two flat colour layers are left out; the
moon, the stars and the lightning flash still run, and layer 1 survives the dome when
`GF_LIGHTNING` is set, and only then, because the game paints the flash through that
layer in the lightning's own colour. Rain and snow were never part of this phase and are
untouched. Where a level has no sky group the engine's procedural sky is drawn as before
and the HD walls paint over it: JOBY3 and JOBY5 have none, TITLE has two, and the other
twelve levels have one, always the last group. The sky group's alpha pass blends -
source alpha against one minus source alpha, alpha reference 0 - where every other
alpha-pass group is an alpha test at 0.5, and its depth write stays on.

**Why.** Every `.TRG` whose level has a sky ends in one group past the last room: an
origin-centred dome spanning the full int16 range - ANDREA1 group 242, x -17250..17250,
y -3956..3956, 1580 alpha triangles; RICH1 group 165 the same; JOBY4 group 137, plus or
minus 4098 - real geometry that was at first deliberately not drawn, TROne drawing its
own dome only because its games have no procedural sky. The group holds the band (1,280
triangles on a sphere of about four blocks' radius, 21 rings, radius 1060 at the poles
and 4100 at the equator, wearing one 4096 x 2048 panorama out of the page block
7000..7011, alpha 0 above the horizon line and opaque below it) and one to three flat
cloud discs of up to 24,000 units' radius at fixed heights above the camera, material 1,
which therefore scroll on their own parameters (`p1` -0.03 to 0.06 page units per
second) and carry baked light of 0.26 to 2.00. The band's baked light is exactly zero on
every vertex of every level, so through the room formula it would be black. The two
alpha-pass sky pages carry a soft ramp with every value in between - 42.0 per cent of
their texels under alpha 16 and 35.9 per cent over 240 for the second cloud sheet, 33.5
and 59.2 for the dome - and a test at 0.5 leaves a feathered cloud as a hard-edged
silhouette and puts a hard rim across the dome. The depth write stays on, unlike the glass
surfaces, because the sky sorts inside itself in its own depth slice: the dome stands in
front of the cloud sheets at the horizon and behind them overhead.

**How.** A sky part with no light anywhere is drawn at light 1 and its page is the whole
picture. No scaling and no rotation: the sphere's four blocks sit far inside the far
plane of 20480, the discs reach past it, which only cuts a disc where the band already
covers it, and the group is centred on the origin, so it takes the matrix the classic
path builds for its own horizon - `phd_TranslateAbs(camera.pos)` and nothing else - and
rides on the camera exactly as the horizon did. Because the discs hang in front of the
band overhead and behind it at the horizon, no draw order gets both right, so the sky is
given its own depth range instead: the viewport's `MinZ` is pushed to `HD_SKY_MINZ` =
0.996 for the length of the call, folding the whole sky into the last four thousandths
of the depth buffer, where the depth test sorts it properly and outside which every
pixel of the world is nearer, the classic depth of the far plane itself being only 0.995
(`SetupZRange(20, 20480)`: a - b/z = 0.99500); the viewport is read back and put
together again before the call returns. The dome is drawn in `SkyDrawPhase`
(`game/draw.cpp`), in the classic horizon mesh's own place in that function - after the
moon and before the stars, because none of the three writes depth and the order in that
function is the order on the screen; drawn with the rooms in `HDFrameDraw` it would have
painted over the moon. It rides on the classic path's own two gates because it is drawn
inside them - `outside`, which `GetRoomBounds` sets when a room that sees the sky is in
view, and `objects[HORIZON].loaded`, which `SkyDrawPhase` returns on - so a level with
an HD sky group but no classic HORIZON object draws no sky at all. The blend branch is
in `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp:3245`, in the alpha pass state block (`gPass.x` carrying
the alpha reference); only a group past the last room takes it, and `HDRenderRoomMask`
is the one place that still knows a group's number. Texture addressing needed no change:
the renderer already sets `D3DTADDRESS_CLAMP` for every range that does not scroll and
`WRAP` only for the ones that do, which is what TROne's sky finding (a clamp-to-edge
sampler for the painted dome) asks for. The opaque and the alpha pass multiply by
exactly one and the sort key's two new fields are constant across them, so no ordinary
surface can change. `RoomProbe` gained `-sky` and `-skyonly` (whose device-state bracket
reports no watched state left changed after the sky call) and `-groups`; the engine
writes one `HDLOG ... sky groups=` line per level.

**Commits.** `1087750`, `c0f9ede`, `5285f99`

### A floor whose page is part-way clear is drawn blended, and a mirror shows the room's items
2026-09-29

**What.** Two rules of the HD level. The alpha-pass triangles of a room whose page is
part-way clear in every texel - every texel at or above the alpha test's 0.5, the smallest
at most 243 of 255 - are no longer drawn with the alpha test but blended, `SRCALPHA` over
`INVSRCALPHA` with the depth write on, in a phase of their own (`HD_PASS_CLEAR`) after
every room's solid art and before the models and the classic buckets. And the two washroom
mirrors of RICH2 show Lara and the items in front of them: with an HD level active, every
item whose reflection in a mirror's plane lands in the copy of the room behind the glass
is drawn once more through a view reflected in that plane, and Lara the same.

**Why.** The Remaster builds RICH2's polished floors as a floor on pages at alpha 231 to
239 lying over an upside-down copy of the room: the lobby, room 8, is 657 floor triangles
on pages 1047 and 1045 (0.917 on the average) over 2,895 triangles of copy. The alpha test
at 0.5 kept every texel of those pages and drew the floor solid, so the copy was drawn and
never seen. An inventory of every alpha-pass page of the fifteen `.TRG` files, decoded
with the engine's own BC7 reader, finds the class in three levels: RICH2, 13 pages (1029,
1045, 1047, 1049, 1053, 1079 and 1081 at 231 to 239, the inlaid floors 3314 to 3319 at 231
to 255) with 17,989 triangles; RICHCUT2, page 1103 (211 to 255) with 936; TITLE, pages
2147, 2149 and 2154 (174 to 255) with 1,860; no other level has one. The glass pages of
the same range (3068 and 3309, 165 to 247) are material 14 and were blended already. The
mirrors: TR5 has no mirror of its own. Neither the game's SCRIPT.DAT nor the original one
carries a `CMD_MIRROR` or sets `GF_MIRROR` for any level, so `gfMirrorRoom` stays unset
and `Draw_Mirror_Lara` never runs. The Remaster builds its two washroom mirrors out of
art, a copy of the room reflected in the wall behind a pane, and the copy holds nothing
that moves: at the glass a player saw the cabins and a toilet in it, no Lara and no doors,
and looked straight into the cabins.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_pageclass.h:59`, `HDPageClassOf`, is the class, a pure function
of the smallest and the largest alpha. `hd_pagecache.cpp:682-697` measures both over every
texel of the top mip a page keeps, beside the cut-out share and on the decoding thread;
`:1302` keeps the class per slot and `:1703`, `HDPageCacheSlotClear`, answers it.
`hd_render.cpp:4516` decides per triangle: an alpha-pass triangle of a room group, not
glass already, on a clear page gets blend 1 (its page's own alpha) and `HDRange::clear`.
`draw_pass` draws the clear ranges alone when asked with `clearOnly` (`:5766` the depth
write, `:5780` the filter), `HDRenderRoomMask` draws them after a room's alpha pass
(`:6190`), and `hd_level.cpp:4549` draws `HD_PASS_CLEAR` for every room of the frame that
has one, after the solid loop. `hd_render.cpp:2552`, `FindMirrors`, runs at the level
build (`:5019`) over the four walls of every room's inside box and records a mirror where
the wall has a pane (triangles in its plane in the additive pass or of material 14), a
room's worth of the group's art behind it (100 triangles or more, reaching 1,024 units
deep) and 90 per cent of that art the reflection of the level's art in front to one 8-unit
cell; `HDRenderMirrorInfo` and `hd_level.cpp:4034`, `HDLevelMirrorCount` and
`HDLevelMirrorAt`, hand them to the game. `game/draw.cpp:2498` calls `Draw_Mirror_Items`
(`game/mirror.cpp:285`) after Lara's own draw and before the rooms' objects are printed,
while the mirror room's portal window is still this frame's. For a mirror whose room is on
the draw list and whose glass faces the camera, `DrawOneMirror` (`:156`) copies the view -
`w2v_matrix`, `aW2VMx` and the bases of both matrix stacks - and reflects it
(`game/mirror_math.h`, `MirrorView`: the view's column of the plane's axis negated, the
camera reflected). It draws every item in front of the glass whose reflected origin lands
in the copy's box, with 256 units of slack along the glass's normal and in height and none
along the glass (`MirrorLandsInCopy`), through `PrintObjectReflection`
(`game/draw.cpp:1182`, the item loop's body with the mirror's room as the clip room),
moves Lara's fifteen matrices into the reflected view (`MirrorViewSpaceApply`) and draws
her with `DrawLara(lara_item, 1)`, and copies the view back. The classic path's winding
test is turned round with `SetCullCW` as `Draw_Mirror_Lara` turns it; the HD models are
drawn double sided (`hd_object.cpp:3014`) and need nothing, and HD Lara in first person
culls the other side on her mirror flag (`hd_laradraw.cpp:1309`). `HDObjectReflection`
(`hd_object.cpp:3037`) tells the object seam the items are a reflection: they are left out
of the two light checks (`:3023`) and counted for the mirror's log line. A reflected item
casts no shadow - its slot's `shadow_size` is 0 for the call - and its ambient fade, which
`CalcAmbientLight` steps per draw, is put back. The motion line of `HDLOG level=` ends in
` clear_pages=%d clear_parts=%d mirrors=%d`, the level's first frame line in
` clear_calls=%d`; one `HDLOG mirrorwall` line per mirror at the build, and
`HDLOG mirror items=%d plane=%ld room=%d axis=%c lara=%d hd=%d` once a second while a
mirror draws. `RoomProbe` draws the clear phase in its frame and in the alpha-pass
picture of `-all` (`HDRenderRoomPass`), gives the before picture with `-noclear`, and
prints a `clear:` line and, with `-roombox`, the mirrors.

**Checked.** The inventory, by a probe built against the engine's BC7 decoder and the
`.TRG` reader, over all fifteen levels, and the engine's own count through `RoomProbe
-nodraw`: 55 parts on 13 pages and 150 draw calls in RICH2 (149 without the room boxes),
one part on one page in one draw call in RICHCUT2, nine parts on three pages in nine draw
calls in TITLE, none elsewhere. Against a `RoomProbe` built from the tree before this
entry the vertex, index and range counts and the glass lines of all fifteen levels are the
same, and renders of JOBY3 room 9, ANDREA2 room 65 and RICH2 room 134 are the same to the
pixel. Every RICH2 group with a clear floor holds art beneath its floor's plane, down to
the one-sector doorways (groups 53, 54, 90, 95, 97, 101, 103, 117, 118, 154 and 176), but
for groups 170 and 171: their own art holds nothing beneath the floor but 18 vertical
triangles, and the neighbouring group 84's copy lies under the whole of both sectors, so
they show it only while 84 is drawn. TITLE groups 50 and 51 hold none. The lobby from the
pose `RICH2 8 4100 -25300 1700 -12 35 -size 1600 900 -roombox`: with `-noclear` the same
to the pixel as the build before, without it 792,628 of 1,440,000 pixels change, all on
the floor, which shows the copy's doorway and a light stripe faintly. The mirrors, through
`RoomProbe -roombox` over the fifteen levels: RICH2 room 134 (plane x = 33792, pane 12,
6,161 triangles behind reaching 2,054 deep, 6,107 reflected; copy x 31738..33785, y
-25607..-24042, z 74758..78848) and room 135 (x = 30720, pane 16, 6,237 behind, 6,201
reflected), nothing else; the rule costs 77 ms of the level build in RICH2 and 13 to 21 ms
in ANDREA1, JOBY2 and JOBY5. The items the rule draws, out of the original RICH2 item
list: in room 134's glass the kick doors 189, 190 and 192 of cabins 131 to 133, the
ceiling trapdoor 188, and Lara; in room 135's the kick doors 199, 200 and 202 of cabins
136 to 138, the large medipack 201 and room 177's door 246; the three ANIMATING4 items of
each washroom (193 to 195 and 196 to 198) and the generator slot 247 count in `items=` but
draw nothing, because RICH2 binds them to the DUMMY slot and the room art carries them,
and the electrical light 191 has no draw routine; nothing that stands behind either glass;
every one of them inside the copy's box along the glass. ModernTest pins the class, the
reflection and the point past a copy's end (14,018 checks become 14,050); MenuTest 42,364,
InterpTest 683, and LipsTest 270 with the lip objects and 243 without, all without a
failure. The mirror itself cannot be drawn outside the game - `RoomProbe` draws no item -
so its picture is the play test's.

**Unchanged.** `hd_enable 0`: the clear phase is part of `HDFrameDraw`, whose rooms are
the HD ones only, and the page class exists only in the page cache the HD level builds;
`Draw_Mirror_Items` is called behind `HDLevelActive()` (`game/draw.cpp:2498`), false with
`hd_enable` off (`hd_level.cpp:3126`), and `HDLevelMirrorCount` asks it again (`:4036`).
The classic mirror of Lara and its call, the classic item loop, the tick, the logic camera
and the savegames: nothing of them is written - the reflection lives in the view and in
copies of it, and an item's own position and pose are never touched. The three frame-rate
modes alike: the reflection draws the pose the frame draws. Every alpha-pass page outside
the class keeps the alpha test; the glass and the cut-outs of every level are as they
were.

**Decisions.** A rule from the data and no list per level: a page part-way clear in every
texel is meant to be seen through. The class reads the smallest alpha: from the alpha
test's reference, 128, up to 243 - halfway between the highest smallest alpha of a floor
over a copy (233, TITLE page 2149) and the first near-opaque page (254, JOBY3 pages 14070
and 14071, ANDY1 page 793, three sky sheets); a page that also carries texels at 255 stays
in the class, because the floors of TITLE and RICHCUT2 and RICH2's inlaid ones do, and a
texel at 255 blends as solid. The floor keeps the depth write and is drawn in a phase of
its own before the models, not with the glass after everything: Lara stands on it, her
shadow falls 16 units above it, and the glass and the glows of the copy must stay beneath
it. HD only. The mirrors come from the art, because the script has none, and every item
whose reflection lands in the copy is drawn, not a list of objects. The reflection is put
into the view and not into the item, so every item keeps the pose the frame draws: a pose
written into the item needs the -1 scale `CalcLaraMatrices(2)` gives Lara and
`DrawAnimatingItem` does not have, and both mirrors stand in planes of constant x, which
the z plane of `Draw_Mirror_Lara` does not serve. A reflected item casts no shadow of its
own and its effects are not reflected.

**Left.** TITLE groups 50 and 51 carry the class on page 2154 with nothing beneath the
floor in their own art: there the floor blends over whatever the frame holds behind it and
comes out a little darker (`RoomProbe` over black: a mean of 18.1 against 17.0 of 255 in
group 51); whether the title flyby ever shows it is the play test's. RICH2 groups 170 and
171, two one-sector doorways, hold nothing beneath their floor in their own art; the
neighbouring group 84's copy lies under the whole of both sectors, so they show it only
while 84 is drawn. Shadows and effects - flames, sparks, the gun flash - of what the
mirror reflects. The lobby floor shows its static copy only: Lara and the items are not
reflected in it. In first person the reflected Lara is drawn the way the first-person draw
draws her, without her face and her braid. A reflection is held only by the depth test and
not cut to the pane: a body whose origin stands at a copy's end along the glass can reach
about 100 units past it, into corridor room 56 or doorway room 130. `DrawLara` steps its
look-transparency fade once per call, so while a mirror draws Lara the fade back from look
mode runs twice as fast. The frame line's object counts (`objects=`, `object_calls=` and
the `hd=`, `classic=`, `baked=` line) include the reflected draws. A Lara drawn the
classic way, without an HD body, takes into a second mirror's glass the light the first
mirror's last item left, since `DrawLara` with the mirror flag keeps the light arrays; in
one mirror she is drawn before its items for that reason. The play test judges the lobby's
brightness, the floor's edge, a kicked door swinging open in the glass, the 56 to 177
doorway and the way from 134 to 130 for a second Lara, and that nothing is doubled outside
the glass.

### The reflection stays behind the glass
2026-09-29

**What.** A mirror's reflection is drawn only where the copy of the room behind the glass
is. The HD draws of a reflection, the items and every piece of Lara with the braid, are
clipped per pixel in the model shader against three planes: the copy's side of the glass
and the copy's two ends along it. The classic draws of a reflection are cut by the classic
clipper to the copy's rectangle on the screen. When an item or Lara is reflected does not
change.

**Why.** The mirror decides by an origin (`MirrorLandsInCopy`) and nothing bounded the
body drawn about it. The log of a RICH2 run with HD on holds a still camera for 151 ticks
(`CAMLOG` 44985 to 53016): eye (31953, -25213, 74166) in corridor room 56, target (30877,
-24723, 74784) in doorway room 177, and 26 lines `HDLOG mirror items=8 plane=30720
room=135 axis=x`, `lara=1` on 21 of them. Glass 135's copy is the box x 28669..30716, y
-25607..-24042, z 74764..79872 (its `mirrorwall` line). Lara's origin reflected in x =
30720 stands at (30563, -24723, 74784), 20 units inside the copy's end at z 74764; a body
150 units about it reaches to z 74634, 130 units past that end, 118 of them over room
56's floor (z 73728..74752), which is open west of the glass's plane (x 29696..30720).
From the corridor that part of her stood in front of the corridor's north wall: a
second Lara beside the doorway, her other half inside the wall of room 177. The same cause

### A seam for the poison sway
2026-09-29

**What.** With `-log`, two `POISONLOG` lines while Lara is poisoned (`lara.poisoned` or
`lara.dpoisoned` not zero). A `view` line per build of the view matrix: `call=`, `tick=`,
`tween=`, `rebuild=`, `who=`, `poisoned=`, `dpoisoned=` and `scale=`, the three factors
the sway applied to the matrix stack's base (16384 when it applied none). A `frame` line
per drawn frame: `frame=`, `tick=`, `tween=`, `alpha=`, `base=` and `poisoned=`, `base=`
being the three column lengths of the float stack's base times 10000 (10000 unscaled).

**Why.** In RICH3's gas the sway is absent or faint at the interpolated frame rates and
normal at 30; after a stretch at 30 the interpolated rates look right. Two readings fit.
The sway's amplitude never rises at the interpolated rates, because the ramp that walks
`lara.poisoned` towards `lara.dpoisoned` does not step there; or the scale sits on the
frames that carry a logic tick and is missing on the frames between them, because a
rebuild of the view builds it without. The `view` line tells the first (a `poisoned=`
that stands while `dpoisoned=` moves), the `frame` line the second (a `base=` at 10000 on
the in-between frames only).

**How.** `specific/3dmath.cpp:602`, `PoisonLogView`, writes the `view` line;
`aGenerateW2V` calls it behind `gLogEnabled` after its scale block (`:713`) with its own
scale vector, which holds the factors only when the block scaled. `who=` reads two flags:
`PoisonLogRebuild` (`:586`), set by `RebuildView` around its `phd_LookAt`
(`game/interpolate.cpp:733`, `:735`), and `PoisonLogTickCamera` (`:591`), set by
`ControlPhase` around the tick's camera block, `CalculateCamera` or `CalculateSpotCams`
(`game/control.cpp:653`, `:679`); every other view build is `other` - the pickup icon,
the gun's aim view in `FireWeapon`, the load screen, the inventory. `PoisonLogFrame`
(`3dmath.cpp:623`) writes the `frame` line from `aMXPtr`; `DrawPhaseGame` reads
`InterpAlphaNow` once into a local, hands it to `InterpBeginFrame` (`game/draw.cpp:470`)
and then to `PoisonLogFrame` behind `gLogEnabled` (`:473`). `phd_GenerateW2V`'s own scale
block has no line: it runs right before `aGenerateW2V` in the same call, one ramp step
earlier and with the same phases.

**Checked.** The engine builds without an error; ModernTest 14,063, MenuTest 42,364,
InterpTest 683, LipsTest 270 with the lip objects and 243 without, all without a failure;
RoomProbe and TrgProbe build.

**Unchanged.** Everything the engine does: the ramp, the scale, the tick, the camera, the
matrices and the draw order. The two flags are written whether `-log` is on or not and
only the log reads them; the two counters step only with `-log`; `InterpAlphaNow` is read
once per frame as before. `hd_enable 0` draws the same picture.

**Left.** The fix, once a log of a poisoning at an interpolated rate says which reading
holds.

### A tick is never a tween frame
2026-09-29

**What.** A logic tick lowers the tween latch at its first statement, so the poison ramp
that the tick's own camera steps runs once per tick at every frame rate: in RICH3's gas
the green veil and the sway rise, and the poison deals its damage, at the interpolated
rates as at 30. The counters that sit before `DrawPhaseGame` in a loop read the latch of
the frame drawn last, which the tick leaves standing. A frame drawn between two ticks
builds its view at the sway's phases of its own time instead of the tick's.

**Why.** The game loop draws first and ticks after: `DoLevel` calls `DrawPhaseGame` and
then `ControlPhase` (`game/gameflow.cpp:1155`, `:1174`), `DoTitle` the same (`:923`,
`:925`). The latch `InterpBeginFrame` sets at the top of a frame was lowered only by the
next frame, a 30 Hz present or an invalidation, so it outlived its frame and stood
through the tick that followed. At fps_mode 2 the frame that carries a tick is the first
one drawn after it, so whenever a tick lasts two frames or more the frame before the next
tick is a tween frame. The ramp guard in both halves of `phd_GenerateW2V`,
`lara.dpoisoned != lara.poisoned && !InterpIsTweenFrame()`, read that latch from
`CalculateCamera`, the spot cameras and `FireWeapon`'s aim view, and `lara.poisoned`, the
sway's amplitude, stood. Measured with POISONLOG in RICH3: at 165 Hz from a fresh
poisoning every tick build ran under the latch (`who=tick tween=1`), `lara.poisoned` 0
throughout while `lara.dpoisoned` climbed from 2 to 1006 in fifteen seconds; at 30
`poisoned` climbed from 122 to 2091 following `dpoisoned`; back at 165 it froze at 2108
while `dpoisoned` climbed to 2535. The frames between two ticks carried the same scale as
the tick's frame (the same `base=` on `tween=0` and `tween=1` frames, none unscaled), so
the scale itself was never at fault. And the tick's poison block (`game/control.cpp:604`,
`if (lara.poisoned && !GLOBAL_playing_cutseq)`: the climb of `dpoisoned`, the office
levels' decay and the poison damage) never ran while `poisoned` was 0, so at 165 Hz a
fresh poisoning dealt no damage either. The one ramp step left at fps_mode 2 was
`S_DrawPickup`'s `phd_LookAt` (`specific/output.cpp:70`) on the frame that carries a
tick, while a pickup icon was on screen. At fps_mode 1 the frame before a tick is live,
at fps_mode 0 the latch is never up. The sway's six phases step once per tick
(`control.cpp:597` - `:602`) while at fps_mode 2 the eye moves on every frame, so the
sway held each value for five or six frames at 165 Hz and then jumped.

**How.** `InterpCapturePrev` (`game/interpolate.cpp:997`), the first statement of every
tick (`control.cpp:272`), sets `g_tween = false` (`:1007`) before `g_tickSerial++`; the
next `InterpBeginFrame` latches anew by its own rule. A second reading, `g_drawnTween`
(`:356`), is written wherever the frame side writes `g_tween` -
`InterpNoteClassicPresent` (`:1290`), `InterpNoteMenuFrame` (`:1299`),
`InterpBeginFrame` (`:1348`), `InterpInvalidate` (`:1964`) - and never by the tick;
`InterpDrawnFrameWasTween` (`:1273`, `game/interpolate.h:130`) returns it. Four readers
that sit before `DrawPhaseGame` in a loop take it, because on the lowered latch they
would step on the tick and again on the frame that carries it: the level caption
`gfLegendTime` (`gameflow.cpp:1148`), and, walked by `DoTitle` before its draw
(`:893`, `:910`, `:922`), the sky's lightning (`game/draw.cpp:590`), the credits roll
(`specific/alexstuff.cpp:437`) and the cutscene wind-up (`game/deltapak.cpp:2136`);
after `DrawPhaseGame` and before the tick the two readings are equal, so the wind-up
DoLevel calls there (`gameflow.cpp:1162`) and the sky inside a frame read what they read
before. `FireWeapon` builds its aim view in the tick (`game/larafire.cpp:795`) and is
covered by the same lowering. The sway: `InterpCapturePrev` captures the six phases
(`interpolate.cpp:1106`); `InterpBeginFrame` blends them with `LerpAngle` from the
capture to the tick's values at the frame's `alpha` and hands them to
`PoisonSwayBlend` (`specific/3dmath.cpp:649`) around its own `RebuildView` only
(`interpolate.cpp:1778` - `:1785`); both halves of `phd_GenerateW2V` read them through
`PoisonSwayPhases` (`3dmath.cpp:660`, `:745`, `:840`), the globals otherwise.

**Checked.** Every `InterpIsTweenFrame` caller read by the function it sits in. In the
tick: the ramp in both halves of `phd_GenerateW2V` (`3dmath.cpp:733`, `:828`) and
POISONLOG's `view` line, whose `tween=` now reads 0 for `who=tick`. Before `DrawPhaseGame`
in a loop: the four readers above, now on the drawn latch. Inside the frame, after
`InterpBeginFrame`, the latch is the frame's as before: the footprints, the flash and the
game info, the health bar's `PoisonFlag`, the pickups, `Fade`, `DoScreenFade`, the rain,
the snow, the underwater dust, the sparks, the lightning bolt, the floor lasers, the gas
cloud, the stars, `DrawRooms`, `frigup_lara`, `DoMonitorScreen`, the room-walk log, the
arm log and POISONLOG's `frame` line, `S_OutputPolyList` (`specific/output.cpp:1773`,
`:1875`, `:1893`), `S_DumpScreen` (`:1505`), the cutscene interpolator's log and the
ring's six (`game/newinv2.cpp`), which the ring latches itself before each of its frames.
The frame before a tick presented before the tick ran, so the per-present counters step
under its own latch as before. A modal loop entered from the tick - the pause, load, save
and death menus - or right after it - the load screen at a level's end, the title's
special-features screens - now finds the latch down on its first present, where it
inherited the last game frame's; from the second present on `InterpNoteClassicPresent` had
lowered it anyway. The inventory ring latches its own frames and is followed by
`InterpInvalidate`. InterpTest's `tick_latch` walks the loop for a simulated minute at 60
and 165 Hz under fps_mode 2 - under the frame's latch all 1,800 ticks found it up, under
the tick's none; the per-present counters, the caption on the drawn latch and the wind-up
step once per tick; the caption on the lowered latch would step 3,600 and 3,601 times -
and at fps_mode 1 and 0, where the lowering finds the latch down. `sway_phase` pins the
blend on the six steps: the capture at 0, the tick at 1, the wrap at 0x8000, never
backwards, and at 165 Hz a phase that moves on every frame, where the tick's value stands
still on 134 frames of a second's 165. The engine builds without an error; ModernTest
14,063, MenuTest 42,364, InterpTest 711 (683 before), LipsTest 270 with the lip objects
and 243 without, all without a failure; RoomProbe and TrgProbe build.

**Unchanged.** fps_mode 0 to the count: the latch is never up there, the lowering
changes nothing, the drawn latch equals it, and no frame reaches the phase blend. A live
frame at any rate draws the tick's phases. The ramp's arithmetic - a sixteenth per call,
two calls per `phd_LookAt` - and its guard, word for word; `RebuildView` keeps its save
and restore of `lara.poisoned`; `InterpEndFrame`'s rebuild restores the tick's view with
the tick's phases; the globals `XSoff1` .. `ZSoff2` are written by the tick alone. The
savegames, the level data and the HD path. POISONLOG's two lines.

**Decisions.** The latch describes a drawn frame, and a tick is no frame: the tick lowers
it at its first statement and the next frame sets it anew. The ramp guard stays word for
word; the tick's own camera builds see the latch down at every rate, and with
`S_DrawPickup` stepping on the frame that carries the tick the count per tick is the
vanilla one at every rate. The sway's phases between two ticks are blended for the view
the interpolator builds for the drawn frame and for nothing else. No change to the ramp's
speed, the damage or the office decay: they come back on their own with the amplitude.
The counters before `DrawPhaseGame` in `DoLevel` and `DoTitle` read the drawn frame's
latch, not the lowered one, which would step them twice per tick. The phases are blended
from a capture, not from the six literal steps, so a tick that returned before stepping
them draws them still.

**Left.** The play test at 165 Hz with `-log`: a fresh poisoning in RICH3 - the green
veil within seconds, the sway rising over a minute, the health dropping under the
poison, the sway smooth; the same at 30; a poisoned savegame loaded at 165 goes on rising
or decaying instead of freezing; the decay in the office levels at 165. In the log the
`view` lines with `who=tick tween=0` at 165 and `poisoned=` following `dpoisoned=`, and
`frame` lines whose `base=` changes from one `tween=1` frame to the next.

**Commits.** the commits 'Round 187b (#187): a tick is never a tween frame', 'Round 187b

and the sway's phase', 'Round 187b (#187): the record follows'

### A shine on metal, marble and ice
2026-09-30

**What.** In an HD room the surfaces of metal, marble and ice carry a sheen, whatever
way they face: floors, walls, crates, ducts, shelves and the props the .TRG bakes into
the room. It is a highlight from the room's own lamps, the level's sun and the eye, and
a reflection of the room's light, weighted by Schlick's Fresnel term and added to the
surface's own lit colour. A second compiled variant of the room pixel shader draws it,
for the draw calls whose page resolves to a gloss while `hd_reflect` is on. Four sources
name a page's gloss: the .TRG's material 3 or 17, a file `hd_gloss.txt` beside the
executable, a page table compiled into the engine, and a seed out of the classic
floor's footstep materials. With `-log`, `GLOSSLOG` says which pages shine and why.

**Why.** The .TRG has no metal class for props: ANDREA1 room 3's riveted crate, its
forklift and its overhead box are material 0 on pages whose alpha is flat (254 to 255
on the top mip). The two gloss materials, 3 (165,897 triangles) and 17 (17,453), sit
mostly on walls, and 34 of the 35 pages that carry them hold a mask - a smallest
top-mip alpha below 250 - that selects window glass, armour, ice and puddles, or is
coverage. The classic floor marks metal (footstep material 8) on 6,258 squares in ten
levels, marble (9) on 95 and ice (4) on 211. The grazing-angle lift the room shader drew
out of materials 3 and 17 was invisible even at strength 1: at most 82 of 255 on 69
pixels of that room, from RoomProbe on a copy with the strength forced. The room pixel
shader used 476 of the 512 slots shader model 3 guarantees. And the .TRG's 1,306 point
lights and 91,569 light cubes were read and counted (`hd_scan.cpp:251`) and drawn by
nothing.

**How.** The variant is `hd_room.hlsl` compiled with `HD_GLOSS`
(`specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl:517`, `GlossSheen` `:983`, the add `:1294`) into
`hd_room_gloss_ps.inc`, 499 of 512 slots (`hd_room_gloss_ps.inc:541`); it leaves out the
ripple, the caustic and the additive-pass lines, which no glossy draw call needs, and
every line that differs sits under the define. Its registers are `gGloss` in c36,
gRipple's (F0, how far the reflection takes the texel's colour, the mask switch),
`gGlossCube` c80 - c85, `gGlossAxes` c86 - c88 and `gGlossLights` c89 - c96 (four lamps);
`gSpec` c19 keeps strength, exponent and `hd_reflect`. The shading is in view space,
where `viewNrm`, `viewPos` and the eye already are: Blinn-Phong with the (n + 8) / 8
normalisation per lamp, the eye as a lamp added after that normalisation, so that its
peak is a quarter of the surface's own light whatever the exponent, the normal and the
half vector normalised under a floor, so that a zero normal gives no sheen and no NaN,
the ambient cube looked up along the reflection turned back into world axes, Schlick's
weight, the page's alpha as mask where the page has one, and the fog and the bulbs'
haze taken off the sum as off the surface. `bshader.bat` compiles it and `be.bat`
guards its stamp. `hd_render.cpp` creates it beside the plain variant (`:3332`, a device
that refuses it keeps the plain one); `draw_pass` picks it per draw call (`:6510`),
writes `gGloss` (`:6602`) and the lamps and the cube (`upload_sheen_lights`, `:6114`),
enters it after those writes (`:6719`), leaves it before a plain draw call's writes and
ends every pass on the plain variant, because each variant keeps literals in registers
the other one names. The lights: the level build keeps each room's point lights room
local and scaled (`:3707`), the cubes when their count is the count of floor squares
(`:3738`), and the sun towards it (`:3742`); `hd_level.cpp`'s `BuildRoomSectors`
(`:1438`) hands the floor squares in (`HDRenderSetSectors`, `hd_render.cpp:3496`), x-major
like `ROOM_INFO::floor` and like the cubes. `LightSheen` (`:2981`) gives a glossy draw
call the mean cube of the squares under its triangles (a wall triangle takes the square
half a square in front of it), its room's lamps nearest its box and, where the level
has a sun, the share of it its cube says it sees. The next entry replaces these lamps,
the sun and the cube with a light field of the level. Which surfaces: `ResolveSheen`
(`:3100`) runs after the sort and changes no range; `ResolvePage` (`:2913`) and
`HDGlossResolve` (`specific/hd/hd_gloss_math.h:547`) take the material first, then the
file, the table and the seed; the seed walks the rooms' surface triangles
(`hd_gloss_seed.h:50`, `HDGlossSeedVote` `hd_gloss_math.h:709`): an up-facing triangle
within 300 units of its floor square's height votes for the square's footstep
material, and a page takes metal, marble or ice when that class holds half of its
votes, at least two of them and at least one per cent of its triangles
(`HDGlossSeedClass`, `:642`); the table is `hd_gloss_pages.h:42`, 40 lines; the file is
read at every level build (`ReadGlossFile`, `hd_render.cpp:2942`, named by
`hd_level.cpp:3476`) with `HDGlossParseLine` and `HDGlossParseText`
(`hd_gloss_math.h:332`, `:481`), which steps over a UTF-8 byte order mark. The mask is
a page's smallest alpha below 250
(`HDPageCacheSlotAlphaMin`, `hd_pagecache.cpp:1723`). `MaterialGloss`
(`hd_render.cpp:1132`) reads the base material, so RICH3's destructible panes 0x8003 to
0x8403 count; `MaterialAlphaRef`,
`MaterialAddWeight` and `MaterialBookTime` go on comparing the whole number, which a
destructible piece never matches (they exist over bases 0, 3 and 14 only), so a
destructible decal keeps the additive weight 1. The seam: `GLOSSLOG` (`hd_level.cpp:3597`,
`:3610`), the HDLOG level line ends with `gloss_pages=` and `gloss_draws=` (`:3571`), and
the HDLOG frame line with `sheen_calls=`, the solid bracket's draw calls on the variant;
its `gloss_calls=` goes on counting the draw calls with a material's gloss. The tools:
TrgProbe `-gloss`, `-glossseed`, `-glossfile` and `-glosslight`; RoomProbe `-glossmax`
and `-glossfile`, and `-roombox` hands the floor squares in; ModernTest's `gloss_*`
family.

**Checked.** The engine builds without an error or a warning; ModernTest 14,116 (14,063
before), MenuTest 42,364, InterpTest 711, LipsTest 270 with the lip objects and 243
without, none failed; RoomProbe, TrgProbe, DdsProbe and ModelProbe build. The plain
room pixel shader, the room vertex shader and the glow shader compile to the bytecode of
`ca2e904` but for the stamp line. ANDREA1 room 3 from room-local (2679, -690, -1169),

**Decisions.** The shine is light-driven and orientation-free: a highlight and a
reflection of the room's light per pixel, no mirror image, no second room pass, no
stencil. The unit of selection is the texture page, beside the .TRG material per part,
and the order is the material, the file, the table, the seed: the table stands before
the seed because it holds the seed's misreadings (a relief, planks, a label atlas) as
well as what the seed cannot see, and the file before both, so that a page the seed
names can be tuned or taken out without a rebuild; a material part keeps its own
strength and exponent and takes only the class the file or the table names, so neither
can take a material 3 or 17 page out. That order corrects the one first set down for
this entry - the material, the seed, the table, the file - under which the table's
take-outs and the file's `-` line could not remove a page the seed names. RICH2's lobby
is kept out page by page: its clear-class pages (1029, 1045, 1047, 1049, 1053, 1079,
1081) and marble pages (1010, 1032, 1033) take nothing but the material, and every room
with a clear floor takes nothing at all (the next entry lets those rooms shine by page);
the other pages numbered between 1029 and 1081 are not the lobby's class and may shine,

1040 by the seed. The lamps are the room's own .TRG point lights, four at most, one of
them the sun where the level has one, and the eye at a quarter of the surface's light at
its peak, outside the exponent's (n + 8) / 8 scale; the dynamic lights give no
highlight. One cube per draw call, the mean over the squares under it, lifted by a gain

with the level's light field. F0 is 0.5 for
metal, whose reflection takes the texel's colour, and 0.08 at strength 0.6 for marble,

### The shine belongs to the place, not to the draw call
2026-10-01

**What.** The sheen of an HD room surface reads its light out of a light field of the
level: a grid of cells, one floor square across and one square up, over the part of the
rooms' boxes the .TRG's point lights reach, built once with the level's HD data, in which
every cell holds one direction towards the light - a light probe's dominant direction, the
weighted mean of the directions to the lamps within six squares - how one-sided that light
is, and one bounded colour. Two volume textures carry it to the gloss variant of the room
pixel shader, which reads them with linear filtering at the pixel's world position and
forms one Blinn-Phong highlight out of them. The per-draw-call lamps, the level's sun, the
eye as a lamp and the per-draw-call light cube are gone; the environment term is the
surface's own baked light. The whole sheen is held under the surface's own lit colour and
composed as a screen. Every room that wears a glossy page shines with it, the rooms with a
clear floor too, and a draw call with a UV scroll, a flipbook, a book or a caustic within
reach takes the sheen its page names; the water surfaces, the sky band and the clear
floors keep the plain variant and are counted per level in a new `GLOSSLOG skipped` line.
With `-log`, the GLOSSLOG level line also names the field's grid, cells, memory and build
time. The page table names three more pages, 43 lines in all: the locker doors' two
halves, 93 and 94, and 470, the twin of JOBY2's painted steel with a pipe across.

**Why.** A play test of the previous entry's sheen showed, in pictures and videos: white
discs with a cyan rim on JOBY2's diamond-plate floors that travel with the camera; steps
along straight lines - one horizontal step across RICH1's locker wall where two rooms
meet, one on the wall of a JOBY2 corridor, and the discs cut off at polygon edges; combs
inside the discs where two layers of art lie on one plane; burnt-out edges, ANDREA1 room
3's forklift cage and lamp bracket white; JOBY2's hull plates washing to a pale lilac at a
grazing angle; and rooms that wear a glossy page left matt. It also showed Lara's own
sheen going and coming between rooms, which the build before that entry shows the same way
and which is a task of its own. The code said why, finding by finding. A directional
light's highlight on a flat floor sits at a fixed direction of view, so the sun's slot -
JOBY2's sun has a colour, and its share was read off light cubes the lamps light indoors -
drew a disc that moves with the camera exactly, and the eye as a lamp is tied to the
camera by construction. The four lamps nearest a draw call's box out of its own room, the
sun's share and the mean cube were chosen per draw call, so the shine stepped wherever one
draw call met another and differed on two layers that lie on one plane.
HD_GLOSS_LAMP_SCALE 0.1 made a median lamp - a largest channel of 10 in ANDREA1, 15 in
RICH2, 20 in JOBY2 - one whole white or more and ANDREA2's brightest twelve, the highlight
was then multiplied by (n + 8) / 8, 7 at exponent 48, and metal's F0 0.5 at strength 0.8
left 2.8 whites at the peak of a median lamp. The cube was lifted by 3, and JOBY2's cubes
are the brightest of all levels (a mean face of 41 to 52 of 255), so at Fresnel's full
weight a whole draw call of hull plates took up to 0.6 of a white of the cube's lilac. And
every draw call of a room with a part-way clear floor - 55 rooms of RICH2, 1 of RICHCUT2,
9 of TITLE - stayed plain, as did every draw call with a scroll, a flipbook, a book or a
caustic within reach, although only the caustic is a line of the pixel shader.

**How.** The field is `specific/hd/hd_gloss_field.h`, a header of pure functions like
`hd_gloss_math.h`: the cell (`HD_GLOSS_FIELD_CELL`, `:65`), the reach (`:70`), a lamp's
colour to the field's scale (`HD_GLOSS_LAMP_NORM`, `:82`), the falloff (1 - d^2 / R^2)^2
(`:121`), the exposure 1 - e^-m that bounds a cell's colour below one and keeps its hue
(`:136`), the grid over the rooms' boxes that a lamp reaches, one cell more each side,
powers of two where a device asks for them (`HDGlossFieldLayout`, `:207`), the build
(`HDGlossFieldBuild`, `:296`) with an optional sight test by the rooms that only the tools
use (`HDGlossFieldSight`, `:282`), and the sample as the shader reads it (`:452`).
`hd_render.cpp` builds it at the level build out of every room group's point lights in
world units and the rooms' boxes made world (`BuildField`, `:3158`, called at `:3759`)
into two `D3DFMT_A8R8G8B8` volume textures in the managed pool (`MakeFieldTexture`,
`:3125`) - a device without filtered volume textures gets none, and the variant then draws
its environment term alone; the state bracket saves samplers 1 and 2 and their textures
(`:5891`), sets them linear, unmipped and clamped (`:5945`), binds the field in the room
bracket (`:5994`) and puts all of it back (`:6080`). Per room, `prepare` (`:6822`) writes
six registers, `upload_gloss_rows` (`:6154`): `gGlossAxes`, the view rotation's transpose,
and `gGlossField`, the rows that take a view-space position to the field's texture
coordinate - the room's world-view matrix undone, the room group's origin kept from the
build added, the field's corner taken off and its size divided out - so the engine, whose
matrix is the finished D3DMView, and RoomProbe, which draws a room at its own origin, land
on the same world. Per glossy draw call only `gGloss` changes, its `w` the tool's field
picture (`:6606`). The shader: the note "The sheen"
(`specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl:528`), the constants (`:590`), the registers (`:596`)
and samplers (`:603`), `GlossSheen` (`:997`) with the bound (`:1047`), the caustic in both
variants (`:1260`) and the screen (`:1305`); `hd_room_gloss_ps.inc` uses 502 of the 512
slots (`:543`). The bound's twins for the suite are `HDGlossSheenBound` and
`HDGlossSheenCompose` (`hd_gloss_math.h:742`, `:753`). Which draw calls keep the plain
variant is `RangeKeepsPlain` (`hd_render.cpp:2893`); `ResolveSheen` (`:3010`) no longer
looks at the room and counts what it keeps plain (`:3034`, `:3058`), and the GLOSSLOG part

field_weak= field_kb= field_ms=` (`hd_level.cpp:3605`), and `GLOSSLOG skipped level=
ripple= caustic= flat= scroll= flipbook= book= clear=` follows it (`:3611`,
`HDRenderSheenSkipped`, `hd_render.h:1105`). The tools: TrgProbe `-glossfield`
(`TrgProbe.cpp:3005`); RoomProbe `-glossfield [colour|direction]` and `-fieldsight`
(`RoomProbe.cpp:5137`, `:5155`, through `HDRenderGlossFieldView` and
`HDRenderGlossFieldSight`, `hd_render.cpp:7163`, `:7168`), and its state-bracket check
watches samplers 1 and 2 and their textures (`RoomProbe.cpp:929`, `:7055`); ModernTest's
`gloss_field_grid`, `gloss_field_texels`, `gloss_field_build` and `gloss_field_bound`
(`ModernTest.cpp:10764`, `:10806`, `:10856`, `:10964`) take the place of `gloss_cube` and
the lamp ranking.

`hd_gloss_pages.h` but for its three new lines, `hd_gloss.txt` and its format, the seed,
the barred lobby pages, GLOSSLOG's page lines and the existing fields of its level line,

**Decisions.** The shine is a function of the place: what the gloss variant reads for a
pixel is its world position, its normal, its page's gloss and the eye, nothing chosen per
draw call or per room, so it steps nowhere the baked light does not step, and two layers
on one plane take the same shine. No light is tied to the camera: the eye as a lamp and
the directional sun are gone, and a highlight belongs to a lamp of the level at its place.
No burn-out: a lamp's colour is scaled by HD_GLOSS_LAMP_NORM so that the 90th percentile
of the lamps' largest channel over the fifteen levels (20; the median is 10 and the
largest 120) gives one, a cell's colour is bounded below one by the exposure, the lobe's
normalisation is folded into HD_GLOSS_HIGHLIGHT 2, and the whole sheen is held under the
surface's own lit colour plus 4 of 255 - softly, B (1 - e^(-t / B)) - and composed as a
screen, so a dark surface stays dark and a lamp behind a wall cannot light a surface the
bake left dark. The environment is the surface's own baked light at a quarter, continuous
by the art, its Fresnel rise held by the same bound. The highlight's source is the light
field, built once per level, a cell a floor square across and a square up; a second
direction per cell is not built - weak cells are 0 to 4.3 per cent of the lit ones, and a
second lobe and a third texture would not fit the ten slots left. No sight test in the
engine: the pictures show no visible leak without one, a test by the rooms on this grid
takes a floor's own lamps half away where an unconnected room lies under it at a cell
boundary, and it would need the rooms' portal lists in the renderer; the tools carry it
for the measurement. Lara's own sheen is not part of this entry: her draw path is
untouched. Every room that wears the page shines: the exclusion of rooms with a clear
floor is gone, the lobby's pages stay matt by page and the clear floors by class; the
caustic is back in the gloss variant (its slots came free with the lamp loop), the scroll,
the flipbook and the book need nothing of the pixel shader, and the water surfaces' ripple
and the sky band's flat light keep the plain variant and are counted. The dynamic lights
give no highlight in the gloss variant: ten slots are left, and one lobe per light costs
more. No per-frame work on the processor per glossy draw call beyond the variant and the
page's own constants: the rows go up once per room, the textures once per bracket. The
strengths chosen here are raised in the entry 'The sheen at a strength that shows'.

**Left.** Page steps between levels: the seed votes per level, and ten pages take its
metal in one level and nothing in another - 548 and 560 in JOBY3 against JOBY5, 977, 3008,
3009, 3011, 12040 and 12042 among RICH1, RICH2 and RICH3, 12049 in JOBY2 against RICH1 and
RICH3 (TrgProbe `-glossseed`; 94 was the tenth) - so one picture shines in one level and
stays matt in the next until a table line names it. The ripple of a water surface in the
gloss variant (no level has a water page that names a gloss). The dynamic lights'
highlight. A second direction per cell. The sight test in the engine. Lara's own sheen, a
task of its own. The play test at 165 Hz with `-log` and HD on: JOBY2 first - the
diamond-plate rooms around room 90, the table room 104 and the hull outside, room 143: no

### The sheen at a strength that shows
2026-10-01

**What.** The sheen of the previous entry at about two and a half times its strength at a
highlight: the highlight at six times the field's colour (`HD_GLOSS_HIGHLIGHT`, was 2),
the environment at 0.35 of the surface's light (`HD_GLOSS_ENV`, was 0.25), the bound at
two and a half times the surface's own lit colour plus 8 of 255 (`HD_GLOSS_BOUND`,
`HD_GLOSS_FLOOR`, were 1 and 4 of 255), and a cap the bound never passes, three quarters
(`HD_GLOSS_CAP`, new).

**Why.** In the play test of the previous entry's build the sheen was hardly to be seen.
Its measure says the same: on JOBY2 room 90's dark diamond plate the brightest place of
the highlight gained 23 of 255, on a locker wall 24. The bound at the surface's own lit
colour held it there - a floor that is 45 of 255 bright could gain about 45 at most - and
the weight of metal, 0.4 face on, left the highlight under that bound almost everywhere. A
highlight on dark steel is brighter than the steel; a bound of one cannot show it.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`: the five defines over `gGloss`, and
`min(..., HD_GLOSS_CAP)` in the bound of `GlossSheen`; the gloss variant takes 503 of 512
instruction slots (502). `specific/hd/hd_gloss_math.h` carries the twins of the bound, the
floor and the cap in `HDGlossSheenBound`. With a bound above one the screen alone would
let a mid-bright surface reach white where the highlight saturates - lit (1 + B (1 - lit))
is one at lit 0.4 for B 2.5 - so the cap holds the sheen under three quarters, and the
screen, lit + sheen (1 - lit), then closes at most three quarters of the way to white. The
environment is raised least: it lifts a whole surface evenly, which reads as a paler
picture and not as a shine.

**Checked.** The engine builds (`be.bat`, the full build); ModernTest 14,130 (14,128 and
two of the cap), MenuTest 42,364, InterpTest 711, LipsTest 270 and 243, none failed. The
plain room pixel shader and the room vertex shader differ from the previous entry's in the
stamp line alone, so with `hd_reflect` off every room is drawn as before; ANDREA1 room 3
drawn with `-noreflect` equals the picture drawn at `ca2e904` in all 1,587,200 pixels. Ten
views, gloss off against on, the mean over the drawn pixels and the most the gloss adds
anywhere, the previous strengths in brackets: JOBY2 room 90 at the column 47.4 to 52.8, 60
(51.0, 23); JOBY2 room 114's corridor 33.9 to 39.9, 75 (36.9, 28); JOBY2's hull outside,

room 79 16.6 to 18.9, 9 (18.1, 6); ANDREA2 room 16 40.9 to 42.3, 16 (41.9, 10); RICH1 room
60 38.5 to 38.8, 33 (38.7, 14). The share of pixels with a channel at 250 or more is the

**Unchanged.** The light field, the pages that shine and their classes, strengths and

**Left.** A page step shows more at this strength: the vent grille of JOBY2's corridor
