### The projected shadow: Lara's outline on the HD rooms, cast by one fixed light
2026-10-03

**What.** In an HD room the HD Lara throws a projected shadow in place of the classic
blob: her composite of the drawn frame is drawn into a depth map as seen along a key
light, and the HD room groups near her are drawn a second time with a small pixel shader
that looks the map up and darkens the picture where she stands between the light and the
surface. The shadow is soft-edged, lies on floors, steps and slopes as they are and climbs
a wall she stands close to. `tomb5.shadow_mode` (registry `shadow`) gains the value 5,
*Projected*, and a fresh installation starts with it; 1 Original, 2 Circle, 3 Faded circle
and 4 PSX keep their meaning and their pictures. With 5, every blob still drawn - a
creature's or an item's that does not give way to the second map (the next entry), and
Lara's in a frame the projected shadow does not run in - is the faded circle. Three new
log lines behind `-log`: `HDLOG shadow target`, `HDLOG shadow mode` and `HDLOG shadow
second`. The *Shadow mode* row on the *Graphics* page offers *Projected* as its fifth
state while HD is on and steps the four blobs while it is off, showing a stored 5 then
as *Faded circle*, which is what is drawn for it. The shadow
is thrown by one fixed light for the whole game - 30 degrees off straight down, from one
side, at one darkness - so it lies the same way in every room and moves only as she does.
The lights that light her model can turn and deepen it by one number of the table,
`HD_SHADOW_PULL`, which stands at 0; above 0 the shadow lies where her movement through
the light puts it in every frame and stands still the frame she stands still, and only a
change of the lights themselves - another room's list coming in, a lamp that goes out or
fades - is blended in, over about half a second of game time.

**Why.** A shadow that shows her outline. The blob says where she stands and nothing
more; a silhouette laid on the floor and the steps, offset to one side, ties her to the
room she stands in. The light is a fixed one because the lamps of the levels are set to
colour the walls - low, close and one at a time - and each throws the shadow somewhere
else, so a shadow turned by them wanders by itself. Measured over 45 seconds of ANDREA2
with the lamps' full part (pull 1): her list held no lamp or one at a time; the drawn
direction turned by more than 40 degrees from one second to the next in 27 of the 44
steps, by up to 104; it stood within a degree of the 55-degree slant limit in 19 of the
45 seconds; and the largest angle of a second between the drawn direction and the frame's
target passed 20 degrees in 28. The darkness the lamps gave there, 0.28 to 0.43 and 0.32
on average, is what the fixed darkness, 0.45 x 0.75 = 0.34, stands near.

**How.** The arithmetic is one pure header, `specific/hd/hd_shadow.h` (new; no engine
header, like `hd_softbody.h`), with one table of the numbers that shape the look (:108
to :123: map 512 texels, box 2048 units across and 2048 along the light, darkness 0.45,
LOW 0.75, PULL 0, W_REF 0.5, W_FALLBACK 0.15, the fixed slant 30 degrees, slant limit 55
degrees, TAU 0.5 s, FULL 1024 and END 2048 units below her lowest node, EDGE 0.1, FACING
0.2, BIAS 8 units) and the machinery under it (:141). The key light, `HDShadowKeyTarget`
(:329), takes the pull as a last parameter that defaults to the table's `HD_SHADOW_PULL`
(:113) and is held to 0..1 (:332); `HDShadowFollowLights` takes it the same way, so
`shadow_step`'s calls stand as they were. Every sun, point and spot of her two engine
light lists (`HDObjectShadowLights`, `hd_object.cpp:3867` - the dynamic lights are not in
them, so a gun flash does not swing it) gives a weight, its luminance times the model
shader's own falloff (`HDShadowFalloff`, :263), and the direction it travels at her torso
node; the key light uses the weight times the pull. The weighted sum plus W_FALLBACK times
the fixed slant is made unit and held to the slant limit with its bearing kept
(`HDShadowLimit`, :291), and a sum of nothing leaves the fixed slant exactly as
`HDShadowFallback` (:186) gives it (:398); the darkness is DARK times LOW..1 by how far
the pulled lights agree and how far their pulled weight reaches W_REF. At pull 0 every
product is 0, so the target is the fixed slant at DARK x LOW, the same bits for any lights
at any place, while the key's `lights` and `weight` - the log's `lights=` and `weight=` -
still count her list before the pull. The following, `HDShadowFollow` (:453), tells her
movement from a change of the lights: `HDShadowFollowLights` (:492) weighs the frame's
lights at the last step's torso position with the same pull, and `HDShadowFollowStep`
(:540) takes that minus the last step's target, which is what the lights alone changed,
measured at one place, into an offset and lets the offset decay by exp(-dt / TAU)
(`HDShadowDecay`, :480, :580) on a clock of its own on the soft motion's `HDSoftClock`
(`hd_laradraw.cpp:136`). The drawn direction is the frame's target plus the offset, made
unit and held to the slant limit (:602), the drawn darkness the target's plus its offset
held to 0..DARK (:623). With the lights unchanged - at pull 0 in every frame - the offset
is nothing and the target is drawn as it is, so her own movement shows at once; with a
pull above 0 a change of the lights starts from what was drawn and reaches the new target
along exp(-t / TAU), the same at 30, 60 and 165 frames a second. The pause and the
inventory stand the clock still: a change of the lights in such a frame goes into the
offset whole and decays once the clock runs. A level start, a load, a jump further than
she can move, a gap of a quarter of a second and the first frame after the shadow was
off snap and clear the offset (:543). A step given only a target, with no measurement
before it, counts the whole change of the target as the lights'. The box
(`HDShadowBasis` :665, `HDShadowBoxMake` :700): right is fwd x (1, 0, 0), which cannot
flip inside the slant limit; the centre between her lowest and highest node, snapped to
whole texels so a still light does not let the outline crawl; one mapping,
`HDShadowMapUVD` (:752), as a matrix on view space
(`HDShadowViewToMap`, :776) and as the cast's clip matrix with Direct3D 9's half-texel
rule (`HDShadowCastMatrix`, :820). The gate, `HDShadowGate` (:860): the option, the level
drawn HD, Lara drawn as the HD composite, her room drawn HD or counting as HD for her
shadow (`HDRoomShadowHD`: drawn as another group's art keeping no classic face she can
stand on, or with no classic face at all and no bare floor), and last the map. The receive
side: `HDShadowEdgeTerm` (:960), `HDShadowHeightTerm` (:972), `HDShadowFacingTerm`
(:980), `HDShadowLookup` (:1004) - the 4 x 4 texels round the position weighted 1 - f, 1,
1, f along each axis, so the result is continuous in the position -,
`HDShadowReceiveConstants` (:1056), the receive shader's seven registers out of the same
mapping, and `HDShadowReach` (:1106), the world box a room group must touch to be drawn
again. The mode: `HDShadowBlobMode` (:916) draws a stored 5 as the faded circle,
`HDShadowEffectiveMode` (:924) is 5 exactly when the gate is open. The shaders:
`hd_shader/hd_shadow.hlsl` (new) includes `hd_model.hlsl` and calls `ModelVS`, replacing
only the projection, and writes the depth into an R32F map, alpha-tested by the part's
page;
`hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl` (new) reads `RoomVS`'s outputs by semantic (TEXCOORD0,
2 and 5), runs the range's alpha test, the three terms and the lookup in a dynamic branch
with explicit-level taps, and writes 1 - strength x lookup x terms; about 55, 5 and 125
instruction slots, built and stamped by `bshader.bat`, checked by `be.bat`.
`hd_render.cpp`: the target, `HDRenderShadowTargetReady` (:6222), asks the adapter for
R32F as a render target texture and D24X8 or D16 and their match before it makes the 512
texture and its own depth surface in `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT`, and a refusal stands for the
device's life; it is released by `HDRenderShutdown` (:3525), which every path that drops
the default pool takes - a lost device before `Reset` (`dxshell.cpp:309`) and `DXClose`
(`dxshell.cpp:359`, also on Alt+Enter and a resolution change) through `HDLevelDeviceLost`
(`hd_level.cpp:4081`) - and made again on the next frame that asks.
`HDRenderShadowCastBegin` (:6333) and `End` (:6397) read back and put back the render
target, the depth surface, the viewport, the scissor, thirteen render states, the shaders,
the declaration, stream 0, the indices, texture 0 and the constants the pass writes. The
receive: `HDRenderShadowReceiveBegin` (:7526) sets `RoomVS` with the room path's buffers,
the receive shader and its registers c96 to c102 (above every register a room, gloss, glow
or model pixel shader names), the map on sampler stage 3 (point, clamp; no room or model
draw samples it), the depth test EQUAL with no depth write, the blend source ZERO,
destination SRCCOLOR, colour write RGB only, and - where the depth surface has a stencil,
which the engine's D24S8 has and never uses otherwise - clears the stencil and lets each
pixel be darkened once; `HDRenderRoomShadow` (:7610) draws a group's opaque and alpha
passes and its clear floors again through `draw_receive` (:7379), with every vertex
constant `draw_pass` writes per range, its cull, its page (`receive_page`, :7345, the
flipbook and book choice) and its alpha reference, so `RoomVS` puts every triangle on the
very depth it wrote; `HDRenderShadowReceiveEnd` (:7632) puts back every state Begin read
and unbinds the map. `hd_model.cpp`: the cast draw of a model, `HDModelCastBegin` (:4328)
and `HDModelCastDraw` (:4348), the joints with the bind fold, the soft motion and the
speaking face, passes 0 and 1. `hd_object.cpp`: a mark on a frame-list entry - cast as
well, or into the map only - set by `HDObjectPush`'s two defaulted parameters, and
`HDObjectCastFrame` (:3925). `hd_laradraw.cpp`: `HDShadowFrameDecide` (:1060), the one
decision of a frame, also asks for the receive shader (:1071); `shadow_step` (:963) takes
the key light and the box from her main draw's own matrices and the frame's world-to-view
(`aW2VMx`), weighing the lights at the last step's torso position before the step (:989);
her main draw marks every part it pushes (:1641), and in first person the face and the
braid go into the map only, so the shadow keeps its head; `shadow_log` (:1029) writes the
two state lines. `hd_level.cpp`: `ShadowCastPass` (:4542), then `ShadowReceivePass`
(:4608) - every room group of the frame whose box, moved by its room's origin, touches the
reach, again in the windows and scissors `DrawRoomWindowed` used
(`DrawRoomShadowWindowed`, :4582), only in a frame whose map was drawn just now - and
`ShadowSecond` (:4694), which ends its line in `lag=`, the largest angle of the second
between the drawn direction and the frame's target (:4732, cleared at :4712 and :4743),
0 at pull 0; all three in `HDFrameDraw` (:4902) after the room loop, the clear floors and
`HDRenderScissorOff`, before the models' solid passes. The blob:
`specific/drawlara.cpp` (:133, :388, :652) calls `S_PrintShadow` only in a mirror's draw -
where the HD level's mirror has zeroed her slot's shadow size, so it draws nothing - or
when `HDShadowFrameDecide` says no; `specific/specificfx.cpp` (:6652, :6667,
:6876, :6878) reads the option through `HDShadowBlobMode`. `tomb5/tomb5.cpp` (:102, :343)
and `global/types.h` (:2657) for the default and the comment. The row:
`game/menu_frame.cpp` includes `hd_level.h` and `hd_shadow.h` (:32, :33);
`MenuShadowModeShown` (:700) is the stored value while `HDEnabled()` answers true - the
*HD textures* option and an installed Remaster, no level asked, so the title screen
answers as a level does - and `HDShadowBlobMode` of it otherwise; `MenuValShadowMode`
(:705) shows 1 Original, 2 Circle, 3 Faded circle, 5 Projected and any other value PSX,
and writes nothing; `MenuStepShadowMode` (:714) steps from the shown value with 5 as the
top while HD is on and 4 while it is off, past the top to 1 and below 1 to the top, with
the select sound and the same storage as the rows beside it; the table line (:1574) is
unchanged. `game/gameflow.cpp` (:1445): *Projected* in `CustomText`'s table, German
*Projiziert*, the English repeated in the French, Italian and Spanish columns. A change
reaches the running level on its next drawn frame: `HDShadowFrameDecide` reads the option
every frame, a frame without the projected shadow resets the following
(`hd_laradraw.cpp:1080`), and the first step after that reset snaps (`hd_shadow.h:543`).

**Checked.** The engine builds (`be.bat`). ModernTest 14,443 (14,280 and 163 in fourteen
groups: `shadow_key`, `shadow_pull`, `shadow_fixed`, `shadow_follow`,
`shadow_follow_move`, `shadow_follow_lights`, `shadow_follow_both`, `shadow_follow_edges`,
`shadow_box`, `shadow_gate`, `shadow_terms`, `shadow_lookup`, `shadow_receive`,
`shadow_mode`), MenuTest 42,613, InterpTest 729, LipsTest 270 and 243, none failed;
ModelProbe, RoomProbe and MapProbe, the tools that link the changed files, build. The
fixed light (`shadow_fixed`, 10 checks): at the table's pull the key light gives the
fixed slant and DARK x LOW bit for bit, and an agreement of exactly 0, for 35 light
sets - none, a list pointer of nothing,
a lamp above her, at her feet, below her and at the reference point itself, a spot beside
her, a sun from each of 26 sides, thirty lights at once and lights that are not numbers -
at five reference points from the origin to 1e30 and NaN, the same as an explicit pull of
0, with `lights` and `weight` those of pull 1; the same sets at pull 1 turn the direction
by over 5 degrees in at least 100 of the 175 cases, so the check is not empty; a walk of
five seconds through lights that change every four steps, driven as `shadow_step` drives
it, draws the fixed slant and DARK x LOW bit for bit in every step at 30, 60 and 165 steps
a second, with no offset, one snap and a lag of exactly 0, while the same walk at pull 1
turns the drawn direction away from the target. The lights' part (`shadow_pull`, 8
checks): every check of `shadow_key` and of the following calls the key light with the
pull given as 1 and holds as it stood; for a sun and for a lamp, 21 pulls from 0 to 1 turn
the direction along the arc from the fixed slant towards the lights' own within 1e-3
degrees, monotone, and give a strength between DARK x LOW and the lights', rising; half
the pull is neither end; a white sun at pull p has the strength of a sun p as bright
within 1e-5; a pull above 1 counts as 1 and one below 0, minus 1e30 or NaN as 0, bit for
bit. Against the key light of before, with LOW and the slant set to the same numbers,
200,000 random light sets at pull 1 give the same bits in 161,144 and, where the sum is
nothing (38,856), the fixed slant exactly where the old rule gave the unit vector of
W_FALLBACK times it, with the same strength, weight and count. Thirteen mutations of the
header, each in a `git archive` copy, fail checks: the pull left out (11), the pull on
the direction only with the strength from the unpulled lights (9), the pull on the
strength only (9), the strength's weights unpulled (1), no exact fixed slant for a sum of
nothing (4), the weight counted after the pull (1), the pull not held to 0..1 (1), the
measurement before the step without the pull (82), the table's pull 1 (6) and 0.5 (6),
the default of the key light's pull 1 (5), the slant 25 (2), LOW 0.6 (1). Eighteen
mutations of the header outside the following, each in a `git archive` copy, fail at
least one check each: a sun reversed, the falloff stretched, no slant limit, no
half-texel shift, no texel snap, a basis that flips, two gates swapped, a hard box edge,
the height term reversed, faces turned away taking it, flat tap weights, no bias, the
clear value casting, the height plane without her lowest node, the light's row reversed,
the reach cut at her feet, a 5 handed to the blob and projected without the gate.
Fourteen mutations of the following each fail at least one check: the measurement not
used, so every change of the target trails again, the jump measured at the new reference
point, offset times decay minus jump in place of (offset - jump) times decay, no decay, a
linear decay, the jump's sign reversed, the offset not drawn, a snap that keeps the
offset, a standing clock that drops the jump, no jump test, no slant limit on the drawn
direction, the strength not held to 0..DARK, an offset that is not a number kept, no lag;
a measurement before the first step, which that step's snap discards, is the one change
that fails none, and changes nothing. The groups pin one sun to within 1e-3 degrees of its
own direction beside the slant's weight. With fixed lights (one lamp; two lamps and a sun)
and her walking past the lamp at 30, 60 and 165 steps a second, the drawn direction is
each step's target within 0.001 degrees and the strength within 1e-6, the lag stays under
0.001 degrees, and every step after she stops draws the same bits as the one before. With
a lamp removed, a sun added or a lamp's colour halved (turns of 31, 8 and 14 degrees)
every later step follows the closed form within 0.005 degrees and 1e-5 of strength, the
change's own step is the curve's first step, and the three rates draw the same at 1.2,
1.6, 2 and 3 seconds; walking while a lamp is removed, the offset is -jump exp(-t / TAU)
within 1e-5 whichever way she walks on. Further: the half-texel rule by rasterising the
cast matrix, the lookup falling from 1 to 0 across an edge by under 0.01 per hundredth of
a texel and the receive registers on the one mapping within 0.01 texel 60,000 units out.
On this machine the device gives R32F 512 x 512 with D24X8; the device's reference count
reads 72, 74 and 72 before, with and after the map; the map is the same bit for bit across
a device `Reset`. The two passes cost 0.087 ms a frame on JOBY2 room 8 and 0.090 ms on
ANDREA1 room 0 against a 2560 x 1440 target, the cast pass alone 0.061 ms (ModelProbe
`-shadowtime` and `-shadowdevice`, 300 frames each waited for with an event query). The
pictures (ModelProbe `-shadowroom` with `-shadowreceive`, looked at one by one): with the
light at 22 degrees a short outline at her feet; at 45 degrees her whole outline beside
her on the floor; at the slant limit a longer one; on ANDREA1 room 159's steps the shadow
lies on the treads, broken at the edge of each step; against the pillar of JOBY2 room 8 it
runs along the floor and up the wall; through ANDREA1 room 0's railing the floor behind
the bars takes it and the bars do not; every one meets her feet without a gap, has a soft
edge without steps, stripes or speckles, darkens nothing outside the outline, and the
box's border is nowhere to be seen. With nothing cast the picture with both passes is the
picture without them byte for byte, so the passes leave the device as they find it and the
models drawn after them see the states they always saw; with the stencil guard switched
off the three scenes come out byte-identical as well, so none of them has two faces in one
plane. The row: MenuTest 42,613 (42,439 and 174 in `graphics_shadow_row`), none failed. It
reads the row's lines and the new string in the tree and includes `hd_shadow.h`; swept are
the five states with HD and both wraps and their texts, the four without, a stored 5 shown
as *Faded circle* and stepped to PSX and Circle and kept with no direction, every other
stored value against the four-state rule, and `HDShadowFollowStep` snapping on the first
step after the reset a frame without the shadow makes. Against the tree before the row it
fails 4 checks; eleven single changes each fail one: five states without HD, a stored 5
not mapped, showing that writes, 5 shown as PSX, either wrap wrong, HD read from the
level, no sound, the save class dropped, the German untranslated, the following not reset.

**Unchanged.** `hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_model.hlsl`, `hd_glow.hlsl` and their six `.inc` are
byte for byte the files of before. With `tomb5.hd_enable` 0 the HD path is not reached
(`HDLevelActive`, `hd_level.cpp:4139`) and the stored 5 draws the faded circle, the
picture a fresh installation had. With the option on 1, 2, 3 or 4 the gate answers
`option` before anything touches the device, neither pass runs, every push is unmarked and
the blob is the one it was. RoomProbe's pictures of ANDREA1 rooms 0 and 159 and JOBY2
rooms 8 and 92, and ModelProbe's of two outfits from two angles and of first person, are
the same md5 built at the round's start and at its end. The classic blobs' drawing code,
the mirror pass, every other HD draw - items, creatures, cutscene actors, the inventory -
and the savegame are untouched.

**Decisions.** On by default. The four classic blobs stay selectable in HD too. The new
state of the *Shadow mode* row is reachable only while HD is on. The shadow's light is a
fixed one - one slant for the whole game, 30 degrees, and one darkness, 0.34 - so the
shadow moves only as she does; the lamps' part stays in the arithmetic behind one number
of the table, `HD_SHADOW_PULL`, set to 0, which multiplies every light's weight in the
direction and in the darkness alike, so that the lights' rule stays built and checked and
a pull between 0 and 1 mixes the two. The key light takes the pull as a defaulted last
parameter, so the engine's calls and the lines MenuTest reads stay as they were. With a
pull above 0, a change of the lights is blended over time and never stepped, the darkness
as well as the direction, while her own movement through the light is drawn at once, so
the shadow comes to rest the frame she does; the change between the blob and the
projected shadow itself is made from one frame to the next. The lights are told from her
movement by weighing the frame's lights where she stood in the last step, in a call of its
own before the step, so the step keeps its arguments; a step without that measurement
counts every change as the lights' and blends it, the soft side. In this first round the
HD rooms and the statics that are part of their art receive, and only Lara casts. The
receive draws the room groups again with their own vertex shader and a pixel shader of its
own, instead of a lookup inside the room shader, which has no instruction slots left. The
key light reads her two engine light lists in world space rather than the model shader's
view-space list, which cannot tell the dynamic lights apart. The row asks `HDEnabled()`
for HD, the setting and the installation, not whether the level on screen is drawn HD, so
it answers in the title screen too and does not change with the room she stands in. With
HD off a stored 5 is shown as what is drawn for it and stepped from there, but not written
back, so switching HD on again brings *Projected* back.

**Left.** Lara's shadow on herself, and - until the third entry gives it - on HD items and
creatures; casters other than Lara and the creatures and items the classic engine gives a
blob, which cast into a second map once drawn HD (the next entry) - the cutscene actors
among them cast nothing; the shadow in a mirror's image, which the third entry gives (her
reflection has no blob: the HD level's mirror zeroes her slot's shadow size around it);
the parts of her drawn classic (the diving suit's two propulsion units are not in the
map); classic rooms that keep a face she can stand on (her blob is drawn there); the
classic statics (`HDStaticDrawnClassic`) do not receive; the tuning of the numbers. The
fixed light falls the same way in every room, so near a lamp the shadow can lie towards
the lamp rather than away from it. A shadow that reaches past a wall falls on the floor
beyond it as well, because receivers never cast; the height term stops a storey below,
nothing stops a room beside. A face turned away from the light is not darkened even where
the room's baked light lights it. If the frame list is full and her body cannot be pushed,
the frame has neither shadow nor blob (the blob gave way, the map stays empty). The change
from the blob to the projected shadow is a cross-fade of a quarter second since the fourth
part below; back to the blob - at the border between an HD room and a classic one, on a
step of the row and when the map is lost - one gives way to the other within a single
frame. The shadow multiplies the finished colour of the room: the distance fog takes light
towards black, so the shadow fades with the floor, and since the fourth part the fog
bulbs' haze in front of a floor is given back. With a pull above 0, whatever changes her
two light lists while she walks, a light that enters or leaves them or a brightness the
engine fades, counts as a change of the lights and is blended, so `lag=` above 0 while she
only moves says that her lists changed under her; at pull 0 `lag=` stays 0. What cannot be
proven without playing: how the fixed shadow looks in motion and in the levels' rooms, its
slant and darkness against taste, a pull between 0 and 1, cutscenes, first person, and
whether the frame's world-to-view (`aW2VMx`) is the camera her main draw's matrices stand
on at sixty frames a second as well.

### The projected shadow: the creatures cast as well, into a second map
2026-10-04

**What.** In a frame the projected shadow runs in, every creature and item the classic
engine gives a blob (its object's `shadow_size` is not 0) and that is drawn as an HD model
gives up its blob and throws a projected shadow along the same fixed light: it is drawn
into a second map beside Lara's, and the HD room groups take both maps in the one receive
pass. The second map reaches four sectors to every side of her and along the light; a
creature whose feet stand up to 819 units beyond its sides still casts what of it reaches
in, so its shadow fades out at the map's edge on every side. Its texels are of her map's
size, so a creature's outline is as soft as hers and its shadow as
dark; where two shadows overlap the floor is as dark as under one. A receiver up to 1536
units behind a creature along the light takes its whole shadow, from 2560 on none. Lara's
own shadow is the one of before, to the bit, and so is every frame without a creature in
the second box. `HDLOG shadow second` gains `others=`, `omap=`, `orooms=` and `oms=` at
its end, and a new line, `HDLOG shadow others`, reports the second map's target.

**Why.** With Lara's projected shadow in the room, the creatures beside her stood on round
blobs: two kinds of shadow under one light. Now they carry the shadow she carries.

**How.** The table (`specific/hd/hd_shadow.h:173` to `:178`) gains OTHERS_MAP 2048
texels, OTHERS_BOX 8192 units across, OTHERS_MARGIN 0.1 of it, OTHERS_DEPTH 8192 along the
light, OTHERS_FULL 1536 and OTHERS_END 2560, each with what it does to the picture. The
box carries its own extent, depth and map size (`HDShadowBox`, :719):
`hd_shadow_box_snap` (:769) snaps a centre to whole texels of the box's own map,
`HDShadowBoxMake` (:791) gives her box the table's BOX, DEPTH and MAP, `HDShadowBoxAround`
(:828) makes the second box round hers - the same light, basis and middle, snapped the
same way, so with texels of her size its centre is hers to the bit - and the mapping, the
matrices, the receive block and the reach read the box's own size; `HDShadowBoxHolds`
(:864) says whether a point lies inside the box grown by a margin, a part of its extent
on each of its four sides across the light and the same part of its depth on the two
along it (the depth grown with the fade of the next entry). The rule with its two
faces (:1473, :1479): an item's blob gives way when the projected shadow runs, her step
ran, the second target exists, the item is drawn HD and it is not mirrored; the item casts
when it also has a blob and its place lies inside the second box grown by OTHERS_MARGIN.
The frame (`HDShadowFrame`, :1504) gains `stepped`, the second box and its two matrices,
filled by `shadow_step` (`hd_laradraw.cpp:1008` to `:1012`), `stepped` cleared every frame
(:1483). The blob's one call, `game/draw.cpp:781`, asks `HDObjectBlobGivesWay`

**Decisions.** A second map beside hers rather than one larger map for both: her texel and
her picture stay as they were, and the second map has a texel of the same size, so the
two shadows match. Overlapping shadows take the darker of the two, not their product, so
a crowd does not blacken the floor. The two-map shader writes the smaller of the two
factors, the form in which her factor is `ReceivePS`'s own expression, so a pixel the
second map does not reach is that shader's pixel to the bit. The variant is a second entry
point of the same file, its own `.inc` beside the first. In place of her height plane,
which measures from her lowest node, each tap measures from its own caster, because the
second map holds many casters at many heights. A creature's place is its world position,
the point its blob is laid under; the box that place is asked against is grown across the
light by a fixed part of its width rather than by each caster's own height, one number
that covers every caster up to 2160 units tall, because the map's border clips the rest
and a caster with nothing inside costs one model in the cast pass and changes no pixel.
The blob gives way only on a device that has the
variant, the cast shaders and the second target, so it never gives way to a shadow that
cannot be drawn. The receive draws the groups within either reach; the second reach is the
second box's prism with OTHERS_END beyond its far side and no height bound. Should only
the second map be drawn in a frame, her block is silenced rather than her map read. The
log line gains `oms=`, the second cast pass's time, beside the three fields asked for; its
receive is in `ms=`.

**Left.** A creature further from her than 4096 and 819 units across the light, or 4096
and 819 units along it from her middle, has no shadow at all, neither blob nor projected
one; across the light the edge term fades the projected one out on every side before.
Along the light the second box ends 4096 units from her centre, about 4730 straight above
or below her at the fixed slant; the next entry fades each tap of the second map by its
own caster's depth near both ends and grows the mark's box along the light to match, so a
creature crossing there no longer loses a shadow of full strength in one frame. An HD item
clipped away (its bounds outside the view or the portal window) has had its blob skipped
before the clip is known; its shadow reaches 440 to 900 units beyond its bounds along the
light, and the next entry walks such an item's nodes for the second map alone, so its

entering the view and for a creature walking four sectors away from her. A creature that

### The projected shadow on the HD models, in a mirror and from a creature out of view
2026-10-04

**What.** The HD models take the projected shadow as the rooms do: her outline falls on a
creature or an HD item that stands down-light of her, a creature's on her and on the HD
items, each at the darkness it has on the floor, and two shadows over one model are as
dark as one. A mirror's image shows the shadows of the room in front of it, reflected: the
copy behind the glass takes them at the place it reflects, and so do the reflections of
Lara and the items. A creature the picture has clipped away - its bounds outside the view
or its door's window - still casts into the second map, so its shadow lies on the floor
before the creature comes into view. The second map's shadow fades out over the box's near
and far side along the light as it does across it, so no creature loses its shadow in one
frame. `HDLOG shadow second` gains `models=`, `mcalls=`, `castonly=` and `mirror=` at its
end. The table gains one number, OTHERS_FADE.

**Why.** With the rooms darkened and the models not, a creature in her shadow stood lit on
a dark floor, and her outline stopped at its feet; the mirror's copy looked the maps up
at its own place behind the glass, where none of the shadows in front of it lie, instead
of at the place it reflects, and the reflections took none; and a creature
walking into view brought a strip of shadow with it at the screen's edge. The rest of the
projected shadow, as decided for this round, closes those three; a second light for walls
turned away from the fixed one is not built.

**How.** The number: `HD_SHADOW_OTHERS_FADE` 0.05 (`specific/hd/hd_shadow.h:192`), with
what it does to the picture and which way to turn it in the table's comment. The fade:
`HDShadowFadeTerm` (:1149) weights each casting tap of the second map by saturate(min(tap,
1 - tap) / OTHERS_FADE), exactly 1 in the box's middle, in `HDShadowLookupBehind` and in
the shaders' `OthersShade` (`hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl:254`, the slope in c107.z);
`HDShadowBoxHolds` (:882) grows all six sides of the box by its margin, so a caster's mark
holds along the light as across it and the fade has eaten its shadow before the mark
drops. The second target is asked for in the frame's decision beside hers
(`hd_laradraw.cpp:1109`, read through `HDShadowFrameOthersReady`, :1127), so its state
line is written in the frame it changes and no blob asks for a target;
`HDFrameShadowOthersDrawn` is gone, the receive pass reads `g_others_cast_now`. The
models: who takes which map is a pure rule of what an entry is (`HDShadowReceiverTakes`,
:1611) - Lara's pieces the second map only, never her own; an item whose object has a blob
her map only, never the one it is cast into; every other HD item both; the ring and the
pickup display nothing - and a block not taken is silenced through its u row
(`HDShadowReceiveWithoutHer`, `HDShadowReceiveWithoutOthers`, :1402), so one shader serves
all and reads no map it is not to read. `ModelReceivePS` (`hd_shadow_receive.hlsl:428`) is
the two-map body on ModelVS's outputs with ModelPS's three clips; `HDModelReceiveDraw`
(`hd_model.cpp:4483`) draws an entry again with ModelVS, the same joints, neck cut, soft
constants, lips stream, indices and cull as the solid draw, the opaque and alpha ranges
only; `HDRenderShadowModelsBegin` (`hd_render.cpp:7989`) sets EQUAL, no depth write, ZERO
/ SRCCOLOR, RGB and guards each pixel with stencil bit 1, which the rooms' receive leaves
0; `HDObjectShadowReceiveFrame` (`hd_object.cpp:4277`) walks the frame list, tests each
entry's bounding sphere (`entry_sphere`, :4170) against the reach of the maps it takes
(`HDShadowSphereTouches`, :1633), and `ShadowModelsPass` (`hd_level.cpp:4826`) runs it
after the models' solid pass, only in a frame whose rooms' receive ran. The mirror: for a
mirror in the plane of constant `axis` at `plane`, `HDShadowMirrorView` (:1678) makes the
reflected world-to-view R' = R S, t' = t - R S c (S negates the axis, c is 2 plane on it);
a pixel of the image at view position v stands for the world point R'^T (v - t'), the
place it reflects, so every receive block made with R', t' is the block of the image - for
the copy's art, drawn through the real view at the image point, and for a reflection,
whose node matrices the mirror's view puts at that same view position.
`HDShadowMirrorPlane` (:1695) is the glass in view space, `HDShadowMirrorFaces` (:1713)
whether the camera sees it from its room's side. The rooms: `ShadowReceivePass`
(`hd_level.cpp:4716`) draws a mirror's group first with the mirror's blocks
(`ShadowMirrorBlocks`, :4671; the loop at :4775) through a new variant, `MirrorReceivePS`
(`hd_shadow_receive.hlsl:356`), which clips everything in front of the glass (c108,
`HD_SHADOW_RECEIVE_MIRROR`, :1726) and marks the copy's pixels in the guard's stencil bit,
then the group as every group, which the guard keeps off the copy;
`HDRenderShadowReceiveMirrorBegin` and `End` (`hd_render.cpp:7855`, :7875) switch the
shader and the blocks inside the open receive and put the receive's own back (kept at
:7749). The reflections: `DrawOneMirror` hands the seam its index (`game/mirror.cpp:256`)
and, before it zeroes an item's `shadow_size` for the draw, whether the object has a blob
(`HDObjectReflectedBlob`, :332); `HDObjectBegin` reads the class from that
(`hd_object.cpp:2958`), every entry recorded while the reflection is on carries its mirror
(:3103, :4481), and `HDObjectShadowReceiveFrame` gives it its mirror's blocks
(`receive_blocks_mirror`, :4254), taking its sphere back to the world through the same
reflected view. Out of view: `HDShadowItemWalk` (`hd_shadow.h:1563`) is the rule of an
item's node walk - a drawn item walks as always; a clipped one walks for the second map
alone when it is HD, its blob gave way and its place lies inside the grown second box;
every other clipped item walks nothing. `DrawAnimatingItem` asks it through
`HDObjectCastUnseen` (`game/draw.cpp:883`, `hd_object.cpp:3289`) and walks the nodes under
`clip || unseen` (:885), without `CalculateObjectLighting` and without `InterpRootNow`
(:908); `HDObjectEnd` leaves the light out for it (:3197) and marks it
`HD_OBJ_CAST_OTHERS_ONLY` (:3244), which the second map's cast pass draws and no picture
pass does (:3852). The log: `ShadowSecond` (`hd_level.cpp:4894`) ends its line in
`models=`, `mcalls=`, `castonly=` and `mirror=` (:4935), counted by `ShadowModelsPass` and
`ShadowOthersPass` (:4635), and is called after the models' pass (:5143) so its line holds
the whole frame. Builds: `bshader.bat` compiles the two new entry points into
`hd_shadow_receive_model_ps.inc` and `hd_shadow_receive_mirror_ps.inc`, and `be.bat`
checks their stamps.

**Checked.** The engine builds (`be.bat`), and with it ModelProbe, RoomProbe, MapProbe,
TrgProbe, MenuTest, InterpTest and LipsTest. ModernTest 14,505 (14,481 and 24 in six
groups: `shadow_others_fade`, `shadow_others_holds`, `shadow_takes`, and
`shadow_mirror_view` - a point of the copy through the mirror's blocks gives its
reflection's u, v, depth, height term and facing through the frame's, both axes and both

`.inc`, against the first part of round two for the cast shaders, and the one-map receive

on her leg and boots at the floor's factor (0.55); a medipack without a blob in her
shadow; a medipack under her shadow and a SWAT's no darker than under one (433 pixels,

one picture and none in the next, no cut line; a SWAT walked unseen (`-shadowunseen`) -
its shadow on the floor where the drawn SWAT's lies, at the same factor (0.551), no body,
and the second map bit for bit the drawn run's. The mirror (RICH2 room 134, the glass in x
= 33792, a camera above her looking down through the pane over the basin): the copy's
factor against the factor of the room in front of the glass seen from the camera reflected
in the glass (`-shadowmirrorview`), pixel for pixel over the copy's 431,734 pixels
(`-shadowmirrormask`): her shadow on the copy's floor 55,504 pixels at median 0.760 (the

while the copy without the mirror's blocks takes none of it (mean difference 0.027, 53,129
pixels off by more than 0.05); with a SWAT beside her the same (57,501 against 57,129,
mean 0.002); with a light towards the glass her shadow lies under the basin and the copy's
matches the reflected room's (mean 0.001). On this machine both targets are made,
released, the device `Reset` and made again with the same maps bit for bit, the reference
count 76 / 78 / 76 (one above the first part with the mirror's variant made), the second
target made in 0.08 to 0.39 ms; the device's 2,197 values of state are the same after the
models' pass as before it, also in the mirror's frame with two reflections. Against a 2560
x 1440 target, 400 frames each waited for: the models' pass with Lara, four creatures and
three items 0.086 ms; RICH2 room 134 with the mirror, her and a SWAT: her cast, the second
map's cast and the receive 0.215 ms with the mirror's draw against 0.095 ms without it -

**Unchanged.** The light, its following, the gate's rule for her, the option, the row and
every number the table had; her box, her map, her terms; how the rooms take the two maps
in a frame without a mirror, but for the fade along the light, which is exactly 1 in the
box's middle, so a creature there gives the earlier picture byte for byte. The one-map
receive shader's bytecode; `hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_model.hlsl`, `hd_glow.hlsl` and the cast
shaders. With `tomb5.hd_enable` 0, the stored modes 1 to 4, a classic Lara or a frame
without her step, nothing of this runs: the gate stops the cast passes, the models' pass
runs only after a rooms' receive that ran, the second target is asked only in a frame hers
runs in, and an item clipped away walks nothing because its blob never gave way. The walk
of a drawn item, the poses, the interpolation's counters and seams, the classic blobs'
drawing code and the savegame. A frame without a mirror's group in the receive pass binds
nothing new.

**Decisions.** Which maps a model takes is what it is, not whether it cast in the frame,
so a creature does not change its look as it walks into the second box; Lara never takes
her own map and a caster never the map it is cast into, because the fixed light is not the
light that lights them and a model's own outline would darken half of it. The models guard
with a stencil bit of their own, because the rooms' receive leaves its bit set on the room
pixels behind them. The mirror's image takes the same two maps through a reflected view
rather than maps of its own: nothing is cast twice, and the copy's art and the reflections
share one arithmetic. The copy is told from the room by the glass's plane in the pixel
shader and kept apart by the stencil guard; on a depth surface without a stencil the copy
takes the ordinary receive, and so it does while the mirror is seen from behind. A
reflection takes the class of what it reflects from the value the mirror's loop hands
over, not from `shadow_size`, which that loop zeroes so that a reflection has no blob and
casts nothing. The fade along the light is a fade of each tap's own caster depth, so a
caster in the box's middle casts as before. An item walked unseen takes the frame's own
root offset and no light: those belong to a drawn item and their counters to the picture.
The log's line is written after the models' pass, so `models=` and `mcalls=` count the
frame they belong to; the new fields are means over the frames the shadow ran, `mirror=` a
count over them.

**Left.** Her shadow on herself, a creature's on itself or on another creature, and a
second light for walls turned away from the fixed one are not built. An item in a room
that is not on the frame's list is never visited and casts nothing, whether the second box
holds it or not; an item walked unseen takes a slot of the frame list, which holds 128.
The probe draws neither `game/draw.cpp`'s item loop nor `game/mirror.cpp`: the unseen walk
is proven by its pure rule (`HDShadowItemWalk`, ModernTest), by the walk read at
`game/draw.cpp:883` to `:1048` and by a probe creature cast and drawn in no pass; the
reflections' class and mirror by the code walk (`game/mirror.cpp:256`, :332;
`hd_object.cpp:2958`, :3103, :4254) and by probe reflections made by hand through the
world's reflection in the glass, whose arithmetic `shadow_mirror_engine` holds against the
engine's own `MirrorView`. Only the game shows the item loop, a real clipped creature
entering the view, Lara's and the items' reflections in RICH2 rooms 134 and 135 in motion,
and both mirrors in one frame (each has its own blocks; the probe draws one room). The
wall faces lying in the glass's plane take the mirror's blocks or the frame's pixel by
pixel; there both give the same place. A creature's reflection drawn classic (a slot
without an HD model) takes nothing. The play test should look first at the RICH2 washrooms
with Lara before a mirror, at a creature behind her in her shadow, and at creatures
walking into view from the side their shadow points to.

(#188): the suites', 'Round 188 (#188): the mirror's image takes the shadows, and a

### The projected shadow: its arrival, a block's depth and the fog bulbs' haze
2026-10-11

**What.** The rest of round two of the projected shadow. Where the shadow starts to run -
the Shadow mode row stepped to Projected, HD switched on with it, Lara walking from a room
drawn classic into an HD one, the map made again after a lost device - it comes in over a
quarter second of game time instead of in one frame, and her blob and every creature's
blob that gives way to it go out over the same quarter second. The depth terms are cut so
that a floor a block or more below her soles, or about a block below a creature's feet,
takes nothing of the shadow - a storey under it, and the floor of the room beside behind
a wall - while the floor a creature stands on, a step and half a block below it take its
whole outline: the creatures' map keeps each creature's feet beside its outline.
The receive gives the fog bulbs' haze back: a shadow no longer stands dark inside a
glowing bulb. The shadow's log line times the models' pass and counts the arrival.
ModelProbe surveys where the shadow lands behind a face, draws the models' glows after
their receive and leaves its Resets out with rooms.

**Why.** Round two's Left: the switch between blob and projection inside one picture, the
shadow through walls and floors, the fog, and the probe's two lows.

**How.** The arrival: `HDShadowPresence` (`specific/hd/hd_shadow.h:773`) is 3f^2 - 2f^3 of
f = t / `HD_SHADOW_FADE_IN` 0.25, exactly 1 from there on; `HDShadowArrive` (`:785`) sets
t back to 0 in a frame the shadow does not run in and adds the frame's game time in one it
runs in; `HDShadowBlobAlpha` (`:803`) scales a blob vertex's alpha byte, and a weight of 1
gives the colour itself. `HDShadowFrameDecide` steps it on a clock of its own
(`specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp:1136`), so her blob, drawn before her step, and the strength
the step draws (`:1014`, the following's strength times the presence) read the same value;
`HDShadowFrameBlob` (`:1146`) draws her blob while the presence is below 1, the three
`DrawLara` variants ask it (`specific/drawlara.cpp:137`, `:396`, `:664`), and
`HDShadowFrameBlobWeight` (`:1151`) gives her blob's weight. A creature:
`HDObjectBlobGivesWay` (`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp:4410`) lets it cast as before and
answers false while the presence is below 1, remembering the item and 1 minus the presence
for `HDObjectBlobWeight` (`:4446`), which `S_PrintCircleShadow` reads for the alpha of
every vertex (`specific/specificfx.cpp:6691`). The way back is not faded: a frame the gate
refuses draws no map. The cut: `HD_SHADOW_FULL` 576 and `HD_SHADOW_END` 1088 below her
lowest node, `HD_SHADOW_OTHERS_FULL` 1024 and `HD_SHADOW_OTHERS_END` 1280 behind a
creature's place (`hd_shadow.h:218` to `:229`); her reach shrinks with hers, and the
second reach (`HDShadowReachOthers`, `:1570`) runs OTHERS_END past the farthest place a
caster may have, OTHERS_MARGIN of the depth beyond the far side. A creature's place is
its position, the point at its feet: `HDObjectEnd` keeps its depth in the second box
(`hd_object.cpp:3275`), `HDObjectCastOthersFrame` hands it to the cast (`:4162`) through
`HDRenderShadowPlace` (`hd_render.cpp:7766`, pixel c18, which the cast bracket saves and
puts back, `:7732`), `CastPS` writes it into the green channel
(`hd_shader/hd_shadow.hlsl:91`) of the second map, a G32R32F target now
(`hd_render.cpp:7668`; hers stays R32F), and `OthersShade` measures each tap's distance
from it (`hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl:425`), as `HDShadowLookupBehind` does with
the places beside the depths (`hd_shadow.h:1328`); the second part's measure from each
tap's own caster is replaced. The fog: every receive variant ends in `ReceiveOut`
(`hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl:180`) - the bulbs' haze, `BulbIntensity`
copied from the room shader, summed and saturated as RoomPS sums it, times gPass.w, times
1 - k in colour, k in alpha - and the two receive brackets blend ONE / SRCALPHA
(`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`, `HDRenderShadowReceiveBegin` and
`HDRenderShadowModelsBegin`), so a pixel is surface * k + haze; without a bulb the colour
is 0 and the picture is the picture times k. The log: `ShadowModelsPass`
(`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp:6535`) times itself, and `HDLOG shadow second` gains `mms=` and
`arrive=` at its end. ModelProbe (`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`):
`-shadowsurvey` with `-surveyplace`, `-surveyrooms`, `-surveyterms`, `-surveyslots` and
`-surveyout`, her term measured from her lowest node and a creature's from its place;

**Measured.** Through walls and floors (ModelProbe `-shadowsurvey` on the thirteen levels'

### The Mods folder: models, texture pages and sounds from a mod
2026-09-13 - 2026-09-14

**What.** The engine reads the Remaster's own drop-in mod layout,
`Mods\<Category>\<Mod>\{4,5}\{ITEM,TEX,DATA}`. A mod is a folder directly under `Mods`,
or one level deeper, that has a `4` or a `5` subfolder or a `mod.txt`; a name beginning
with `_` is switched off at every depth, which is the whole way back to vanilla and
needs no uninstall. The order is the relative path compared as lower-case ASCII, and
that order is the priority. The scan runs once per session and both the HD level build
and `HQSfxOpen` ask for it, so the two see one list. A mod may supply models (`.TRM`,
resolved in front of the installs), texture pages, a whole `MAIN.SFX` sound bank, and
single replacement samples as loose `<NNNN>.wav` files - exactly four digits, at any
depth under an active mod, first active mod wins per number. `OUTFIT_*.TRM` is refused
as a replacement, because a mod's outfit is an entry in the wardrobe scan. `mod.txt` may
carry `origin=tr1|tr2|tr3`, which puts that game folder of the Tomb Raider I-III bundle
and its two siblings into the mod's page chain. The sound half does not depend on
`hd_enable`. `HQSfxOpen` walks three bank candidates: the first active mod that ships
`5\DATA\MAIN.SFX`, then `audio\MAIN.SFX`, then the installed Remaster's own
`5\DATA\MAIN.SFX` read where it lies, the third making a hand copy into `audio\`
unnecessary. Two further rules act on a mod's models. A weapon hand whose pages resolve
into the origin bundle is drawn on the install's own hands: the mod's triangles on those
pages are dropped and the install's file of the same name is loaded into a companion
slot cut to the pages it shares with `HAND_BARE_REST`, the two drawn together with the
same matrices, node mask and light. And a `.TRM` inventory model a mod brought over from
Tomb Raider I, II or III is put into the donor game's own pose before the ring fits it.

**Why.** A mod may never change a page of a model it did not supply: vanilla is
untouchable, and the mechanism makes that impossible rather than merely unlikely, which
is why the page namespace is arithmetic with compile-time assertions behind it.
`origin=` exists because a mod's model may name pages belonging to another game of the
collection: a measured hand model names 6111 and 6112, its own, and 8002 and 8010, which
are Lara's skin sheets of the I-III bundle, while in the IV-VI bundle those numbers hold
other art (`4\TEX\8002.DDS` is a cut-out sheet that reads 14.5 per cent holes) - without
the line the hand is painted with it, with it both pages come from `1\TEX` and read 0.0
per cent holes. `4\DATA\MAIN.SFX` is deliberately not used: that is Tomb Raider IV's
bank with its own numbering. The plausibility rule that has guarded the HQ bank since
#117 compares the bank's sample against the level's own - at twice the rate the same
recording must be about twice as long, and anything further off than a fifth is a wrong
pairing - and a sound mod breaks it on purpose: at one measured sound id the unmodded
bank holds 3388 bytes at 44100 Hz (0.038 s) against a mod's 28782 bytes at 48000 Hz
(0.300 s), 7.81 times longer, and the landing 1.64 times, so the rule as it stood would
have refused precisely the samples the mod exists to change. A mod's file is a
stranger's file, so the bank and wav readers had to be safe against a crafted one:
`long` is 32 bit in this build, so a chunk guard written `at + 8 + len > bytes`
overflows to a negative number on a length near `LONG_MAX`, the test comes out false,
the cursor is driven negative and the next read lands about two gigabytes below the
buffer - a 60-byte file ended the process that way. A legal wav need not begin with its
format block: a `fact` or a `LIST` may stand in front of `fmt`, and the shape audio
workstations write is a 28-byte `JUNK` block first, so a `WAVEFORMATEX` laid over offset
20 reads the middle of that header, the format test comes out false, the mod's recording
is dropped without a word and the log goes on claiming an overlay nobody will hear; of
six crafted files the gate accepts four and three of those have their format block at
+56, +48 and +28. Without the hand rule a mod's hand is painted with the donor bundle's
skin sheets and comes out looking gloved; the decision is made inside `hd_model` and not
by the caller, because only `hd_model` has the file open and the pages resolved, and the
twin's pages are cut against `HAND_BARE_REST` because that file's pages are skin and
nothing else, so the cut cannot bring the install's own gun in beside the mod's. Without
the classic pose a converted model stands in half a pose: a Remaster `.TRM` stores each
node's vertices with the classic mesh tree's offsets applied and no rotation at all, the
game it came from putting the rotation on when it draws out of the classic object's own
frame 0, so no turn of the rigid file can reproduce the picture the donor game draws.
Applied, the two guns of a mod's `UZI_OPTION` go from parallel to the crossed pair its
home game shows - the angle between their long axes from 0.0 to 65.5 degrees, the pair
from 132 units thick to 60, its overflow of the ring's place from 3.36x to 1.65x - and
the ammunition crosses the same way (0.2 to 42.1 degrees).

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_mods.cpp`/`.h` are the scanner, engine-free like
`hd_install.cpp` so the diagnostic tools link the same file; `winmain.cpp` starts it.
The model resolver sits in front of `find_model` (`hd_model.cpp`): the active mods in
order, each `5\ITEM` then `4\ITEM`, then the installs exactly as before - a replacement
by resolution and never on disk. The page namespace (`hd_pagecache.h`/`.cpp`) offers a
mod's page to the cache as `HD_PAGE_MOD_BASE + modIndex * HD_PAGE_MOD_STRIDE + page`,
`HD_PAGE_MOD_BASE` = 0x50000000 and `HD_PAGE_MOD_STRIDE` = 0x00010000, so a mod's 6111
and the install's 6111 are two cache slots holding two pictures; three `static_assert`s
prove the three namespaces - plain, the I-III bundle's `HD_PAGE_ALT_BASE` (0x40000000)
and the mods' - cannot meet, and a build in which they could fails to compile. A page a
vanilla model asks for never carries a mod key. The chain for a mod's page is the mod's
own `5\TEX`, then its `4\TEX`, then - only with `origin=` - that game folder of the
I-III bundle and its two siblings, then the ordinary IV-VI chain with the plain number,
which lets a mod ship models and no art. `hd_lara.cpp`'s rule that tells a weapon hand's
gun from its skin ("every page this model has that `HAND_BARE_REST` has not got is the
weapon") strips the namespace and compares page numbers. One consequence is left
standing: a page a mod's model shares with the install is loaded twice, +4 pages and
+5.3 MiB on one wardrobe (21 to 25 pages, 28.0 to 33.3 MiB) and nothing on the whole
level; sharing the slot would be safe, but the rule that a mod's model never shares a
slot with a vanilla one is worth more than 1.5 per cent of a wardrobe. Sound:
`specific/sfxbank.cpp`/`.h` hold the `MAIN.SFX` layout, the chain walk that tests it,
the RIFF check and the chain's order (`SfxBankChainLink`, lazy so nothing pays for
`HDInstallRoot()`'s walk through the registry and every Steam library unless the link
that needs it is reached), and both the engine and `SfxProbe` walk that one order;
`hqsfx.cpp`/`.h` keep the level bridge, the substitution and the log. A loose `.wav` is
checked the way the bank's own samples are - RIFF WAVE, uncompressed PCM, mono, 16 bit,
a `data` chunk inside the file - with a 4 MiB cap so a mistyped name cannot pull a video
into memory; without any bank there is no bridge from a level's sample number to a bank
number and the log says so once. The ruler is the first unmodded bank of the chain,
opened beside the mod's and never played from, walked through its own sound id table
rather than by sample number, because the two banks have different sample counts (473
against 463 in the measured case) and nothing says a number means the same sound in
both; if the ruler's sample for this level sample is the right length the bridge is
right and the mod's recording plays whatever its length. The chunk guards subtract
instead of adding - `len > bytes - at - 8`, where the loop's invariant `at + 8 <= bytes`
makes the difference non-negative by construction - in `SfxRiffCheck` and in
`SfxBankOpen`'s outer chain walk, and a bad file is refused with `a chunk runs past the
end of the file`. `HQSfxPayload` goes through that same bounds-checked gate, which
matters because a mod's `5\DATA\MAIN.SFX` stands at the head of the chain and
`SfxBankOpen` validates only the outer chain of RIFFs. `SfxRiffCheck` hands back where
it found the chunks as `SfxRiffParts` and `HQSfxPayload` passes that on; `LoadSamples`
(`specific/file.cpp`) reads the format block at `parts.fmtAt` and the audio at
`parts.dataAt` and takes the PCM branch on `hq` alone, because everything the payload
path returns has already been shown to be mono 16-bit PCM, and the contract that makes
`HQSfxSubstituted()` and `HQSfxOverlaid()` true by construction is written into
`hqsfx.h`. The level's own samples are untouched - their tag is still read at 20, and
the one call that still lays a `WAVEFORMATEX` over offset 20, `DXCreateSampleADPCM`, is
only ever handed `samples_buffer`, which no mod can reach; the two walks differ in one
point (`file.cpp`'s breaks at the first `data` chunk, `SfxRiffCheck`'s reports the last)
and over 1409 samples of three banks and five loose files not one has a second `data`
chunk, a second `fmt`, or a `fmt` anywhere but +20. The hand rule: `hd_model.cpp` asks
`HDPageCacheOriginOf`, which calls `resolve_page` and loads nothing, for where each of a
model's pages really resolves (`hd_pagecache.cpp`/`.h` export it); measured on one level
with nine mods, the mod's hand keeps 2 pages and 31,267 vertices on nodes 10 and 13, the
install's twin brings 1 page, and the mod's holster model stays whole at 27,624 vertices
on nodes 1 and 4. The twin is counted in every column of the part line - vertices,
indices, ranges, pages and both byte counts, about 155 KiB of buffer under one Uzi mod -
its own fold counters are printed there, and its second `.TRM` read is counted into
`read_ms`; the twin's page cut and a caller's own `onlyPage` cut are one mechanism,
combined as a DROP set with a line in the log, because dropping every page of a file is
representable and keeping none of it is not. The classic pose:
`specific/hd/hd_classic.cpp`/`.h` is engine-free, plain C on the outside, with no engine
global and no `Log`; it walks `<I-III bundle>/<game>/DATA` in name order until a level
file holds the object with at least one mesh and hands back the mesh count, the bones,
frame 0 and the level file it used, every count read out of a file checked against the
bytes that are left and the texture pages seeked past rather than loaded, one parse per
(game, id) per session with refusals cached. The three level layouts are the published
TR1/TR2/TR3 formats; the `.TRM` says which node a vertex rides on and the classic level
file says where the mesh tree puts that node, and both are the player's own data files -
nothing of any Remaster binary is in it. Two format facts were settled by measurement
against the files' own data: in a TR1 frame the SECOND of the two rotation words is the
high half (read that way the walk reproduces the frames' own bounding boxes to 2.1 units
at worst over the eight weapon and ammunition objects of `1/DATA/GYM.PHD`, against 50 to
107 units the other way, and Tomb Raider 1's object 102 then gives the same rotations,
bones and bounds as Tomb Raider 2's 160 and Tomb Raider 3's 188), and the pose is
`phd_RotYXZ` (y, then x, then z) with the point taken as a column and the frame's offset
part of the pose, reproducing those boxes to 2.1 units where the next family of
conventions misses by 40.8 and the worst by 184.7. "The first level in name order" is a
rule and holds: over the eight option objects of games 1 and 2 every level file that
holds the object holds the same mesh count, bones and frame 0, and game 3 agrees on 17
of its 20, the three exceptions being `TITLE.TR2` and `AREA51.TR2` carrying a stub or a
left-over. The pose is applied in `hd_model.cpp` where the mirror fold is, right after
the `.TRM` is read and before `build()` takes the box and the principal axes, and it is
real skinning - three nodes, three weights, normals turned and re-normalised; it refuses
with a line unless the model came from a mod with an `origin=` game, its name is in the
table, and the classic object's mesh count IS the `.TRM`'s node count, which is the
proof that the two belong together because a `.TRM`'s bone numbers are classic mesh
numbers. The table in `hd_classic.cpp` has thirteen rows - the four weapons and the
ammunition boxes under the donor games' own names and under this engine's slot names -
and its object ids come from GPL sources: TR3's out of the **tomb3** sources
(`game/objects.h`), TR1's and TR2's out of the **TRX** project (LostArtefacts),
`catalog_objects.csv`, whose TR3 column agrees with tomb3 on every id; each was then
found in the player's own installation. Cost, whole process: 85 to 93 ms once per (game,
id) per session. Seams behind `-log`: `MODLOG folder=` (with `mods=` on both branches),
one `MODLOG mod<i> path= origin= models= pages= bank= wavs=` per mod, `MODLOG disabled
<path>`, `MODLOG model <NAME> <- mod<i>` once per replaced model per session, written
where `find_model` accepts the answer and keyed by name and mod so a face looked up for
a body from another mod cannot log a replacement that was never drawn, `MODLOG page
mod<i>:<n> comes from ...`, `MODLOG bank <label> (<path>) - opened/not opened`, `MODLOG
bank ruler:`, `MODLOG bridge:`, `MODLOG bank sample <n> ...`, `MODLOG wav <nnnn> <-
mod<i>` and `MODLOG wav <nnnn> refused - <why>`; a mod page prints as `mod<i>:<n>`

`HDLOG classic <game>/<level> object <id> meshes=.. bones=.. frame0 ..`, its refusal,
and `HDLOG level=.. ring pose slot=.. model=.. classic=<game>/<level>#<id> nodes=..
applied (box .. -> ..)` or `not posed: <why>` cover the pose. Tools: `ModelProbe -mods
<folder>`, `-tr3 <3-folder>`, `-nohandmix`, `-classicpose <game> <MODEL_NAME>`,
`-noclassicpose`, with the page list naming the folder every page was really read from;
`SfxProbe` and `bsfx.bat` are new, `-samples` pushing every sample of the chosen bank

### Imported enemy sounds are named in the sidecar, not guessed at by length
2026-09-13

**What.** A run that imports a Tomb Raider III enemy writes the sound ids it wrote into
the level as one `sfximport <id> <id> ...` line in the `.hdm` sidecar, ascending out of
a `std::set` so that the same seed gives the same file, and no line at all in a run that
imported nothing. The HQ sound bridge refuses to pair those ids with the Remaster's bank
and writes a line for each; ids the run merely moved between TR5 levels are not in the
list and keep their pairing. Beside that the bridge works out, from the level's own
sound map alone, which of the bank's 64 level bits is the level being loaded - the bit
whose ids cover this level's and no others, every id the level has and the bit claims
counting for it and every one it does not counting against it - and writes a line for
every pairing that bit excludes. The sidecar is read above the HD gate, so the list is
in force in the shipping build with `hd_enable` off.

**Why.** The guests take free slots of the TR5 sound map - the vulture 420..423, the
Compy 430..434, the raptor 438..444, the T-Rex 445..449 - and free means free in a TR5
level; it says nothing about the Remaster's bank, where ids 418..423 are six voice
lines. The bridge pairs by sound id and judges a pairing by length, and a length cannot
tell a wrong pairing from a different recording: on one randomized level the level's own
420, 421 and 423 (322, 425 and 406 ms) were refused against the bank's 624, 624 and 1037
ms, but 422 at 604 ms against the bank's 624 was accepted at 1.03 times the expected
length, so an imported vulture died speaking an English voice line. A mod's bank with
390 sound ids against the install's 396 simply has not got 418..423. A length cannot
decide this and a name can: the run knows exactly which ids it wrote. The level bit is
worked out and not tabulated, because a table of level names would be silently wrong
about a randomized level or a level pack, and it is sound: over all sixteen classic
levels each matches exactly one bit and matches it completely while the runner-up covers
at most two thirds (ANDREA1 bit 1, ANDREA2 2, ANDREA3 3, JOBY2 4, JOBY3 5, JOBY4 6,
JOBY5 7, ANDY1 8, ANDY2 9, ANDY3 10, RICH1 11, RICH2 12, RICH3 14); on one randomized
level it names 32 excluded pairings, every one an enemy the run moved there. The sidecar
is read above the HD gate because it is a level fact and not an HD fact: read below it
the list was empty in the shipping build - the bank chain the refusal protects is
deliberately not gated, since sound does not care whether `hd_enable` is on - so the
wrong pairing came back and the summary reported nought imported ids, and no tool could
show it, because a tool calls the sidecar loader unconditionally by construction.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_markers.cpp`/`.h` read the `sfximport` line and answer
`HDMarkersSoundImported`. `hd_level.cpp`/`.h` call `HDMarkersLoad` above the
`HDEnabled()` gate; the other half of the bracket, `HDMarkersFree` in `HDLevelUnload`,
was never gated. The order is unchanged and all on the load thread: `FreeLevel` ->
`HDMarkersFree`, `HDLevelLoad` -> `HDMarkersLoad`, then `LoadSamples` -> `HQSfxBuildMap`
-> the refusal. `specific/hqsfx.cpp`/`.h` hold the bridge and the refusal lines;
`SfxBankLevelBit` and `SfxPairPlausible` live in `specific/sfxbank.cpp`/`.h`, so a tool
judges a pairing with the engine's own arithmetic rather than a copy, and the mask
counter counts first and prints second, so the summary is not capped at the 32 lines it
prints. On the writing side, `TR5Randomizer/src/core/Tr5Level.cpp`/`.h` collect the ids
and `core/ApplyPatch.cpp` writes the line, the slot ranges being `Tr5Source::dinos`; an
engine older than this has no rule for the word and ignores the line, which is what the
sidecar format was built for. Tool: `SfxProbe -level <path.trc>` reads a finished level
and the sidecar beside it and prints the whole decision table, `-samples` checks the
bank's 473 samples, and `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/bsfx.bat` builds it.

### The font in HD
2026-09-09

**What.** Every line of text the game draws - the title menu, the names under the
inventory ring, the options pages, the load and save lists, the statistics, the
ammunition counter, the name of a pickup, the subtitles of a cutscene - is drawn from
the Remaster's 2048 x 2048 font atlas when it is installed, through one branch in
`DrawChar` (`game/text.cpp`). Position, size, `FontShades` colour and specular stay the
classic ones, because they stay the classic code. Thirteen of the 106 glyph rectangles
keep the classic picture: the twelve PlayStation pad icons, which the atlas does not
carry, and the c-cedilla.

**Why.** All text in the engine comes out of ONE 256 x 256 page and ONE table of 106
rectangles, so a single branch covers every text path and there is no second one to
forget. The big atlas is a new drawing and not the small picture times eight: shrunk
back to 256 with an 8 x 8 box filter it differs from `FONT0_OG.DDS` in 12.6 per cent of
the texels of the matched rectangles, its letters reach up to three classic texels past
the eightfold rectangle, and it carries a dark rim and a drop shadow the small one has
not (over the 93 matched glyphs, fully opaque texels have a mean brightness of 224 of
255 and the half-transparent ones 44), which is what makes white letters readable over a
bright wall.

**How.** The page is the same in every level - md5 `191cfc2fdba5b4c54024361c463d7537`
over all sixteen shipped `.TRC` files, the title included - so the match runs once in a
session and every further level load is a comparison of that md5 (`HDFontLevelPage`,
`specific/hd/hd_font.cpp`); it is keyed on the page and not on a flag, so a level file
carrying a different font page would be matched again rather than drawn with another
alphabet's table. Matching: the classic rectangle's ink mask is slid over
`5\TEX\FONT0_OG.DDS` (256 x 256, uncompressed B8G8R8A8, the classic glyph bitmaps
re-typeset in ASCII order) and scored intersection over union
(`specific/hd/hd_fontmatch.cpp`, `HDFontMatchAll`), accepted at 0.94 and above. The idea
and the threshold are TROne's (GPLv3, TROne by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931), and the reason is theirs too: a similar character is
the wrong character. 93 of the 106 rectangles are found, 92 at score 1.000 and the K at
0.975; `FONT1` is checked in the same run and matches 22 - it is a Cyrillic alphabet and
those 22 are the letters both scripts draw alike - so which atlas is used is decided by
the count and not by the file's name, and an installation that ships them the other way
round still works. Drawing: `5\TEX\FONT0.DDS` is 2048 x 2048, BC7, six mip levels, the
same alphabet in the same places at eight times the size, so a normalised coordinate on
the one is a normalised coordinate on the other and the glyph sits at the same place
plus a whole number of classic texels; the UV is therefore not recomputed but SHIFTED by
that number, and rendered classic and HD the texels a screen pixel walks agree to
1.6e-06 relative. The margin is per glyph: the classic arithmetic samples the rectangle
inset by half a texel on each side, which the classic page needs because it packs its
glyphs with no gap, and at eight times the size that inset is four HD texels and cuts
off exactly the antialiased rim and the drop shadow, 12.6 per cent of a glyph's ink; the
sampling window and the quad are widened by the same fraction of themselves (TROne's
rule), which changes what is visible and not where anything is. A uniform margin does
not work - at every margin from half a texel upwards a slice of the neighbouring tick
appears beside the apostrophe and beside the comma - so `HDFontMargins` works out per
glyph how far the window may open before it touches another letter, with one texel as
the ceiling: 90 of the 93 get the whole texel, the apostrophe 0.25, the asterisk and the
comma 0.125, none gets zero. The flood fill runs over WHITE ink, which the dark shadow
between two letters separates where alpha does not; it runs on the big picture and is
seeded from the classic page's ink rather than from the whole matched rectangle, because
a neighbour's larger letter can reach a texel or two into that rectangle. Accents keep
their classic arithmetic: `PrintString` composes an accented letter from two ordinary
glyphs - the base at the letter's place and the mark at `def->w / 2 + x - 3, y +
def->YOffset` - and each goes through `DrawChar` on its own, so the relative position
between them is the classic one. Colour and alpha needed no change: the engine
multiplies the texture by the vertex colour and adds the specular half
(`D3DTOP_MODULATE` with `D3DTA_DIFFUSE`, `specific/function_table.cpp`), the atlas's ink
is white so it takes that colour as the classic page's white ink does, the dark rim
stays dark whatever it is multiplied by, and `D3DRS_ALPHAREF` is 0 with
`D3DCMP_NOTEQUAL`, so the alpha test throws away only what is completely transparent.
`Textures[]` must not grow, because the font is addressed as `nTextures - 2`, the sky as
`- 1` and the two title pages as `- 4` and `- 5`, so the glyph quad carries
`HD_FONT_TPAGE` = 4096, which is not an index at all, and `HWR_DrawSortList`
(`specific/polyinsert.cpp`) turns it into the font texture before any of its cases can
read `Textures[4096]`; nothing else can write that number, a tpage being otherwise
always an index and `LoadTextures` refusing a level with more than the 256 entries the
array has, and the sort list already groups by tpage, so every glyph of a frame ends up
in one draw call. Mips and a LOD bias: at 1920 x 1080 a thirteen-texel glyph is drawn 58
pixels high out of 104 atlas texels, so the atlas is minified by 1.8 - by 2.7 at 1280 x
720 and 1.35 at 2560 x 1440 - and without mips that is a bilinear undersample in which
thin strokes crawl, so the whole six-level chain out of the `.DDS` is uploaded and the
draw sets `D3DTEXF_LINEAR` with `D3DSAMP_MIPMAPLODBIAS` -0.7, which lands at level 0.14
at 1080p and 0 at 1440p, the sampler states being put back the way the classic path
keeps them the moment the call returns; the three minification figures are our own
measurement and the bias -0.7 is TROne's number (GPLv3, `host/render/game_renderer.cpp`
of its copy of 2026-09-13; in TROne-main, copy of 2026-10-05, the shader `k_ui_frag`),
cited as such in `specific/polyinsert.cpp`. Where it lives:
`game/chardef.inc` holds the 106 rectangles, moved out of `text.cpp` unchanged, and
`game/accent.inc` the 46 accented letters, so the engine, the HD font and `FontProbe`
read the same numbers; `specific/hd/hd_fontmatch.cpp` holds the matcher, the margins, an
uncompressed-DDS reader and an MD5 with no engine dependency at all, so `FontProbe`
compiles that very file; `specific/hd/hd_font.cpp` finds the atlas, runs the match on
the load thread, makes the texture on the main thread and answers `DrawChar`'s one
question; `game/text.cpp` gains one branch, `specific/polyinsert.cpp` one, and
`specific/file.cpp` two lines - the font page to the matcher where it is read, and
`HDFontBuild` beside `HDLevelBuild`. Seam: `HDLOG font atlas=FONT0 matched=93/106
below=13 page=<md5>`, one line per glyph that did not make it with its score, and one
line saying how many glyphs got the whole margin. Classic path: `HDFontLevelPage`
returns at its first line with `hd_enable` off, so no file is opened and not a byte of
the page is copied, `g_matched` stays false, `HDFontBuild` returns, there is no texture,
`HDFontGlyphAt` returns 0 on its first test, and `DrawChar` runs the same arithmetic
with the same `tex.tpage = nTextures - 2`, while `HWR_DrawSortList`'s new branch tests
for a tpage no quad can then carry; `fps_mode` is not touched. Files: `game/text.cpp`,
`game/chardef.inc`, `game/accent.inc`, `specific/hd/hd_font.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_fontmatch.cpp`/`.h`, `specific/polyinsert.cpp`, `specific/file.cpp`,
`specific/function_table.cpp`, `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/FontProbe.cpp`.
