### Where the HD rules come from, counted on our own data
2026-10-06

**What.** Every rule of the HD path that came by way of TROne or TRForge now carries this
project's own evidence, is declared this project's free choice, is credited to TROne's own
design under the GPLv3, or is gone; `THIRD-PARTY.md` keeps the list as an origin ledger of
39 entries, each with its class and its evidence. Five `TrgProbe` switches count the rules
on the player's own files: `-shadeorder` (how the two colour triples of a `.TRG` vertex
make the room light), `-uvbytes` (which bytes are u, v and the layer), `-normals` and
`-trmnormals` (the normal bias of a `.TRG` and of a `.TRM`, and the sway range) and
`-ddssizes` (the size of every page). With the room light settled as the SUM by that
count, the room shader drops the spare scale it carried on the first triple, the one
place where the shape of a rule read off the Remaster's shaders stood in the code; the
room vertex shader now reads nothing of `c4`, which `fxc` gives a literal of its own, so
the room passes write `c4` to the pixel file alone. `HDScanPagePath` no longer tries
`<n>_2048.DDS` and `<n>_1024.DDS` for ids 8000..8499, a branch that never applies.
`vendor/trforge/src/trf_remaster/Trg.h` leaves out its two passages that told in words
what the Remaster's renderer does with a vertex and with the point lights, and its
dangling "see below"; `VERSION.txt` and `NOTICE.md` say so with the new hash. Sentences
about what the Remaster's program does become the file facts they rest on; every line
number into TROne's files becomes the function it falls in and the copy it was read in;
sentences about TROne's state are dated. The picture of the game is the same.

**Why.** A reading of every line of TROne, TRForge and this tree found four rules of the
HD path that TRForge's or TROne's text names as readings of the Remaster's shaders, none
of them in this tree as code, an address, a table or shader text, all of them as plain
prose rules: the room light as `colour1 * factor + colour2` with the factor at 1
(TROne's, resting on TRForge's reading of the extracted shaders); which bytes of a `.TRG`
vertex are u, v and the biased normal (TRForge's names); which of material 16's
`param[0]` and `param[2]` is the ripple's scale and which its rate (the order TROne's
prose names); and `param[0]` of materials 6, 7 and 8 as the cut-out threshold. The first
three had come at second hand with no evidence of this project's own and no origin
sentence naming the route; the fourth already had its own count here. The vendored
`Trg.h` carried TRForge's prose about the renderer's use of the vertex and of the point
lights besides. Beside them stood
numbers with no stated origin - eleven pages "of 4096x4096" (they are 4096x2048), the
slot names "strength, scale, scale" of materials 7 and 8, the three-resolution id range of
TRForge's - and the cleanup of 2026-09-22 had shortened the origin note over material
16's order. The keyword search of the push audit found none of it, because none of it
names a program.

**How.** `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/TrgProbe.cpp`: `classicRoomData` (`:4414`) walks a
classic room's 28-byte vertices and faces straight out of the `.TRC` the way
`Tr5Level::roomFaces` does and keeps each vertex's prelight, the colour
`aRoomletTransformLight` lights it with; `dumpShadeOrder` (`:4650`) pairs them with the
`.TRG` vertices of the same group at the same room-local position (the water marks'
road; several `.TRG` vertices at one position are averaged) and prints, per level and over
all, the Spearman rank correlation of the classic shade with `c1+c2`, `c1*c2`, `c1` and
`c2` (each the sum of its three channels), the agree / disagree / tie counts over 200,000
sampled vertex pairs, and the pairs that sum and product put in opposite order with the
side the classic shade takes; `dumpUvBytes` (`:4947`) interpolates the classic texinfo's
u and v at every `.TRG` vertex lying inside one classic face (in its plane, inside one of
its two triangles with a margin of 0.02), counts per face the order of every two vertices
under the classic coordinate against the byte, fits each byte on the classic (u, v) and
holds the fits of the faces wearing one texinfo against each other; `dumpTrgNormals`
(`:5440`) and `dumpTrmNormals` (`:5509`) hold every triangle corner's normal against the
triangle's plane; `dumpDdsSizes` (`:5571`) reads the width and height of every `.DDS`
header. `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl:875`: `o.light = lerp(inC0.rgb + inC1.rgb,
1.0f, gFlat.x)`; the header (`:4`), the light note (`:87`) and the register note name the
count. `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp:7527` and `:8442`: `gPass.z` is written 0 and `c4` goes
to the pixel file only; `MaterialRipple` (`:876`, note at `:816`) states the order of
scale and rate as a free choice, the coincidence with TROne's reading, and TROne's own
design of the ripple's structure (also `PartUvSpan`, `:753`, and `hd_room.hlsl`'s ripple
note); the material list names the ranges of materials 7 and 8 in place of slot names.
`specific/hd/hd_scan.cpp:95`: the plain page name only. The page sizes:
`hd_render.cpp:4197`, `hd_level.cpp`'s `kWidestPage` note, `hd_pagecache.cpp`'s staging
and batch notes, `hd_memory.h`. The water surface the `.TRG` has no geometry for:
`hd_level.cpp:282`, `:1614`, `:4795`, and the table's "0 of 15" is 0 of 13, 61 of 93 rooms
in all. `hd_pagecache.cpp:367` (`WHITE.DDS`, the install's white tile in `4\TEX`) and
`:659` (the cut-out threshold, 42 of 44 tuples). Credits: TROne's measurement of a facial
rig's inverse binds (`hd_trm.h`, `hd_trm.cpp`), its six default control constants
(`game/modern_move.h`), its ripple design, its caustic shape and scale with the strength
0.32 named as ours, and the notice in `hd_wardrobe.h`. Citations by function and copy in
`hd_render.cpp/.h`, `hd_model.cpp/.h`, `hd_object.cpp/.h`, `hd_lara.cpp/.h`,
`hd_laradraw.cpp`, `hd_level.cpp`, `hd_fontmatch.cpp`, `hd_pagecache.cpp`, `hd_room.hlsl`,
`hd_model.hlsl`, `game/draw.cpp`, `specific/polyinsert.cpp`, `game/modern_move.cpp`,
`game/modern_camera.h` and `ModernTest.cpp`. `vendor/trforge/src/trf_remaster/Trg.h:44`
and `:113` carry the one-line notes.

**Measured.** The room light (`TrgProbe <5> -all -shadeorder -classic <data\Backup>`):
107,118 of the 126,170 classic room vertices of the fifteen levels have a `.TRG` vertex of
their own group at exactly their position. Rank correlation with the classic prelight,

### The water sheets: this project's own water surface
2026-10-07

**What.** Every water square of every HD level the sheet can cover - a square over an
underwater room, in a room drawn HD - gets a water surface of this project's own design,
built from the classic level's data at level load: a *sheet*, a grid that moves,
reflects, lets the pool floor show through and foams at the bank. A water plane with no
underwater room below keeps the level's own restored faces. Its wave, the swell and
UV wobble on the Remaster's own marked water art and the caustic on pool floors and walls
are one design of this project's own, which replaces the wave, swell, wobble and caustic
shapes the entry "Water in the HD rooms" took from TROne; the wind keeps TROne's shape and
its credit. One new option, `tomb5.hd_water` (registry `hd_water`, on by default), one new
options row *Graphics* -> *HD water*, one new text file `hd_water.txt` beside the
executable, one new log seam `WATERLOG` behind `-log`, and RoomProbe `-hdwater 0|1` and
`-waterfile`.

**Why.** At the five places measured first - ANDREA2's fountain hall (rooms 144, 229,
231), its fountain 194, its sewer under room 60, JOBY2's water along the submarine (42,
76) and its southern half (143) - there was no HD water surface at all: the surfaces were
the level's own restored classic faces with the Remaster's glint pages (means 14 and 30 of
255), drawn by the classic path, and ANDREA2 room 76 had no surface by either path. The
water was to be this project's own, from general graphics knowledge and counts on our own
data. Project decisions of 2026-10-07: the sheet replaces the restored classic faces; the
Remaster's own material 16 water in ANDREA2 room 231 stays over it; the palette is judged
in the game; the channel murky and the basin clear; the sea foam finer, and a foam scale
per body of water (`hd_water.txt`); every water room of every level gets its sheet by the
data rule; the override table becomes a text file; the light direction stands per class;
and all fifteen levels are built at once, secured by the option, by a sweep table over
all levels and by the text file, while the tuning stays with ANDREA2 and JOBY2. After the
review, also of 2026-10-07: `hd_water 0` switches the caustic under a surface off too;
every water square of a room drawn HD gets its sheet whatever flat art the Remaster lays
on it, and the rooms where that art lies over a sheet are tuned later, through the text
file's class `none` where needed. After the owner's first play test of 2026-10-07: the
water still looks very static, the waves monotonous, the foam static, opaque and the
same at every bank; the second stage - the floor seen through the sheet, bent by the
waves and tinted per channel - comes first, so that the water can be judged honestly,
and the life of the water is folded in after it; master waits until the water is
complete.

**How.** The data rule (`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`, `HDRenderSetWaterSheets` :8872): a
square of a room that is not under water whose room below (`FLOOR_INFO::pit_room`) is an
underwater room is water, its surface its own floor (clicks times 256); the depth walks
down through further water portals to the first floor that is not one, at most six rooms
(`water_depth` :8686). Squares are joined four-connected at one world height across rooms
into bodies; a flipmap twin joins the body of the square at its place and is counted as a
twin. A square draws a sheet when its room draws its own HD group, whatever flat art the
Remaster lays over it - that art draws in its own pass as it does without the sheet,
opaque art in the opaque pass before the sheet, additive art after it - unless a row of
class `none` reached its body. The class rule (`WaterClassOf` :8515): sea when any room
of the body carries `ROOM_OUTSIDE` or `ROOM_NOT_INSIDE`, channel when indoors with 16
squares or more and twice the area over the perimeter under 2, basin otherwise. The class
table (:8295): wavelengths 260/150/85/47, 420/230/120/64 and 1500/700/330/150 units,
heights 2.0/1.4/0.8/0.45, 3.0/1.8/0.9/0.45 and 38/16/7/2.8, speeds by deep-water
dispersion, omega = calm * sqrt(g k) with g = 4300 units/s^2 (`kWaterG` :8385, 9.81 m/s^2
at 2.3 mm a unit) and calm 0.6/0.8/1.0, a channel's current 180 units a second along its
long axis, swell 0/0.6/1.0, absorption 4000/1500/900 units, shore foam 0/0.7/0.85 in a
300-unit band with a ramp of gain 2, whitecaps 0.6 on a sea above half the wave height,
the foam pattern's grain 1/1.5/1.5, the highlight indoors 55 degrees up at azimuth 40
(exponent 90 for a basin, 70 for a channel, strength 0.8) and out of doors 22 degrees up
at azimuth 200 (exponent 90, strength 0.5). The palette (:8322), RGB shallow / deep /
highlight / foam: Rome 150,170,90 / 62,98,50 / 255,232,170 / 238,232,200; Russia
96,150,160 / 28,62,80 / 205,228,255 / 240,248,255; Ireland 100,125,98 / 34,60,44 /
235,240,230 / 248,248,242; VCI 64,92,150 / 14,28,70 / 190,210,255 / 215,225,245, all
times the body light: the squares' rooms' mean colour1 + colour2 over their light
samples, weighted by squares, times the gain 1.8, never under the floor 0.30 and never
over the cap 1.5 (`kWaterLightGain`, `kWaterLightFloor`, `kWaterLightCap` :8398 to :8400;
gain and floor chosen on the pictures, the cap a free choice, set by eye on the RoomProbe
pictures). The sky table (:8351) for the open-air bodies, one method for every row; the
override table (:8374), whose class may be `HD_WATER_NONE` (`hd_render.h` :761); the text
file (`ParseWaterLine` :8540, `read_water_file` :8622); the look per body (`water_look`
:8763) and the rows applied after the table (`apply_water_row` :8835). The grid: 5 x 5
vertices a square in its own MANAGED 16-bit buffers, colour1's red the depth over 32 and
green the distance to the nearest square without water within three squares over 16; one
range per body of a group. `upload_water_room` (:9546) writes c16 to c23 for every room
in `prepare()` (:8226): the caustic under a surface - only when the level was built with
the sheets (`g_caustic_on` :8455) - the eye in room coordinates out of a full inverse of
the room-to-view matrix, the swell and rows of the room's largest body or the basin's
rows and no swell. `draw_water_sheet` (:9594) draws a room's sheet in
`HDRenderRoomMask`'s blend phase after its glass, for the whole room's or the open half's
call only (:9728), premultiplied ONE / INVSRCALPHA, two-sided, no depth write.
`HDRenderWaterLogLine` (:9421) writes the `WATERLOG` text the engine and RoomProbe share;
`HDRenderWaterSheetAt` (:9358) answers BuildWaterSurfaces; the buffers are released with
every other buffer of the level (`release_buffers` :3414), so a lost device takes them
along. `specific/hd/hd_render.h`: `HDWaterRoom` (:785), `HDRenderSetWaterSheets` (:796),
`HDRenderWaterBody` (:814), `HDRenderWaterLevel` (:837). `hd_room.hlsl`: `Wave2` (:797),
`WaveSum` (:809), `CausticOf` (:837) - one minus half the absolute sum of two warped
waves to the sixth power, 0.0224 radians a unit, its mean 0.2310 and spread 0.2964
counted over 400,000 samples and divided out; the registers c16 to c23 (:384) and c92 to
c103 (:628); RoomVS's swell (:976) and wobble (:1021, 4/512 page a unit of slope); the
submerged weight (0.30, fading over 2048 units down); RoomPS's caustic footprint fade
(:1489, full to 10 units a pixel, gone at 20); `WaterVS` (:1597) and `WaterPS` (:1638),
whose distance fog (:1745) takes the same share of the water's colour as of the body's
light (`gWaterZen.w`, the mean of its three channels, 1 for a body that reflects the
sky), so the water goes black where its banks do. `hd_glow.hlsl` takes the same caustic
with the same footprint fade (:169). `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`: `BuildWaterSheets`
(:1639) fills the rooms, reads `hd_water.txt` (:1685) and writes the log (:1697), the
section from `gfLevelId` (`WaterSection` :1625), a `static_assert` on the room flags
(:1621); `BuildWaterSurfaces` leaves out a face whose square draws a sheet (:1857),
before the majority over the `.TRG`'s flat art, which then decides only the faces no
sheet covers, and ends its three log lines with `under a water sheet`; the call (:4921).
The option: `global/types.h` (:2896), `tomb5/tomb5.cpp` (:245, :465, :696),
`game/menu_frame.cpp` `MenuValHdWater` and `MenuStepHdWater` (:807) and the row (:1593),
`game/gameflow.cpp` (:1429, German `HD-Wasser`). `bshader.bat` compiles
`hd_room_water_vs.inc` and `hd_room_water_ps.inc`, `be.bat` checks their stamps before
and after a regeneration, and checks `hd_glow_ps.inc` against `hd_room.hlsl` as well (a
`// bshader-include` line). RoomProbe: `-hdwater 0|1` and `-waterfile` build through the
same `HDRenderSetWaterSheets` out of the classic file's squares (`Tr5Level::sectorInfo`),
with a room drawn HD by the engine's own test (`StandGroupHD`: triangles, not hollow,
with `-hdm` not marked), and print the same `WATERLOG` lines and the sheet draws' GPU
time.

The frame behind the sheet. `HDRenderWaterCopy` (`hd_render.cpp` :9631) copies render
target 0 by `StretchRect` into a `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` render-target texture of its size and
format, made on first use, once a bracket (`g_copy_valid`, cleared by `HDRenderFrameEnd`
through `water_bracket_end` :8517); `HDFrameDrawGlow` (`hd_level.cpp` :6551) calls it
after its `HDRenderFrameBegin` and before the first blend phase, when a room of the frame
has a sheet (`HDRenderGroupHasSheet` :9619) - so the copy holds every opaque thing of the
frame, the HD rooms and objects, the classic buckets and Lara, and none of the glass. The
back buffer is X8R8G8B8 and not multisampled, sRGB is off everywhere in the HD path, so
the copy is read as it is. `draw_water_sheet` (:9922) binds it to sampler s5 (linear,
clamped, one level) for the sheet draw alone and unbinds it after. `WaterPS` takes its
screen place from `VPOS` plus half a pixel (`hd_room.hlsl` :1752), so `WaterVS` keeps its
bytecode. The refraction (`RefractUV` :1700): the floor is read at a place moved by the
wave's slope times the absorption length times 1 - 1 / 1.33 times 1 - T - for a short
path the small-angle refraction of a ray through a tilted surface, for a long one no
further growth where the floor fades - 992 units for a basin, 372 for a channel, 223 for
a sea (`water_look`, :8922); the move is carried to the screen by solving the pixel's
footprint (`ddx`, `ddy` of the world position), which shrinks it with the distance and
turns it with the view, at most 256 units and 4 % of the screen, the place clamped
inside it. The absorption per channel (:8902): the channels in the ratio of ln(shallow /
deep) of the section's palette, their mean the class's 1 / absorb (Rome 1.31 / 0.82 /
0.87 of the mean, Russia 1.32 / 0.94 / 0.74, Ireland 1.24 / 0.84 / 0.92, VCI 1.31 / 1.03
/ 0.66). With the copy the sheet writes
F * reflection + (1 - F) * (copy * T_rgb + (1 - T) * scatter) + highlight,
foam over it, the fog on its own colour (the copy is fogged
already), with alpha 1 under the same ONE / INVSRCALPHA; without it the shader is the
stage before term for term. From below, inside the Snell window the copy is read with
the bend at the full slope in place of the 45 % of the frame that showed through
before; outside it as before. The depth texture: where `CheckDeviceFormat` offers `INTZ`
as a depth-stencil texture (`HDRenderWaterDepthOffered` :9719), `HDRenderWaterDepthBind`
(:9746) makes an `INTZ` texture of the depth buffer's size the device's depth-stencil,
keeps the device's own surface and clears the new one once (whole surface, scissor off);
`HDRenderWaterDepthUnbind` (:9812) puts the own surface back and releases both. The
engine binds it in `BuildWaterSheets` (`hd_level.cpp` :1701) when the level built sheets,
between frames, and logs a refusal; `release_water_sheets` (:8538) unbinds it and
releases the copy, so a new level, `HDRenderShutdown` and `HDLevelDeviceLost` before a
`Reset` or `DXClose` take both along, and the HD path makes them again with the next
level as it does its buffers. `depth_has_stencil` (:10457) counts `INTZ` (8 bits of
stencil) so the shadow receive keeps its stencil guard. The depth variant of `WaterPS`,
compiled with `HD_WATER_DEPTH` into `hd_room_water_depth_ps.inc` and picked while the
`INTZ` surface is bound, reads it on s6 (point, clamped, depth writes off, unbound after
the draw): `SceneZ` (:1722) undoes the projection, z = b / (a - d) with a and b of
`HDRenderMakeProjection`; `WaterDepthBelow` (:1739) gives the path through the water as
the view depth between the sheet and what was drawn behind it times the eye distance over
the sheet's view depth, and the depth straight down, for every term that needs it; the
bent place is refused and the pixel's own read where the frame there lies nearer than the
sheet (:1879). The fallback, `hd_room_water_ps.inc`, reads the vertex depth, does not
mask and keeps the sector band for the foam. New pixel constants c104 to c106
(`gWaterAbsorb`, `gWaterScreen`, `gWaterStage`), above every pixel register of the blend
phase's other shaders; samplers s5 and s6, free in every shader. `bshader.bat` compiles
and stamps the new variant, `be.bat` checks its stamp. `WATERLOG`'s level line ends with
`copy=` and `depth=`: what the sheets read, 1 where the level built sheets and the copy
is on and, for the depth, where the adapter offers `INTZ` and no bind refused. RoomProbe
binds the `INTZ` texture for every picture in `ShotBegin` unless `-nodepth`, with or
without `-hdwater`, takes the copy where `HDFrameDrawGlow` takes it (`RoomProbe.cpp`
:8946), prints the copy's GPU time, and has `-nocopy`, `-nodepth`, `-waterdepthview
1|2|3` (the scene's view depth as grey, the water depth out of it over the vertex depth,
the refused pixels in red) and `-waterbend <s>` (the refraction scaled for a proof
picture).

The life of the water. Every class has eight wave rows (`kWaterClass` :8333): the four
it had, which RoomVS still moves the Remaster's marked art with, and four more - three
at the geometric mean of two neighbours' wavelengths and one at the shortest over 1.5,
each as high as 0.8 of its neighbours' mean steepness times its wavelength, so heights
fall with the wave number, directions at least 0.15 radians from every other row's. A
sheet draw uploads all eight in a phase form (`water_rows_now` :8972): the phase is omega
t plus the row's own start, wrapped to one turn in double precision, and each height
carries a slow envelope, `1 - e + e (0.5 + 0.5 sin(2 pi t / P + i golden))`, with P 8 to
15 seconds and different for every row (`kWaterGroupPeriod` :8365) and e 0.30 for a
basin, 0.35 for a channel, 0.50 for a sea. `WaveSum8` (`hd_room.hlsl` :931) sums the
eight with the bend `WaveSum` gives its own position and Wave2's curve for sine and
cosine (eight `sincos` would cost about 64 pixel slots, the curve about 24); `WaterVS`
and both `WaterPS` variants read it, the footprint fade per row now for eight rows from
wave numbers the processor works out (`gWaveK`). The foam (`WaterPS` :2021) is a
density: at most 0.75, lacy at its outer edge and dense at the bank, lit as before; its
reach swings with a swash of 4.5 seconds whose phase runs along the bank and with the
wave's height there; its pattern drifts at two speeds and, through a third slow layer
whose threshold swings over 5 seconds with a phase of its own per region, grows and
dissolves; a smooth variety field of two Wave2 layers (periods about 6,700 and 8,900
units) moves it, turns it toward a second orientation and shifts its phase, so no two
stretches of bank look alike. In the depth variant the reach is the water's real depth
under the pixel, full at nothing and gone at one click (256 units), for water within
three squares of a classic bank; the fallback keeps the class's band. Whitecaps break
where the eight rows stand above the class's share of their whole height now and trail
where the two longest stood half a second earlier, weaker and broken up. The rings
(`hd_render.cpp`, "the rings"): once a frame, only when the level built sheets,
`FeedWaterRipples` (`hd_level.cpp` :1656) hands the live slots of the game's own
`ripples[]` with flags 0x10 or 0x02 and without 0x20 to `HDRenderWaterRipples` (:9729),
which starts a ring where a slot is new and ages it by what its `init` has counted
(`UpdateSplashes` adds 4 a tick, 8 with flags 2); the ring then lives two seconds on the
frame's clock, its front running out at 210 units a second from half the ripple's first
size, its strength a slope of 0.5 times that size over 128, falling with what is left
of its life. A sheet draw takes the eight youngest within 512 units of its squares and
256 of its surface (`gather_rings` :10243); `RingSlope` (`hd_room.hlsl` :1851) adds a
train of waves 56 units long behind each front to the slope, its amplitude divided by
the square root of 1 + d / 256 for the distance d from the centre - a loop over eight
registers, so the slots do not grow with the count. `S_DrawSplashes`
(`specific/specificfx.cpp` :4208) leaves a ripple's flat sprite out where
`HDWaterRippleOnSheet` (`hd_level.cpp` :1683) finds a drawing sheet under it with
`hd_water` and `hd_motion` on; raindrops (flags 0) and the underwater blood
keep their sprites, and with `hd_enable 0` the call is false at its first test. The
indoor stand-in reflects 0.65 of the body light at the horizon and 0.25 overhead and
swings +-40 % with a finer second pattern for 0.4 of it; under the sky it keeps the
measured sky rows and its +-25 %. `hd_water.txt` takes `ripple <x> <z> <size>
<seconds>` on any row (world units, size 1 to 255, seconds 0.1 to 60, `ParseWaterLine`
:8723): a ring source at that place every so many seconds, at the surface of the row's
room's square under it (`apply_water_row` :9121). ANDREA2 194's basin has one without a
file: the engine's own override row for room 194 carries `ripple 55808 32768 80 0.7`
with the sheets on, and a row of the file with a ripple for that room takes its place
(`kWaterOverride`, `hd_render.cpp` :9909).
RoomProbe `-ripple x,z,age[,size]`
(repeatable, world units, `RoomProbe.cpp` :6783) puts a ring of that age in every
picture. `WATERLOG`'s level line ends with `waverows=8 rings=8 sources=<n>`, the ripple
rows that found a body; the key is `waverows` and not `rows`, which the line already
carries for the file's rows.

`hd_water 0` builds no sheet, restores every classic face as without the sheets and
switches the caustic under a surface off; what stays with 0 is only the caustic's shape
and footprint fade on the Remaster's own marked water art and the wave rows on that art,
because they live in the compiled pixel and vertex shaders (the gloss RoomPS stands at 502
of the 512 slots). The bodies and their classes are built either way. With `hd_enable 0`
nothing of this runs.

`hd_water.txt`, read at every level load like `hd_gloss.txt`: one row a line, `<LEVEL>
<room> <class|-|none>` and any of `tint <r> <g> <b>`, `waves <s>`, `foam <s>`, each number
0 to 4; `-` keeps the class; `none` draws no sheet over the bodies the row reaches, which
keep their class, and the classic faces come back there; `#` starts a comment; an
unreadable line is counted. Rows apply after the compiled table's, to every body their
room has water in, so the file wins, and a later row wins over an earlier one. A default
file with the five pinned places was written but is not in this tree and does not ship
(see Left).

`WATERLOG level=<stem> option section sectors sheets built bodies basin channel sea file
rows bad applied unmatched overlaps caustic_rooms verts tris twins`, then per body
`WATERLOG body=<n> rooms surface sectors sheets shape open class rule depth light override
tint waves foam twins raw none`. One definition of the counts: `sectors` and `sheets`
count each place once, the level's and a body's alike, and the second room of a flipmap
pair at a place goes to `twins`; `raw` is the body light before gain, floor and cap;
`none` is 1 when a row of class `none` took the body's sheet away.

**Measured.** The sweep, RoomProbe `-hdwater 1 -nodraw` over the fifteen levels,
places / drawing a sheet / bodies (basin, channel, sea), and the squares of a flipmap
twin where there are any: ANDREA1 34 / 34 / 4 (4, 0, 0); ANDREA2 94 / 94 / 7 (6, 1,
0); ANDY1 30 / 30 / 4 (1, 0, 3); ANDY2 72 / 72 / 18 (15, 3, 0), 20 twins; ANDY3 125 /
125 / 26 (5, 0, 21), 87 twins; JOBY2 69 / 69 / 3 (1, 0, 2), 15 twins; JOBY4 2 / 2 / 1
(1, 0, 0); JOBY5 142 / 142 / 14 (11, 3, 0); RICH2 9 / 9 / 4 (4, 0, 0); ANDREA3, JOBY3,
RICH1, RICH3, RICHCUT2 and TITLE no water square by this rule (the water planes of
ANDREA3, JOBY3 and RICH3 have no underwater room below and keep their faces, see
Left). 577 places, every one drawing a sheet, and 122 squares of a twin, 699 squares
in all; 81 bodies (48 basins, 7 channels, 26 seas); no square held by two rooms that
are no flipmap pair. 107 of the squares lie under the Remaster's flat art and drew no
sheet before the review's rule; they draw one now. ANDREA2 and JOBY2 give the bodies
the design counted (ANDREA2 94 squares in 7 bodies; JOBY2 69 places in 3, 84 squares
with the 15 of room 45, the twin of 143). ANDREA2 room 76 has its surface: body 1, 4
squares, a basin. The body light before gain, floor and cap (`raw=`) runs 0.09 to 0.55
a channel over the bodies of ANDREA2 and JOBY2 (lowest ANDREA2's room 196, highest
JOBY2's 143 with its twin 45) and 0.07 to 1.88 over all levels (ANDY1 room 144; JOBY4
room 7, the one body at the cap); the design gave 0.09 for ANDREA2 231 alone, a single
room's mean - that room's body, 144, 229 and 231, runs from 0.17 to 0.20. The sky, one
method for every row (`RoomProbe -sky -skyonly -black` at 960 x 540 from 1024 0 1024
in JOBY2's room 42, ANDY1's 132 and ANDY3's 17; the mean of the rows 6 to 40 pixels
above the picture's middle toward four directions, and straight up where the dome
covers the view): JOBY2 horizon 152, 154, 171 and overhead 96, 93, 116, in the table
now in place of the 163, 165, 178 and 100, 104, 122 the design row had, which no row
band of the round's pictures repeats; ANDY1 and ANDY3 share one dusk dome, 113, 78, 67
and 11, 19, 32 where its clouds cover 41 % of the view. No class of the sweep was
pinned: no indoor pool came out a sea, no sea a basin; the rule's classes stand. The
slots of fxc 10.0.26100 /O3, 8691e82 to now: RoomPS 476 to 477 (the caustic's new
shape saves 12, the footprint fade costs 13), gloss RoomPS 503 to 502, RoomVS 348 to
412, GlowPS 479 to 478 (465 with the new shape, 13 more for the footprint fade),
WaterPS 247 (243 before its fog took the body light), WaterVS 153. GPU time of the
sheet draws by timestamp queries: 0.027 to 0.041 ms in the thirteen 960 x 540 views
that draw a sheet, 0.091 ms for a screen full of water at 2560 x 1440 (JOBY2 room 42
from above, two draws).

The frame behind the sheet, measured on this machine (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, driver
32.0.15.9636): `CheckDeviceFormat` offers `INTZ` as a depth-stencil texture, and the
texture reads back as the depth - `-waterdepthview 2` gives 124 to 171 of 255 (a depth
ratio of 0.97 to 1.34) over the flat floor of ANDREA2's fountain seen from above, where
the floor data and the scene agree, and it shows the deep shaft under ANDREA2 room 76
and the pit under fountain 194 that the floor data does not know. The slots of fxc
10.0.26100 /O3: `WaterPS` 247 to 307 in the fallback (the copy's read and the
composition 19, the per-channel absorption 5, the refraction 36) and 354 in the depth
variant (the depth path 10, the mask 10, RoomProbe's depth views 27); `WaterVS` 153,
RoomPS 477, gloss RoomPS 502, GlowPS 478 and RoomVS 412 the same bytecode as before.
GPU time by timestamp queries, the full-water view at 2560 x 1440, three runs each: the
copy 0.017 ms; the sheet draws 0.113 to 0.116 ms with the depth texture, 0.106 to 0.107
with the fallback, 0.090 to 0.093 without the copy (0.091 before). At 960 x 540 the copy
takes 0.006 to 0.007 ms and the sheet draws 0.038 to 0.057 ms in the thirteen views that
draw one. The depth texture's mask refuses 332 to 550 pixels of a 960 x 540 view above
the water (A1, A2, B1, C1) and 1,972 from below (D1), along the near banks, the rod
across ANDREA2's fountain and the ice floes' edges (`-waterdepthview 3`); with the
refraction six times as strong, 1,794 to 2,619 and 5,994.

The life of the water, measured with RoomProbe built after its last engine commit. The
slots of fxc 10.0.26100 /O3: `WaterPS` 307 to 436 in the fallback and 354 to 487 in the
depth variant, `WaterVS` 153 to 150; taking one feature out of the final shader at a
time, the rings cost 51 and 52 (eight of them, a loop), the four added rows 42 and 42,
the new foam 75 and 78 against the foam before it (of that the earlier crest 19 and
20), the stand-in's finer pattern 3 and 4; Wave2's curve in place of `sincos` and the
wave numbers worked out on the processor give back about 42. RoomVS 412, RoomPS 477,
gloss RoomPS 502 and GlowPS 478 keep their bytecode. GPU time by timestamp queries,
the full-water view at 2560 x 1440, three runs each: the sheet draws 0.188 to 0.192 ms
with the depth texture (0.113 to 0.117 before), 0.182 to 0.183 with the fallback, and
from 0.188 to 0.191 with eight rings injected; the copy 0.017 ms as before; at 960 x
540 from 0.035 to 0.060 ms in the thirteen views that draw a sheet. The ripple scan on the
processor, by count rather than by clock: 128 slots read a frame, a ring started per
new slot, at most 64 rings kept, and per sheet draw a pass over those rings and the
file's sources and a sort of at most 96 - a few thousand operations a frame. The
pictures for the strips: four views at eight clock times over four seconds (3 to 6.5),
and the sea of JOBY2 42 and the sewer of ANDREA2 19 at 0, 10, ... 60 seconds before
and after.

**Checked.** The engine builds (`be.bat`), and RoomProbe, TrgProbe, ModelProbe, MapProbe,
ModernTest, MenuTest, InterpTest and LipsTest; ModernTest 14,721, MenuTest 42,627 (42,613,
13 in the new `graphics_water_row` and one more in `graphics_softbody_row`, which now
holds fourteen rows - counted on the code, MenuTest prints no count per family),
InterpTest 729, LipsTest 270 and 243, none failed. `be.bat` with a wrong `bshader-include`
line in `hd_glow_ps.inc` regenerates the shaders. The classic faces: RoomProbe
`-classicroom -classiconly` of ANDREA2 19 and 231, JOBY2 42 and 66, ANDY3 17 and 34, built
at 8691e82 and now, are the same bytes (md5). The fifteen views at 960 x 540 (the nine of
the design, the view from under the fountain, the view from above it, ANDREA2 76, JOBY2
66, RICH2's mirror washroom 134 and JOBY5 102's marked Remaster water): with `-hdwater 0`
and without the switch 14 of 15 are the same bytes as at 8691e82, the fifteenth the marked
water with the new wave rows and caustic shape (11.3 % of its pixels); with `-hdwater 1`
the sheets show. The distance fog: the sea of JOBY2 room 42 and the sewer of ANDREA2 room
19 under RoomProbe `-fog 12288` and `-fog 4096` - the water now darkens with its banks,
where it went black ahead of them. The full-water view's straight seam at x 3072 lies in
the floor: 9.9 of 255 across it with `-hdwater 0`, 1.6 through the sheet. The mirrors:
TR5's mirrors are art and a second draw of Lara and the items, never a second draw of a
room through the blend phase, and no mirror room holds a water square, so no sheet is ever
drawn mirrored; the eye is still an inverse in full, right for a reflected matrix too. The
pass order: the engine's HDFrameDrawGlow and RoomProbe both draw every room's blend phase
(its glass, then its sheet), then the stand-ins and statics, then the additive pass. Seen
from below, the sheet is drawn with its dry room's constants, where the underwater flicker
of `gWaterMode.x` is 0 - the classic face it replaces never took it either; the camera's
underwater wobble and the fog reach it as they reach a room. `hd_water.txt` read in
RoomProbe with the five pinned rows, three good test rows, three unreadable lines, one row
for a room without water and two rows of class `none`: ANDREA2 `rows=10 bad=3 applied=9
unmatched=1`, its fountain 194 `sheets=0 none=1` and the level's sheets 94 to 88; ANDY2 57
`none` reaches the five bodies of rooms 57 and 136, the level's sheets 72 to 52; the
bodies name `override=file:<room>` with their numbers. The motion over six clock times in
two views.

The frame behind the sheet, with RoomProbe built after the last engine commit: the
engine and the tools build, the suites count as before and none failed; the
classic faces of the six rooms above with the `INTZ` texture as the depth buffer are the
same bytes as at 8691e82 (6 of 6); the fifteen views with `-hdwater 0` and the `INTZ`
texture bound are the same bytes as the fix round's parity pictures (15 of 15), so both
paths draw into it unchanged; with `-nocopy -nodepth` the fifteen are the same bytes as
the fix round's `-hdwater 1` pictures (15 of 15), the stage before term for term; the
sweep's counts are unchanged; RoomVS, RoomPS, the gloss RoomPS, GlowPS, WaterVS and the
shadow and model shaders compile to the same bytecode, their `.inc` differing in the
stamp lines alone. The state bracket passes with the copy and the depth texture
(83 watched states). The lost device, by reading: `HDLevelDeviceLost` calls
`HDRenderShutdown` whenever the INTZ texture can be bound (it is bound only after the
sheets were built, which needs the HD shaders), `release_buffers` runs before `g_device`
is dropped, and `release_water_sheets` puts the device's own depth-stencil back before
it releases the `INTZ` texture and the reference on the own surface, so `Reset` finds no
`D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` object of the water alive; after the `Reset` the device holds its
automatic depth-stencil again and the next level binds the texture anew.

The life of the water, with the tools built after its last engine commit: the engine
and the tools build, the suites count as before (nothing was added to them) and none
failed; the classic faces of the six rooms are the same bytes as at 8691e82 (6 of 6);
the fifteen views with `-hdwater 0` are the same bytes as the pictures of the frame
behind the sheet and of the fix round (15 of 15), so nothing of the life runs without
sheets; the shared shaders' `.inc` differ in the stamp lines alone (12 of 12); the
sweep's counts are unchanged. ANDREA2's fountain 194 has no ripple of the game's own -
no item stands in room 194 or in the water room 120 below it (ItemCheck on the classic
level), and no caller of `SetupRipple` is an object's control - so a ripple row is what
gives it rings: `ANDREA2 194 - ripple 55808 32768 80 0.7` in a test file read by
RoomProbe gives `rows=1 bad=0 applied=4 sources=1`, the body of room 194 names
`override=file:194`, and the fountain's picture changes in the pool alone; a file of
four unreadable ripple rows (size 0, 100 seconds, three numbers, a word) and one full
row of sixteen words counts `bad=4` and `sources=1`. Rings injected with `-ripple` show
on ANDREA2's fountain at 0.3 and 1.0 seconds and are gone at 2.0, and show on JOBY2's
sea. The motion strips show the foam moving up and down the bank, blotches coming and
going and the waves' pattern changing over a minute, where the foam before it showed the
same blotches at the same places at every clock time.

**Left.** The in-game look, the palette under the game's gamma and fog, the mirror rooms
and the camera under water in the game, all unseen: nobody could play in this round. The
shore foam's softer edge (a ramp of gain 2 where the build had 3) is to be judged in the
game against the 3 it replaces, a one-number change in `WaterPS`. A channel's current runs
along its body's longer box axis, one direction for a turning canal. What the sweep found
odd: ANDY3's rooms 34 and 183 (a flipmap pair) hold water squares at three heights, 10496,
10752 and 11008, where their classic faces stand at 11008 alone - sixteen small bodies,
three of them of depth 0 (bodies 6, 9, 12); ANDY2's rooms 158 and 159 hold eight single
squares at 14592 that get a sheet where nothing showed water. Rooms where the Remaster's
flat art that is not its water lies over a sheet now, to be tuned in the game (the class
`none` takes a body's sheet away): ANDY2 57 and 136 (four single squares at 20992), ANDY2
158 and 159 (a 20-square channel and a single square each, at 15616); ANDY3's twin rooms
0, 42, 43 and 182, 17, 101, 206 and 207, 34, 38, 183 and 184, and 38, 41, 184 and 185
(squares of the second room of a pair); JOBY5 4, 61, 139 and 184. Planes where the
Remaster's material 16 water and a sheet both draw: ANDREA2 231 (additive, 2048 triangles,
7 to 9 units above the sheet), ANDY2 52 (additive, 128), ANDY2 57 (OPAQUE, 2256 triangles
at 22009, 7 units above the sheet at 22016, which it hides and may fight with in depth at
a distance), JOBY5 4, 27, 28, 49 (two parts), 53, 61, 83, 115, 117 (two parts), 139, 143,
151 and 184 (all additive). Classic water planes with no underwater room below, which keep
their restored faces and get no sheet: ANDREA2 70, 204, 237; ANDREA3 70, 120; ANDY1 26;
ANDY3 28, 87, 104, 107, 210; JOBY3 21, 26, 135, 144, 164, 180, 184, 191, 192; JOBY5 2, 14,
26, 50, 52, 102, 114, 119, 161, 178, 182; RICH3 87, 143, 191, 192. JOBY4's one basin (room
7) is lit at the cap of 1.5. The basin's ripples read as regular rings from straight
above; the sheet writes no depth, so models drawn after it are not tinted; a bracket that
takes no copy dims the floor by one alpha and cannot colour it. Whether `hd_water.txt`
ships with the release, as `hd_gloss.txt` does not, is open. Of the frame behind the
sheet: the look of the refraction, the tint and the depth texture in the game, unseen;
a room's glass is drawn after the copy and is not seen through a sheet; the
Remaster's art over a sheet and the ANDY3 planes at three heights stay as listed
above; where the depth texture finds a deep shaft or a pit the floor data does not
know (ANDREA2 76, fountain 194), the water now goes dark there, which is to be judged in
the game; an adapter without `INTZ` draws the fallback, which this machine shows only
through `-nodepth`. Of the life of the water: the waves, the foam and the rings in
motion in the game, unseen - the rings of the game's ripples in particular are proved
only through `-ripple`, since only the game makes ripples; in the depth variant the
foam rises wherever something stands within a click under the surface near a bank,
a wading or swimming Lara included; a sheet draw shows at most its eight youngest rings,
and where more ripples lie under one sheet the classic sprites of the rest stay out as
well; a raindrop's ripple keeps its sprite and gets no ring; the waves, the foam and the
rings step with the game's thirty-hertz clock, as every motion of the HD path does; the
fountain's ripple row lives in a test file and is not in this tree, like the rest of
`hd_water.txt`.

**After the owner's second play test of 2026-10-08.** The build of `77d333c` was played
through ANDREA1, ANDREA2, ANDY1, ANDY3, RICH2, JOBY2 and JOBY5 (reference pictures and two
logs supplied for this project, not in the repository): waves running over solid floor,
white blotches on a swimming Lara, a rat and the pier posts, foam with a zigzag edge, the
Remaster's water and the sheet side by side in one basin, Lara's legs tinted under the
surface, every motion stepping at sixty frames a second, and a crash on Alt+Enter. The
surface seen from above in ANDREA1 and ANDREA2 was judged good and is kept.

The crash seam. `specific/crashseam.h` (header only, `CrashSeamFilter` :73), installed in
`WinMain` (`specific/winmain.cpp` :910), which names the game thread where it starts
(:1024): an exception nobody catches writes `CRASH code=<hex> at=<address>
module=<file>+<offset> thread=main|game|other` through `Log` with `-log` and into
`crash.txt` without it, and a minidump `PCtomb5_<date>_<time>.dmp` beside it
(MiniDumpNormal, through `dbghelp.dll` loaded at that moment; without it the line still
goes out). RoomProbe `-crash` proves both.

Alt+Enter. The log of the crash ends after `HDLOG shadow mode ... reason=hd_off`, in the
first frame on the new device. Read from `WinProcessCommands` through
`DXToggleFullScreen`, `DXCreate`, `DXClose` and `HDLevelDeviceLost`: everything of the
water - the copy, the `INTZ` texture, the device's own depth surface held while it stood
in, the sheet buffers and every table - is released in `release_water_sheets` before the
device goes, and nothing of the water runs again before the next level
(`HDRenderWaterSheetsBuilt`, `HDLevelActive` and the renderer's device are all false
then). RoomProbe `-devicecycle` repeats the path: with the sheets built and `INTZ` bound
the device is released with no reference of ours left on it (`RefCnt = 0`), and the HD
picture drawn again on a third device is byte for byte the first. The 87 references the
log prints at the release are the classic path's own - the level's texture pages and the
other MANAGED textures, made on the old device at level load and not made again on the new
one. Drawing with a MANAGED texture of one device on a second one, the first's own
reference released, runs without a fault on this machine, so that is not shown to be the
crash, and the classic path is not changed: the crash seam names the faulting module and
offset the next time.

The clock. `FillFrameLighting` (`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp` :4008) and the two brackets
(:5523, :5736) hand the frame the drawn state's time, `HDBookClock` - the tick clock less
the part of a tick the blended pose stands behind it, which the material 15 books already
turned on - in place of the tick clock. The water's waves, foam and rings, the wind, the
caustic, the scroll and the flipbooks move on every frame drawn instead of in thirty steps
a second; an improvement of the sixty frames path, not a change of the look. At
`fps_mode 0` the time is the tick clock, and RoomProbe's `-time` is untouched, so every
proof picture stays what it was. A clock of the tick count plus the blend factor was not
taken: it runs a tick ahead of the pose the frame draws.

The clip. `WaterVS` hands the swell's lift on in `TEXCOORD2.y` (`hd_room.hlsl` :1734); the
depth variant measures the frame's depth under the surface at rest (`rest`, :1999) and,
seen from above, `clip()`s where it is under 8 units (:2020), so a deck, a rim or a bank
at the water's height shows itself. 8 against the depth's own error - `rest` is one value
to a sixteenth of a unit over JOBY2 66's flat pool floor at 2560 x 1440, about 2,600 units
away, and 24 bits over the near and far planes of 20 and 20,480 give about 1.2 units at
the far plane - and wide enough for the Remaster's planes, which stand 2 to 9 units off
the classic height. `clip()` and not alpha 0: with the copy the sheet writes the whole
pixel. The fallback cannot know such a floor and keeps the data rule; there a row of class
`none` stays the way.

The refraction guard. `RefractMove` (:1807) returns the move; the bent place's depth
(:2142, the tap the mask read already) refuses it where the frame there lies within 48
units of the surface at rest or above it, and scales the move to the shorter of the two
paths, here and there: `1 - T` of the shorter over `1 - T` of this pixel's own. 48 is a
free choice, set by eye on RoomProbe pictures of JOBY2's pier posts and the floe;
`-waterdepthview 3` shows the refused pixels.

The waterline and the comb. The broad foam is the sector band in both variants; the depth
variant adds a waterline, full under 24 units and gone at 48, broken by the foam pattern
(:2096), so a swimming Lara, a rat or a post gets at most a wet line, and the hull and the
floes keep theirs. The zigzag was neither the shore field (already the distance to the
nearest dry square's box at every vertex) nor the depth foam: it shows in both variants.
The pattern was blended toward a copy of itself turned by 57 degrees, and a blend between
two orientations of world coordinates some 50,000 units from the origin multiplies the
pattern's rate of change by that distance where the blend is half done: drawn alone as
grey in RoomProbe it was a moire of stripes a few units apart, the comb along the banks.
The pattern is now moved by the variety field and not turned (:2076).

The purple. Not changed. The composition cannot make it: what comes through is
`exp(-path sigma)`, at most 1 in every channel, red absorbed at least as much as green in
all four palettes, and the water's shallow and deep colours hold green over red in every
row; `gWaterAbsorb` is written and read in the order red, green, blue. A lilac lighter
than her suit is therefore in the frame the copy holds. A node of Lara under water is lit
with the underwater room's ambient (`hd_laradraw.cpp`, the classic rule of
`InitObjectLighting`), the same light that colours the floors of the underwater rooms
purple and blue (JOBY2 76 in RoomProbe with `-hdwater 0`); the veil of stage 1 hid it,
and the short path of a leg under the surface shows it now. In the play test's picture
the lilac lies beside her legs rather than on them, which this reading does not explain;
RoomProbe draws no Lara, and the classic light rule stays as it is.

The Remaster's water art over a sheet. A draw call that is wholly the Remaster's own water
art - horizontal triangles of material 16 or water-marked at every corner
(`HDRange::artTris` :1340, counted in the triangle walk :6237) - within 32 units of a
sheet's surface over a square whose sheet draws is hidden (step 8 of
`HDRenderSetWaterSheets` :9796; the draws skip it at :7903 and :10949). The sort key and
the draw calls stay as they are; with `hd_water 0` nothing is hidden, and the classic
faces' rule is unchanged. `hd_water.txt` takes `art keep` and `art hide`, the default, per
row (:8874), and a row may hold 18 tokens. This reverses the decision of 2026-10-07 that
ANDREA2 231's art stays over the sheet, on the play test's picture of the fountain hall,
half under that art and half the sheet; `ANDREA2 231 - art keep` puts it back. The
WATERLOG level line ends with `art_hidden=<triangles> clip=<1 for the depth variant>`, the
body line with `art=keep|hide`.

**Measured.** Slots, fxc /O3: WaterPS 436 to 425 (the turn taken out), its depth variant
487 to 499 (the clip 4, the waterline 6, the guard 19, the four depth views now one block
of 16), WaterVS 150 to 152; all under the 512 of one draw. The full-water timing view at
2560 x 1440, three runs each: 0.193 to 0.194 ms against 0.183 to 0.185 at `77d333c`.
`art_hidden` over the fifteen levels: ANDREA2 2048, ANDY2 2384, JOBY5 15906, none
elsewhere; the sweep's counts are unchanged. RoomProbe `-crash`: the line with its module
and offset, and a dump of about 30 KB beginning with `MDMP`.

**Checked.** The classic path (`-classicroom` and `-classiconly` on ANDREA2 19 and 231,

**The look, after the same play test.** The play test also asked for the water's look: the
foam flat and unnatural, a texture where the waves have a body; the rings restless,
repeating quickly, fading too soon; the water at eye level completely flat; the surface
from below and the light on the walls under it less good than from above. The view from
above in ANDREA1 and ANDREA2 was judged good, and every change here leaves it as it was or
nearly so (the fountain hall seen from above, `D2`, changes by 0.68 of 255 on average,
from the walls' caustic and the rows' fade).

The rings (`hd_render.cpp` :8676, :9985; `hd_room.hlsl` :1979). A wading Lara sets up a
ripple every four ticks (`game/effects.cpp`, `WadeSplash`), and each became a ring: a
quick train of rings, all alike. Now one body makes one ring: a new ripple of the same
kind - a body's (flags 0x10) or a small one's (a bubble, a rat, a shell) - within 192
units of a live ring goes into it, taken as its own while that ring is younger than 0.6 s
and starting it again from the new ripple when it is older. The ring is two long, low
swells of 90 units behind its front instead of three of 56, runs at 150 units a second
instead of 210, and lives 3.5 s instead of 2 with its strength, still 0.5, times the
square of the life left: as strong at one second as the straight two-second fade made it
(0.255 against 0.25), still there in the third second, gone at three and a half. A
strength of 0.35, tried first, made every ring fainter at every age - calmer, but not
slower to fade - and was set back to 0.5 (`4fce14b`). All free choices, set by eye on the
play test's words. The rain's white rings are the game's own ripple pictures (flags 0,
kept as they are, entry 71 of the ledger); if those are the restless rings of the play
test, this does not touch them.

The foam's body (`hd_room.hlsl` :2264, `hd_render.cpp` :8543). The foam is lit as a layer
with thickness: its cover times the pattern is a height of up to 24 units, its rise toward
the class's light - the screen gradient against the screen step of one unit toward the
light, the footprint solved as the refraction solves it - lights it with a soft diffuse
term to first order, over what a flat layer gets, never under 0.3; thin foam is shaded to
0.65 and a blotch has a darker rim where its cover is half. The relief was tried at 8
(hardly shows), 24 and 48 (the edges turn to grain). On a sea `WaterVS` lifts a breaking
crest by up to a quarter of the whole wave height (:1796), so the whitecaps ride the
crests. The translucency stays: the foam's cover never passes 0.75.

The body at eye level (`hd_room.hlsl` :2059, :1839). Two causes. The rows' fade measured
the pixel's longest step: seen flat a pixel spans far more water in depth than across, and
the rows faded out - at 3,000 units and 5 degrees over the surface a pixel 0.0015 radians
tall spans about 52 units in depth (3,000 x 0.0015 / sin 5 degrees), so the basin's rows
of 29 to 197 units were gone and the longest, 260, kept a third: the water at eye level
was drawn nearly without waves. The fade is now measured along each row's own direction,
the phase step to the next pixel right and down, worked out per vertex from the
projection's derivative (`gWaterView`, c19) and carried to the pixel shader, so the rows
whose crests run toward the eye stay. And the slopes are raised by the class's gain -
basin 3, channel 2, sea 1, the factors asked for - where the view runs within about 9
degrees of the surface, not at all where it looks down by 37 degrees or more, linearly
between. Not taken: raising the heights themselves - a higher wave is higher from above
too, and the view from above is the one the play test kept - and a swell for a basin: the
sheet has a vertex every 256 units, a row shorter than 512 cannot be carried by the
geometry (every basin row is 29 to 260 units long, so it would alias into a slow crawl of
the whole sheet), and 0.6 of the tripled heights is at most 13.6 units with all eight rows
in step and about 4 as their root mean square - about one pixel at 960 x 540 from A1, some
3,000 units away (80 degrees over 960 pixels).

The view from below (:2163). Outside the Snell window the deep colour covers three
quarters (0.92 before) and the frame behind shows through the rest; the window's edge
spans 0.61 to 0.71 of N.V round the critical angle's 0.66; inside it the bent frame with a
fifth of the reflection colour (0.55 before). Free choices, set by eye on RoomProbe
pictures.

The caustic on the walls (`hd_room.hlsl` :999, :1669, `hd_glow.hlsl` :177). `CausticOf` is
a pattern of the horizontal plane; a wall read it along one axis and got vertical streaks.
`CausticFace` reads it in the plane of the face normal's major axis - x and z on a floor,
z and y or x and y on a wall, the normal from the screen derivatives of the position - one
sample, the planes never blended (a second sample costs about 20 of the 512 slots), the
footprint by the pixel's step in all three axes, which on a floor is the step it always
was. In `RoomPS`'s plain variant and `GlowPS`; the gloss variant, at 502 slots, keeps the
horizontal plane on the polished floors it draws.

The bend key (`hd_render.cpp` :8938, :9279). `hd_water.txt` takes `bend <s>` per row, 0 to
4, the refraction's strength times s; a row may hold 20 tokens; WATERLOG's body line ends
with `bend=`. The default stays 1; a default of 1.5 was asked for and not taken: the
refraction is what the view from above shows, and that view was kept. RoomProbe pictures
of the fountain hall at 1, 1.5 and 2 lie beside this round's proofs.

The depth views of RoomProbe move into a variant of their own (`HD_WATER_VIEW`,

`bshader.bat` and checked by `be.bat`: the game never draws a view, and the 16 slots of
the views pay for the foam's body in the variant it draws.

**After the owner's third play test of 2026-10-08.** The build of `4fce14b` was played
(reference pictures, a video's frames and a sketch supplied for this project, not in the
repository). Kept as they are: the rain's white double rings (the game's own sprites), the
lilac on Lara's legs (the room below's light, accepted), the gain at eye level, the
sheet's look in the fountain hall. Asked for: the bank foam is far too regular, the edge
of a tablecloth - it is to be broken up by other shapes and be gone in places, there or
not at random, in different shapes, never the same; the waterline foam on Lara's body is
to go (the posts' line is fine); the rats are still slightly torn; the surface seen from
below is in places opaque, a milky green, and is to become clear; the waterfall of the
fountain hall stops above the surface, and where it lands a swirl and a splash of drops
are wanted.

The patches (`hd_room.hlsl` :1819, :1855, :2300; `hd_render.cpp` :8548, :9262). The band
of the bank foam reached the same width along every bank, and only the pattern inside it
varied. Now a slow field decides where along a bank foam is at all. `WaterVS` works it out
per vertex - a field of thousands of units needs no more than a vertex every 256 - from
three layers of cells, each the product of two Wave2 along axes turned by 0.35, 1.25 and
2.20 radians (none lines up with the classic grid's banks), periods 3,800, 5,400 and 7,400
units, each times a clock of its own, 26.3, 33.7 and 45.9 seconds, whose phase turns once,
twice and three times over the variety field and a quarter turn with the next layer's
cell. A cell grows in place while its clock swings up, stands and dissolves, and the cells
of the other sign take over elsewhere. `WaterPS` takes a patch where the field stands over
0.05 and lets the band reach 1.5 times the square root of the excess over 0.4: nothing at
a patch's ends, rising like a half circle where the field crosses the threshold, so a
patch is a rounded lobe, and the further the field stands over it, the further the lobe
reaches. Inside a patch the pattern, the swash, the dissolve and the foam's body are as
they were. In a channel the field is read at the place less the drift, 0.3 of the class's
current along the channel's axis times the clock (c19 zw): the water by a bank runs slower
than in the middle. The variety field moves from `WaterPS` to `WaterVS` with it, which
pays for the patches in the pixel shader. All free choices, set by eye against the sketch,
which shows foam on parts of a pool's sides in lobes of different sizes, bare edge
between; RoomProbe's `-waterdepthview 5` draws the patches' strength in green.

Decided against the brief: lobes of about a third of a square to two squares, not one to
four. The sketch's lobes are 0.1 to 0.37 of a side (measured on it, sides of about 450
pixels), and ANDY1's two pools, 14 squares each, are 3 to 5 squares a side, so the sketch
reads as 0.3 to 1.85 squares there; lobes of one to four squares would make a whole side
of those pools one patch or none.

The faint line. Where no patch is, the bank is not left bare: with the depth texture the
waterline is held to 0.25 within the band of a bank and outside a patch, 0.75 inside a
patch and out in the water (the posts, the floes, the hull), and without it the band's
innermost 24 units carry a line of 0.25, broken by the pattern. The sea's whitecaps are
unchanged; a basin has no bank foam.

Lara (`hd_room.hlsl` :2311; `hd_render.cpp` :8554, :10042, :10710; `hd_level.cpp` :1689,
:6637). The waterline gives way round her: no line within 320 units of her place, back in
full 64 further out, while she swims at the surface or wades (`lara.water_status`), set
once a frame from `lara_item` into c123 (`gWaterLara`); the posts, the hull and the floes
keep theirs, and her rings stay. She stands 768 units tall and lies about 700 long when
she swims; 320 and 64 are free choices that cover her. RoomProbe `-lara x,z` places her

The rat (`hd_room.hlsl` :1999). A swimming rat stands at the underwater room's ceiling
plus 50 (`game/rat.cpp` :222, y down) and its mesh reaches 10 below its place

lowest 12 units read the rat - a piece of it drawn beside itself. The guard now refuses
within 96 units. Shown on the guard's own arithmetic, a cut through a rounded body 60

phases and the rat's rings at five ages: water pixels that show the rat 106 with 48, 0

From below (`hd_room.hlsl` :2242). Outside the Snell window the sheet shows the bent frame
under 0.35 of the shallow colour (it was 0.75 of the deep colour times 1.3), inside the
window 0.1 of the reflection colour (0.2); the window's edge stays 0.61 to 0.71 of N.V,

The waterfall's foot (`hd_render.cpp` :8811, :10348, :11215; `hd_level.cpp` :1712, :1792;
`hd_room.hlsl` :2445; `game/control.cpp` :714; `RoomProbe.cpp` :4759). In the fountain
hall of ANDREA2 the falling water stops above the surface, and the owner asked for the
white swirl where it lands - the swirl of room 231's own water art, hidden under the sheet
since the second play test, which he liked but which lay out of place on the moving
sheet - and for a splash of drops like the one of ANDREA1's fountain. Measured first, with
the classic data and the tools: nothing draws the waterfall object there. ANDREA2's `.MAP`
binds the slot WATERFALL1 to DUMMY (`MapProbe -map ANDREA2 -v` lists every slot but Lara's
and the DUMMY ones, and lists no line for it), so in a room drawn HD the object is drawn
by nobody (the baked rule of `hd_object.cpp`) and the room's art draws the curtain: two
flow parts (material 1) from y -3,356 down to 249 and 255, and at their foot a spray part
from 47 to 281 (`TrgProbe -parts 231`). Neither the art nor the classic object stops short
of the water - the classic mesh ends at 256 and so does the surface. What stops short is
the curtain's light: on the additive pass alone, seen level from 100 units over the
surface, it falls to half its peak about 290 units over the water and to a tenth 62 units
over it, and is nothing over the last 25 or so; the spray at the foot adds nothing to that
picture, and the art's swirls were hidden. So the foot is what is built.

The rule. Every WATERFALL1 to 3 and WATERFALLSS1 and 2 object - the slots the game scrolls
as falling water; FISHTANK is a tank's glass - has its classic mesh placed as
`DrawAnimatingItem` places it, and its foot is the vertices within 64 units of the lowest;
an object no taller than that is a scrolling face (ANDREA1's WATERFALLSS1, the upper basin
of its fountain). The foot stands over a sheet where one of its points lies over a square
that draws one, with the surface at most 256 units over the lowest vertex or 1,024 under
it. Where the room is drawn HD and its art has falling water there - a flow part more than
512 units tall whose lowest vertices lie within a square of the classic foot and over the
same sheet - those take the classic foot's place: in room 231 the art's curtains land
about 450 units nearer the room's middle than the classic mesh (x 55,518 to 55,585 against
55,967 to 56,028, the WATERLOG `foot=` lines with and without the art), and two waterfalls
over one sheet stand two squares apart at the least (JOBY2's room 66). The foot's points,
in order along their own principal axis, are cut into runs no longer than 1,024 units and
at every gap over 384; each run is a source at its mean with half its diagonal plus 256 as
its radius, held to 384 to 768. Free choices, set by eye on the round's RoomProbe
pictures: a disc about a square across under every square of a curtain, three quarters of
a square under a narrow jet. ANDREA2's curtain gets four sources, two under each of its
two strands.

A source is three things. The swirl: a second draw of the sheet's triangles with a pixel
shader of its own, `SwirlPS` (the sheet's depth variant stands at 508 of 512 slots and
holds no loop of four Wave2 a source), up to eight sources a draw in c124 to c131, with
the sheet's blend: per source the pixel's place turned about the centre by 0.35 radians a
second and by 1.2 more toward the middle (the spiral turns as a whole and never winds up),
the bank foam's own two drifting layers, slow layer and five-second dissolve read there,
the reach the radius times 0.8 + 0.2 of the patch field (it breathes with the patches'
clocks of 26 to 46 seconds), the bank foam's density with the middle in the bank's place
along the square root of the way in (a dense core over about half the disc, lace round
it), the foam's body and the fog as `WaterPS` lays them on, nothing seen from below. A
half turn of twist drew the foam into spiral arms like a painted sign; a fifth leaves it
foam. The rings: every source is a ripple source of size 64, re-armed every 0.4 to 0.8
seconds by a hash of its place. The drops: on the logic tick, beside `AnimateWaterfalls`,
two `TriggerSmallSplash` drops a tick at every source within eight squares of the camera,
sixteen a tick at most - the engine's own splash of a rat or a shell landing in water,
sparks thrown up at 20 to 28 units a tick and slowed by 2 to 2.5 units a tick every tick,
so they rise about 150 to 200 units over the water within 80 of where they left it and
live 24 ticks (the engine's own arithmetic run offline over the four feet of room 231 for
three seconds: 184 drops alive, the highest 199 units up - RoomProbe draws no sparks).
ANDREA2's four sources keep about 200 of the game's 1,024 sparks alive, and the cap holds
JOBY5's 37 sources to about 380. Nothing of it runs without sheets or with `hd_motion` 0.
The drops draw on `GetRandomControl`, the game's own random sequence, as the classic mist
does: with `hd_water` 1 in a level with a foot, later random draws come out differently,
and nothing saves or replays them. Spin, twist, the square root, 0.8, the ring's period
and size, two drops, eight squares and sixteen are free choices, set by eye on the round's
RoomProbe pictures.

The splash of ANDREA1's fountain is not an effect of the engine. Room 59 holds a
WATERFALL1 and a WATERFALLSS1 at one place and no emitter (`ItemCheck` on the classic
file); the classic engine scrolls their texture and nothing more. The remaster's art draws
the splash: a spray part of material 1, a dense mesh of 6,548 triangles that sways, its
page scrolled at 1.5 a second (`TrgProbe -parts 59`). The same part, same page and
parameters, stands at the foot of room 231's curtain (3,750 triangles) and shows nothing
there - its colours come to half of ANDREA1's and its light adds nothing to the picture
above. So the nearest effect the engine has is taken, `TriggerSmallSplash`: `SetupSplash`
is Lara's three-ring splash with its sound, `TriggerWaterfallMist` already rises where a
WATERFALLMIST object stands (room 231 has two) and the bubbles are under water.

The text file and the tools. `swirl <x> <z> <radius>` (64 to 2,048) puts a source on the
surface of the row's room's square under that place (a fountain's jet that has no object),
and `swirl off` takes the objects' sources of the row's bodies away; a row holds 24 tokens
at most. RoomProbe builds the objects' feet out of the classic `.TRC` as the engine builds
them out of `items[]` and draws the swirls and the rings; it draws no sparks, so the drops
are not in its pictures; `-swirl x,z,r` adds a source to a picture. WATERLOG: `falls=` at
the end of the level line, `swirl=` at the end of a body's, a `fall=` line per waterfall
object (its top and bottom, the surface and the gap, the sources, `art=` for the art's
points that took the classic ones' place) and a `foot=` line per source.

Room 231's own water art stays hidden: the sheet's look in the fountain hall is right. The
swirl the owner liked in it now stands where the water lands, made of the sheet's own
foam.

Decided against the brief: no stretch. The brief asked for the falling water to be
stretched down to the surface where its bottom stops short. All 31 waterfall objects over
a sheet end at their surface (gap 0 on every `fall=` line of the fifteen levels), room
231's curtains end within seven units of it, and the art could not be stretched without
rewriting its vertex buffer, `RoomVS` being shared bytecode. What reads as short is the
art's fading light, which the swirl, the rings and the drops now meet.

The water's own height (`hd_render.cpp` :9456, :9544, :10066; `hd_level.cpp` :1843;
`RoomProbe.cpp` :4766, :4828). Measured first, over every dry square whose room below is
an underwater room, with the classic files and `Tr5Level::cornerFloor` and `cornerCeiling`
(a tool of this round): in ANDREA1, ANDREA2, ANDY1, JOBY2, JOBY4 and JOBY5 the square's
floor byte is the water room's ceiling everywhere. RICH2's two corner plates (room 125
square 2,4 and room 126 square 2,2) are split sectors whose floor byte, -1,280, is their
highest corner: three corners lie at the water's -768, one 512 over it, and the water
room's ceiling there is -768 at three corners and -512 at the fourth, the underside of the
raised triangle. ANDY3 has 29 such squares, 28 of them the island's edge in the pond
(rooms 34 and 183, all of them split sectors with a no-collision triangle, one triangle at
the water's 11,008, the other a click or two over it) and room 12's square 13,3. ANDY2 has
16 squares (rooms 57 and 136, 158, 159; a cross of four round a square) whose flat dry
floor stands 1,024 over the flat ceiling of the water under it - no water at all. So the
surface of a water square is now the top of its water room there, the highest corner of
that room's ceiling over the square, the height Lara's head breaks the surface at, and a
square whose dry floor stands more than a click over that top at every corner is no water
square. A split square keeps its whole sheet at the water's top: the level's raised
triangle covers the part under it, which is what the owner asked. The corners come out of
the floor data's slope entries through one function, the engine's `GetHeight` and
`GetCeiling` with the corner substitution the randomizer's `Tr5Level` makes; the engine
hands the words of `floor_data` (walked as `GetHeight` walks a chain, the ceiling's entry
as `GetMinimumCeiling` reads it), RoomProbe those of the classic `.TRC`. Bodies now join
at the true height. With `tomb5.hd_water` 0 the squares stand at their floors as without
the sheets: the bodies there move the remaster's water art, and that stays as it was.

The rivers (`hd_render.cpp` :8607, :8739, :9165, :10253, :10317, :10518, :10675, :12148;
`hd_room.hlsl` :1798, :1966, :2601). Measured: of the fifteen levels only ANDY3 has a
`TO_SINK` trigger under a water square - in the water rooms under its two rivers, room 47
under body 0 (rooms 0, 42, 43, 182; six places, sinks 9 and 6 of strengths 10 and 8) and
room 50 under the body of rooms 38, 41, 184, 185 (one place, sink 7, strength 4); the rest
of that river runs through rooms with no water square, and JOBY4's 204 and ANDREA3's 6
sink squares lie under none. `LaraWaterCurrent` (`game/laraswim.cpp`) steers Lara's
velocity toward strength x 4,096 / 4 in 1/256 units a tick along the way to the sink and
moves her by a 256th of it: 4 units a tick for strength 1, 120 units a second at 30 ticks
a second. A body whose water names a sink is of the new class *river*: its flow is the
mean way from its places toward their sinks and its speed the mean of 120 x strength -
ANDY3's come to -1,0 at 1,080 and 1,0 at 480 units a second. What the water shows of the
speed is held to 720 units a second, a free choice by eye (rows of a few hundred units
carried a square a second slide past as a smear). The river's rows run 1.11 to 1.25
radians off the flow, so a crest runs 2 to 3 times as far along the current as across it,
low (1.2 units on 300 the steepest), carried at that speed; no bank foam, no waterline, no
whitecaps. A second draw over the river's sheet, `RiverPS` (152 slots), adds thin streaks
along the flow - two sets of ridges across it about 410 and 170 units apart that wander
slowly with the way down the river, carried 1.4 times as fast as the rows, broken by a
slow field whose threshold swings over the bank foam's 5 seconds, at most half of the
foam's cover - and, where the river ends against a wall or a drop, the bank foam's own
pattern laid across it, carried into the end at 0.3 of the speed, dense at the end, broken
further up and gone 768 units upstream (three quarters of a square, inside the half to one
square of a weir's foam on the reference photograph), nothing at the upper end. Per
vertex, colour1's blue holds the way along the flow to the first point with no water,
counting a point on a bank as water when water lies a unit to either side of it. The rows'
angles and heights, the streaks' spacings, speed, strength and threshold and the end
foam's reach are free choices, set by eye on the round's RoomProbe pictures. What moved
under the river was not the classic animated faces - those are the water plane's own faces
at 11,008 (texture ranges 0 and 1), and no restored face lies under a sheet - but the
remaster's own flowing surface: one draw call of material 1, 90 to 108 flat triangles
three units over the water in each of rooms 38, 41, 42 and 43, scrolled at 2.5 page units
a second (`RoomProbe -animtex`, `TrgProbe -parts`). Over a river's squares such a draw
call, wholly flat flow-material triangles within 32 units of the surface, is now left out
like the remaster's still water - 378 triangles in ANDY3; room 34's, over the pond, stays.
`hd_water.txt` takes `river` as a class and `flow <dx> <dz> <speed>` (the way -1 to 1
each, not both 0, the speed 0 to 4,000 units a second) in place of the sinks'; a row of
class `river` without either runs along the body's long axis at 240. A row holds 28 tokens
at most. With `tomb5.hd_water` 0 no body is a river.

The waterfall's foot as one zone (`hd_render.cpp` :8964, :10136, :10185, :11326, :12545;

from above and a photograph of a real waterfall (reference pictures supplied for this
project, not in the repository); JOBY5's feet the same. Measured first: ANDREA2 room 231's
one waterfall object lands on 88 points of the art's falling water in two strands about
1,250 units apart, each cut into two discs of radius 762 and 526 - four discs; JOBY5's 27
objects drew 35. Now the waterfall objects over one body whose foot points come within 512
units of each other's are one curtain; its points, gathered every 512 units along their
principal axis, give the curtain's footprint, a polyline of the steps' means, and a
segment over a step without points bridges a gap at 0.85 of the foam, so the two strands
land in one zone (at 0.6 the bridge left two zones on the pictures). The zone's reach is
614 units plus 0.3 of the longest wet stretch, held to 614 to 1,229 - 0.6 of a square from
a narrow jet, 0.9 from a strand a square wide, 1.2 from one of two (at 0.6 of the whole
length the reach covered the room). `FootPS` takes `SwirlPS`'s place: per segment the
pixel's distance to it, its way along it and its side; the pattern is carried outward at
220 units a second times the square root of what is left of the reach, read at the way a
mark has come (twice the reach times one less the square root of what is left) less the
speed times the clock, so every blotch leaves the curtain fast, slows down and gathers at
the rim; across the line at 0.75 of its scale along it (0.45 drew a comb), so near the
curtain a blotch is a streak pointing away from it; the bank foam's two layers ride at two
speeds, the fine one at 0.55, so the flow does not read as a belt; the two sides are moved
260 units apart over 160 units either side of the line (a shear of the pattern drew a
herringbone, a sign of the side a seam past the ends); the outline breathes with the patch
field and a lobe field of its own; the density is the bank foam's with the threshold along
the fall of what is left of the reach to the power 0.75 (0.5 filled the zone, 1 and 2 left
a thin line). Nothing turns anywhere. Up to eight segments a draw, in c124 to c131 and
c137 to c144. The rings and the drops come from a point every 512 units along the
footprint's wet stretches (ANDREA2: four, as before). `hd_water.txt`: `foot <x1> <z1> <x2>
<z2> <reach>` and `foot off`; `swirl <x> <z> <r>` is read as a foot of length 0 and `swirl
off` as `foot off`, and the level line counts such rows (`old=`); a row holds 30 tokens at
most. RoomProbe `-foot x1,z1,x2,z2,r` (and `-swirl x,z,r`). WATERLOG: `curtain=` ends the
fall and foot lines (the foot line's `radius=` is its curtain's reach), a `seg=` line per

6 segments, JOBY2 3 of 1 each, JOBY5 27 with 36 segments (no two of its objects stand

Under the water (`hd_room.hlsl` :1478, :1789, :2415, :2461; `hd_glow.hlsl` :199;

ray in the water - the whole distance to a point under the surface, the distance times the

absorption, sigma_s its one over the absorption length, both times 0.35 (at the sheet's

132). While the camera is under water the distance fog's start moves past any view and the

view space and the eye's depth - the model shader has no world position. With them all
zero, as in every frame whose camera is not under water and in every frame with

**After the owner's fifth play test of 2026-10-09.** The build of `059a185` was played

repository). Kept as they are: RICH2, ANDY3's pond, the view from under the water, the

The flood under a sheet (`hd_room.hlsl` RoomVS, `hd_render.cpp` `set_room_rows`). Measured
first, with RoomProbe at ANDY3's pond, its island, a bank close up, JOBY5's deck,
ANDREA1's basin and RICH2's pool at the clock times 3, 11 and 19, and on the owner's
frames: the sheet itself does not climb a bank - `WaterVS` tapers its lift to nothing at a
bank vertex, whose shore distance is 0, and the depth clip refuses a pixel whose scene
lies above the surface at rest or within 8 units under it whatever the lift (cause a,
nothing to change). What moved was the land. RoomVS's flood gives the surface bit to every
vertex of a room at the water's height inside the box of the marked corners, and only a
wall's normal keeps a vertex out; ANDY3's pond has no remaster water art at all (0 `.TRG`
triangles in its classic water planes, measured in the material-16 entry), so every
flooded vertex there is the bank's own mesh, lifted by the swell up to 36 units, its UV
wobbled and the surface caustic laid on - the land torn in wave shapes, and the clip's
edge and the waterline riding on it (cause c). JOBY5's deck - room 4's squares 3,2, 3,3,
4,3, 5,2 and 5,3 at one click and 3,5, 5,5 and 5,6 at none, with no room below - is dry
floor at the water's height inside the same kind of box and took the caustic and the
wobble (cause d). Now `set_room_rows` hands RoomVS a gate in c18.z: 1 in a room whose body
draws its sheet and hides the remaster's art, and there the flood lays no swell, wobble or
surface caustic on anything; the colour shimmer keeps the classic selector as before. With
`tomb5.hd_water` 0 no sheet is built and the gate is 0. `RoomVS` 412 to 414 slots. The
waterline (cause b): it painted every pixel whose frame lay 24 to 48 units under the
surface, and the pond's floor rising gently to its banks put that band hundreds of units
out into the water - a 1:10 slope puts 48 units 480 out - at 0.25 to 0.75: the thick white
band of the owner's frames. Now the line is weighed by how fast that depth changes from
one pixel to the next (`fwidth`): whole from 6 units a pixel - round a post, a hull, a
swimming body - and fading toward a flat shore, where it keeps a few pixels along the
edge; its fall from 24 to 48 units is a straight ramp. 6 is a free choice, set by eye on
the round's RoomProbe pictures. To stay under 512 the view variant's switch leaves the
clip of the depth variant: `WaterPS`'s depth variant 508 to 509 slots, the view variant
503 to 507, the under variant 339 to 335; the plain variant keeps its bytecode. No square
is dropped as walkable floor: the deck's squares are dry squares already, and the pattern
on them was the flood's, not a sheet's.

The creatures' mark on the game's path (`hd_render.cpp` `HDRenderWaterMarkLine`,
`draw_water_sheet`; `hd_level.cpp` `HDFrameDraw`; `RoomProbe.cpp`). Measured: on RoomProbe
three stand-ins 60 units under ANDY1's pool (rooms 132 and 142, its bank's patches round

waterline, so in the game the mark did not reach the sheet. Read in order: the rooms'
receive clears the stencil, the mark brackets the HD objects' solid draw, the models'
receive keeps to bit 2, the bracket ends, the classic buckets draw, the glow phase opens a
bracket of its own, takes the copy and draws the sheets; nothing between sets another
