and nothing outside `hd_render.cpp` touches the stencil. RoomProbe drew both phases in one
bracket; `-twophase` now draws them in two as the game does, and the mark holds there too
(three stand-ins, three clock times). The cause in the game is not found by reading, so
the mark gets its own line, once a level with `-log`, for the last frame that drew a
sheet: `WATERLOG level=<L> mark=<0/1> why=<n> mark_intz=<0/1> objects=<n> sheet_intz=<0/1>
sheets=<n> split=<n>` - whether that frame's bracket marked and why not (1 no device, 2 no
sheets built, 3 no depth texture, 4 no depth variant, 5 no stencil), whether the
depth-stencil surface at the mark and at the first sheet draw was the INTZ surface, the
objects on the frame's list, the sheet draws and the ranges drawn twice. RoomProbe prints
it with `-creature`. And the marked pass of a range now draws no foam at all - the line,
the bank's foam and its patches (`gWaterFoam.w`) and the whitecaps (`gWaterMisc.y`) are 0
in its constants - since a rat 50 to 60 units down in a small pool lies inside the bank's

The rivers (`hd_render.cpp` "a sink in the water", `kRiverCover`; `hd_room.hlsl`
`RiverPS`). Measured, over the camera table and every `TO_SINK` command of every square
with the randomizer's `Tr5Level`: ANDY3's sinks are entries 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12
and 18. None lies in rooms 66 or 70 or anywhere in room 34's pond, and no chain of those
rooms names a sink; rooms 66 and 70 are the pond's own shallow water rooms (ceiling
11,008, floors one to six clicks under it) under room 34, and room 34's channel is the
body of rooms 34 and 38 (4 squares) between the pond and the river of rooms 38 and 41.
The red spheres of the owner's map pictures are not entries of this level's camera and
sink table, which the randomized level in the game folder shares entry for entry. Sinks
10, 11 and 12 lie in the tunnels 53, 55, 56 and 57, water rooms with no room above them.
Sink 1 (strength 10) lies in the sea of rooms 10 to 17 (42 squares), its two trigger
squares under no sheet: a pull toward a drain. So the pond's arms are not rivers by any
data of the level, and stay what they are; `hd_water.txt` can still make a body a river
with a flow. The rule now also takes a sink that lies in a body's water - inside one of
its squares, at or under its surface, above the floor there - whatever squares name it:
its flow is the mean way from those squares to the sink and its speed the strength's,
and it counts only where the squares that name the body's lying sinks number at least a

**Alt+Enter, the crash seam's first catch.** In the fifth play test Alt+Enter in the title
of the build of `059a185` ended with the seam's line `CRASH code=0xC0000005 ...
module=d3d9.dll+0x8D06F thread=game` and its minidump (a log and a dump supplied for this
project, not in the repository). Read with the build's own symbols and no symbol server,
the game thread died reading address 8 inside d3d9.dll's `DrawPrimitiveUP`, called from
`HWDrawPrimitive` in `HWR_DrawSortList`'s case 4 (`specific/polyinsert.cpp` :165), the
sky's draw type, under `DrawSortList`, `OutputSky`, `SkyDrawPhase`, `DoTitle`,
`DoGameflow` and `GameMain`: the first classic draw after the device was released and made
again, sent to the new device (its address is not the one the log released). That case
binds `Textures[texture].tex`. Every page of `Textures[]` (`CreateTexturePage`,
`specific/texture.cpp`) and the inventory's and load screen's picture are
`D3DPOOL_MANAGED` textures of the device current when they were made, and nothing on the
way from `WinProcessCommands` (`specific/winmain.cpp` :186) through `DXToggleFullScreen`,
`DXCreate` and `DXClose` made them again: the 22 references the log printed at the release
are those pages, each keeping its device alive. Everything else the classic draw needs,
`HWInitialise` sets on the new device - the stage and sampler state, the render states,
`D3DRS_CLIPPING` and the one FVF; `DrawPrimitiveUP` takes no stream - and the HD side had
let go of all its objects (`HDLevelDeviceLost`; the sky dome waits for the next level, the
text for its font texture). Inside d3d9 the null is an empty parent slot in the released
device's bookkeeping of its managed textures, reached through the page.

Reproduced here, which the second play test's reading had not: a page of a released
device drawn on a new one does no harm when it was the only page drawn on the old device,
and fails once the pages there differ in when they were last drawn - in the game the sky
is drawn in every frame and most pages are not. RoomProbe `-cycleclassic 22 -nomove`
crashes at `d3d9.dll+0x8D06F` reading address 8, and its own dump shows the d3d9 frames of
the owner's at the same offsets under `DrawPrimitiveUP(D3DPT_TRIANGLELIST, 2)`; with a
single page the draw returns and the device has lost the picture (`GetRenderTargetData`
fails with `E_FAIL`).

The fix. `specific/devicemove.h` (header only, `DeviceMoveTexture` :73): a texture not
made on the new device is made again on it, same size, levels and format, managed; every
level is copied through `LockRect`, which needs none of the level's data because a managed
texture keeps its texels in system memory; the old one is released. A texture that is not
managed, of a format whose texel size the header does not know, or whose copy fails, is
released and its pointer set to 0, which draws untextured until the next level instead of
crashing. `DXCreate` (`specific/dxshell.cpp` :386) notes whether a device was there before
`DXClose`, and after `DXCreateD3DDevice` succeeds on such a recreation (:554) calls
`MoveTexturesToDevice` (`specific/texture.cpp` :169): every entry of `Textures[]`, then
the picture (`MonoScreenToDevice`, `specific/LoadSave.cpp` :640), and one new line under
`-log`:

`DXLOG device recreated - pages=<n> moved=<m> dropped=<d> kept=<k> picture=<0|1>
old_device_refs=<r>`

`pages` is the number of entries in `Textures[]`, `moved` those made again, `dropped`
those released and drawn untextured, `kept` those already on the new device, `picture` 1
when the picture was there, and `old_device_refs` what the old device still holds once all
of them have moved: 0 is nothing, and the device is gone; -1 is no texture of it met.
Alt+Enter and the resolution keys both come through `DXCreate`; startup (no device before)
and the reset in `DXShowFrame` (the same device, whose managed textures stay valid) do
not. The HD path is unchanged: released at the device change, made again at the next
level. The extra work is one texture made and one copy per page at the recreation, at most
the 256 entries `Textures[]` holds, and nothing in any frame. RoomProbe `-cycleclassic
<pages>` (:9990) draws pages the classic way - made as `CreateTexturePage` makes them, the
engine's FVF, the state `HWInitialise` sets, `DrawPrimitiveUP` with 40-byte vertices, the
last page drawn once more in a frame of its own - on one device, moves them with the same
header to a second and then to a third, and compares the three pictures byte for byte.

**Measured.** The dump: `ebx` 0 at `mov edx,[ebx+8]` (d3d9 +0x8D06F), the call
`DrawPrimitiveUP(device, 4, 2, vertices, 40)` on a device at a different address from the
released one, the case-4 `SetTexture` with `Textures[]` before it; a minidump holds no
heap, so the texture's own pointer is not in it. RoomProbe `-cycleclassic`: 22 pages (the
title's count), 1 and 256: on the second and third device `moved` equal to the pages,
`dropped=0 kept=0 old_device_refs=0`, the released device's own count 22, 1 and 256 before
the move.

**Checked.** The classic path (`-classicroom` and `-classiconly` on ANDREA2 231, JOBY2 66
and ANDY3 34) md5-identical to `8691e82`, 3 of 3, and the classic picture drawn on the
second device of `-devicecycle` identical to it, 3 of 3, every device released with
`RefCnt = 0`; the fifteen cameras with `-hdwater 0` identical to the fix round's parity
set, 15 of 15; with `-hdwater 1` identical to the foot's-gap pictures of `3136faa`, 15 of
15; no shader changed; the suites (ModernTest 14721, MenuTest 42627, InterpTest 729,
LipsTest 270 and 243) 0 failed; the engine and every tool build.

The HD art still falls back to classic until the next level after a toggle. A film's

**The eye under the water in JOBY4, after the sixth play test.** The sixth play test found
JOBY4 no different from the build before, and the reason is a gate, not the look.
`HDFrameDraw` (`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`) decides once a frame whether the eye is under
the water; only then is `frame.under` 1, and from it `water_under_constants`
(`hd_render.cpp`) fills c134 to c136 and c145, the fog bulbs go and the sheen gives way.
The gate asked `camera.underwater`. `CalculateCamera` (`game/camera.cpp:1433`) sets that
flag from the camera room's `ROOM_UNDERWATER` in every level but `LVL5_DEEPSEA_DIVE`, and
the level start clears it (`game/setup.cpp:2334`), so in JOBY4 it is 0 from the first
frame to the last: the constants stayed zero there, and the extinction, the clear zone and
the deep look - the last made for this level alone - never ran in it. RoomProbe
`-underwater` sets the frame by hand, so every picture of those parts showed the shaders
and none went through this gate. The exception covers two things in the classic engine:
the looped `SFX_UNDERWATER`, played in the same block (`camera.cpp:1437`), and the flag,
whose one classic reader is the screen wobble of the room vertices
(`specific/drawroom.cpp:597`) - the dive keeps its underwater sound and its wobble out.
The draw side keeps a flag of its own, `camera_underwater` (`game/draw.cpp:2420` and
`:3344`), set for every frame from the room it is drawn from, with no exception; it is
static in that file and nothing reads it.

Now the gate reads the camera room's own `ROOM_UNDERWATER` flag - the test camera.cpp
makes and the value draw.cpp's flag holds for the frame, read in `hd_level.cpp` itself
because draw.cpp's is out of reach and stays as it is - and, as before,
`HDRenderWaterUnderOn`, true only for a water room of a level that built its sheets.
JOBY4's 134 water rooms all have a body (two under its one basin, 132 by the fallback;
RoomProbe `-hdwater 1 -nodraw` prints `under=2 under_fallback=132 under_deep=1`), so every
one of them now takes the deep look. Two things follow in the other levels from the same
rule. camera.cpp sets its flag before the camera moves, a logic tick behind the room the
frame is drawn from: the look now opens on the frame the camera enters the water, not a
tick later (on leaving, the gate shut at once already - a dry room has no body). And a
fly-by moves the camera without `CalculateCamera`: the look follows its camera into and
out of the water, where `camera.underwater` kept the value it had before the fly-by.

The screen wobble keeps `camera.underwater` (`FillFrameLighting`, `out.cameraUnderwater`).
It is the classic's own offset on the projected vertices (`hd_room.hlsl` `RoomVS`, step
4, the formula of `drawroom.cpp`), drawn beside classic faces that take it from that
flag, and `ClassicFaceDrawn` repeats the classic projection with it for the corner rule.
In the dive the classic game shows no wobble by its own exception, the owner asked for
none, and following the room flag there would move the HD art while the classic faces of
the same frame stand still. With `tomb5.hd_water 0` the level builds no sheets
(`g_wlevel.built` stays 0), `HDRenderWaterUnderOn` is false and every frame is as before;
with `hd_enable 0` `HDFrameDraw` returns before the gate.

The seam: with `-log`, the first frame of a level outside the inventory ring whose camera
room carries the flag writes `WATERLOG level=<stem> undergate room=<n> flag=<0|1>
cam=<0|1> on=<0|1> deep=<0|1>` - the camera's room, its flag (1 on this line),
`camera.underwater` (0 throughout JOBY4, and 0 as well on a frame the camera has just swum
into), 1 when that frame is drawn under the water, and 1 when the level takes the deep
look (the level line's `under_deep=`).

**Checked.** No shader and no tool changed, and RoomProbe does not run the gate - it sets
the frame itself: the fifteen cameras with `-hdwater 0`, 15 of 15 identical to the fix
round's parity set; with `-hdwater 1`, 15 of 15 identical to the river round's of
`7820bce`. The suites (ModernTest 14721, MenuTest 42627, InterpTest 729, LipsTest 270 and
243) 0 failed; the engine builds, and no tool compiles `hd_level.cpp` (MenuTest reads it
as text).

**Left.** Only the game shows JOBY4 under the water: the deep look's darkness under the
game's own gamma, its fog bulbs gone and its distance fog replaced, its fly-bys. The
`undergate` line of the owner's next log says what each level did; JOBY4 should read
`flag=1 cam=0 on=1 deep=1`.

**Alt+Enter after the sixth play test: the HD level built again, the film's texture, the
screen capture.** The build of `9f2d2ed` was played (a log supplied for this project, not
in the repository). Alt+Enter no longer crashed; it switched the HD art off until the next
level, and the owner's screenshots with the system's own Print key stopped working after
it. His log shows four toggles in ANDREA1: at the first the released device still counted
`RefCnt = 105` and the new line said `pages=105 moved=104 ... old_device_refs=1`, at the
three later ones `RefCnt = 104` and `old_device_refs=0`.

The film's texture. The one reference that was not a page is the playback texture of the
films (`specific/fmv.cpp`, `BinkTexture`): a managed texture made by the first film on the
device of that moment and released only when the game ends. It is made only while none
exists, so the start device got it with the first film and no later device ever had one,
which is the 105 against 104; nothing moved or dropped it at a recreation, so the start
device stayed alive for the rest of the session, and the next film would have bound a
texture of a released device on the new one - the misuse that ended the fifth play test's
toggle inside d3d9.dll. `FmvDeviceLost` (`fmv.cpp`) releases it in `DXClose` beside
`HDLevelDeviceLost`, with a `Released Bink Texture` line; `PlayFmv` makes it again on the
device of the next film.

The HD level built again. `HDLevelDeviceRecreated` (`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`) runs in
`DXCreate` on a recreation, after `MoveTexturesToDevice` has moved the classic pages (the
HD water frames borrow entries of `Textures[]` above the level's own, so the order is
fixed). It builds the level that was drawing HD when the device went - `HDLevelDeviceLost`
notes that, `HDLevelUnload` forgets it - with `HDLevelBuild` itself: everything the build
reads is still loaded (`room[]`, the floor data, `objects[]`, `items[]`, the markers
sidecar, the level's stem), and the art and its pages are read from the Remaster's DATA
again as at a level load. What `HDLevelDeviceLost` released comes back by that path: the
shaders and the declaration (`HDRenderInit`), the buffers, the page cache, the gloss field
and the water sheets with their depth texture (`HDRenderLevelBegin`, `BuildWaterSheets`),
the borrowed water frames (`BuildWaterFrames`), the models and Lara
(`HDObjectLevelBuild`); the shadow targets and the frame's copy are made by the first
frame that needs them, as after a level load; then `HDFontBuild` makes the font's texture
again. The title is a level of its own, so its rooms, sky and font come back the same way;
its logo and the menu pages are classic pages and were already moved. Two things differ
from a load. The build takes group i for room i, which holds only before any flip, while
`FlipMap` (`game/control.cpp`) swaps the rooms' records in place: the pairs whose flip
stands set in `flip_stats` are swapped back for the build and swapped again after it,
keeping each number's `flipped_room`, `item_number` and `fx_number` in place so that the
second swap gives back every byte (FlipMap's own swap hands the alternate the room's item
list and is not its own inverse), and `HDFlipRoom` then moves the art with each pair as it
does when a savegame's flips are applied after its load. And the HD clock keeps running,
so the scrolls, the waves and the books go on where they were. The waterfall mist the
build moves onto the art's footprint is a projection and is not moved further. A level
that was classic when the device went stays classic, and nothing of it runs with
`hd_enable 0`. One new line, `HDLOG device recreated - level=<stem> rebuilt=<0|1>
flipped_pairs=<n>`, and the `DXLOG device recreated` line ends in `hd=<rebuilt|classic>
ms=<n>`, the build's time. The game thread waits at `BeginScene` meanwhile, before the
frame's lists are begun, so the frame that follows starts from the new build. The reset in
`DXShowFrame` (a lost device, which a windowed device does not see on a focus change)
keeps its old answer: classic until the next level.

The screen capture. The window code of `DXCreate`, `WinSetStyle`, `DXShowFrame` and
`CreateMonoScreen` - the two placements, the style of the two display states, the present
parameters, the back buffer read into a system memory surface and the 24-bit TGA - moved
unchanged into `specific/devicewindow.h`, so that RoomProbe `-windowcycle` drives the
engine's own code on a real window of the engine's class and styles: the start state, one
toggle and a second, each presenting a colour of its own. Each state prints its line -
`GWL_STYLE`, `GWL_EXSTYLE`, topmost, the window and client rectangles, the monitor, and
the present parameters and creation flags as the device reports them - then what a GDI
read of the screen (`BitBlt` with `CAPTUREBLT`) and the DXGI desktop duplication see at
the client's middle, and the screenshot path's HRESULT and file. The same lines go into
the game's log: `DXLOG window <start|toggle|mode> ...` after the start, every Alt+Enter
and every resolution key, `DXLOG screenshot hr=<0x...> file=<TombNNNN.tga> bytes=<n>` for
every file of the apostrophe key, and `DXLOG mono picture hr=<0x...> - no picture` when
the inventory's picture cannot be read.

**Measured.** RoomProbe `-windowcycle` on this machine (2560 x 1440): the start state

client both the monitor's rectangle, windowed, discard, X8R8G8B8 2560 x 1440, one back
buffer, no multisampling, interval one, refresh 0, auto depth, `behavior=00000044`
(hardware vertex processing, multithreaded); the windowed state `style=14C20000` (caption,
minimize box) `ex=00040100`, the window the monitor's rectangle and its client 8,31 to
2552,1432 under a back buffer of 2560 x 1440; after the second toggle every field of the
start state again, byte for byte. In every state the screen read and the desktop
duplication showed the colour presented, and so did a frame of the system's window capture

The night (`hd_render.cpp` `kWaterPalette`, "the night" over `kWaterMoon`, `water_lit`,
`water_look`, `upload_water_room`, `draw_river`; `hd_room.hlsl` `RiverPS`). Measured first
with RoomProbe at ANDY3's river from its lower end, at a camera found to match the owner's
picture of the two circles, at an ANDY1 pool and at ANDY2, each light term taken away in
turn in a build made for the measurement alone: the body light to a grey of its luma, the
highlight off, the reflection to grey, the caustic off, the river's sheen off. On the
sheet's pixels (`-waterdepthview 1` against the picture) the chroma-weighted mean hue
stayed at 15 to 17 degrees and the share of gold pixels (hue 15 to 55, saturation
over 0.35, value over 0.25) at 13 to 22 % whatever was taken away: the light of ANDY3's
river is 0.30, 0.32, 0.34 (the floor of 0.30), the sky's horizon and the highlight move
the hue by under a degree. The warm colour is the stream beds' own art seen through 256 to
1,024 units of clear water (with `-hdwater 0` the beds are red-orange), and the gold
lattice on it is the caustic: RoomPS multiplies the floor's own light by 1 + 0.3 w c (up
to 1.78 at the surface) and RiverPS lays the same on the frame's copy, so the bright lines
take the bed's colour. With the caustic taken off the lattice goes and the hue stays.
ANDY2's bodies take 0.95, 0.45, 0.30 and 1.06, 0.48, 0.30 (its lamps); indoors that light
colours the water, its highlight and its foam. Now the palette's sections carry a night
flag, Ireland's set (ANDY1 to ANDY3, a project decision on how those levels look): there a
body's colours take the moon's light - the luma of its rooms' light
times 0.90, 1.01, 1.22, a cool tint of luma 1 -, its highlight and foam the same tint,
under the sky the highlight at 0.4 and the foam at 0.6 of the day's; RoomPS's caustic is
off at night (c16.x 0: a moon colour there would cost slots RoomPS, at 510 of 512, and its
depth twin, at 509, do not have, and the moon casts no caustic the eye resolves), and a
river's drifting caustic stays at half strength as the floor's luma in the moon's tint
(RiverPS c146). The sky rows are the domes as measured and stay. Rome, Russia and the VCI
keep their look: their hue is their palette's, and no word makes them night. Free choices,
set by eye on the round's RoomProbe pictures of ANDY1 to ANDY3.

The flow as the standard (`hd_room.hlsl` `RiverPS`, "the relief's light"; `hd_render.cpp`
`kRiverRelief`). Measured first: the owner's two circles are the river of rooms 38 and 41
(OK) and the stream of room 66 (N.OK), seen from above beside the bank between them. The
streaks in the OK circle are the class highlight on the stretched rows near its mirror
angle - with the highlight off they go; the river's sheen changed nothing measurable,
because it took the reflection's colour from horizon to zenith by the view's slope, and
from above that is ANDY's zenith, 11, 19, 32. The rows' fade (WaterVS `keepA`, `keepB`) is
not what flattens the water: the waves' share of the picture (the mean luma change a test
row `waves 0` makes) on the river, the stream and at eye level was 10.44, 0.77, 1.48 with
it and 10.55, 0.82, 1.65 without it at 960 x 540, the same to the second decimal at 1920 x
1080; the slope gain at every angle raised it to 16.59, 1.40, 2.22 on the river alone, and
it lives in WaterPS, whose depth variant has three slots left. The stream shows no relief
because it is 256 units deep - the bend is 1 - T = 0.17 of the river's absorption length,
three units for the steepest rows - and the highlight stands off its mirror angle. Now
RiverPS lights the relief: the eight rows' slope at the bent place, with WaterVS's fade,
against the class light's way along the surface, lighter toward it by 7 times the slope of
the highlight's colour, darker away through alpha (0.6 of that share), with no Fresnel and
no reflection in it, so the crests read as long streaks along the flow from every angle,
carried with the current and swelling and fading with the rows' envelopes; the sheen's
lighter lines take the highlight's colour too. The waves' share rose on the stream to 5.95
(6.45 at 1920 x 1080), at eye level to 5.68, on the river 9.23 (the gold lattice that
carried the rest is gone at night). WaterPS and the rows' fade are as they were. The gain
of 7 and the moon's highlight of 0.4 are free choices, set by eye with the brightest river
pixel outside the end's foam at 113 of 255.

The streams (`hd_render.cpp` `kWaterFlow`). The owner's picture of room 66 shows the

(the yaw the editor's, 0 along +z and 90 along +x; the pitch counted the other way), so

The shallows (`hd_room.hlsl` WaterPS, "the shallows"; `hd_render.cpp` c106). A wave cannot
stand higher than about 0.78 of the depth under it (the breaking index of a solitary wave,
the textbook figure), so its amplitude, half its height, may reach 0.39 of the depth: the
rows keep their whole height from 2.56 times that height. WaterPS reads the depth under
the pixel - the frame's depth under the sheet with the depth texture, the vertex depth
without - before the waves' slope and takes `shoal` = saturate((depth + 1) x the inverse
of that depth, `gWaterStage.w`); it scales the rows' slope (the reflection, the highlight
and the floor's bend), the bank foam's patches and the whitecaps; the waterline and the
rings keep theirs. Per pixel and not per vertex: inside the pond's squares the vertex
depth is the classic bed's 256 plus the lift at every vertex while half the bank's
crossings lie inside the squares, so a vertex factor would leave the east, south-east and
west banks undamped. A body without a lift has 1e9 there and draws as before to the bit -
the sea and channel bodies elsewhere keep the look accepted in the game; the variant under
the water holds nothing. The whole wave height's floor of 1, which WaterPS applied twice,
comes from the processor. The waterline's own width was not changed: on the level surface
the band at the pond's south edge seen from above went from 857, 494 and 766 white pixels
at 1, 3 and 5 seconds to none.

**The crests: short, in a fan.** Asked for after the tenth play test (reference pictures
supplied for this project, not in the repository): the water of every body at times
throws a chequered pattern where the waves and other things lie over each other - on
ANDY3's stream and pond from the plank bridge, on ANDREA2's sewer canal from Lara's
shoulder at eye level, on the pond from above by its plank bridge - while the same canal
seen from above and behind Lara, about 35 degrees down, looks right and is the look to
keep. His sketch beside the question: on the left the water as it was, a stack of
straight parallel crests between two banks; in the middle the stream's course; on the
right short crest pieces at varying angles, some bent, scattered over the water, their
directions following the stream - waves not monotone but from several directions, fitting
the current. That right side is what this part builds, on every body.

The cause. The lattice is the light on the surface, not the floor seen through it: with
every body's refraction off (`bend 0`) it stays as it was, with the rows' heights at 0
(`waves 0`) it is gone. The eight rows of a body are straight plane waves whose crests
run ruler-straight over many wavelengths, and two or three of like height crossing at
fixed angles light the same diamond cells with the highlight, the reflection's lobe toward
the light and the Fresnel term again and again - the channel's three highest at 0, -0.19
and 0.42 radians, the sea's at 0, -0.29 and 0.61, the basin's nearly all round, the
river's two mirrored families 1.12 to 1.25 radians either side of its flow; the rows'
envelopes bring a lattice up when two of them swell together. Measured again in this
part with the round's own measure (below): the surface light alone - the picture with
`bend 0` less the one with `waves 0` - of the six views of that measurement holds from
15.7 to 30.5 % of its power in its six strongest frequencies, against 6.1 to 12.7 % for
the same power with its directions made random.

The room for it. The crests cost about 45 instruction slots in the sheet's pixel
shader, whose depth variant stood at 511 of the 512 of ps_3_0. A split of `WaterPS` by
class was counted first on a scratch copy: without the foam and the whitecaps (a basin,
a river) the depth variant falls to 334, with the foam alone (a channel) it stands at
487, with both (a sea) at 511 - the split frees room only for the classes that do not
need it. The foam is separable: the sheet wrote the water's colour times 1 - foam and
the foam's times foam, the frame behind times 1 - foam, then the fog over both - with the
blend ONE / INVSRCALPHA that is the sheet without foam with a second premultiplied draw
of the same triangles over it, the fogged foam colour times foam with alpha foam. So the
foam left `WaterPS` (`hd_room.hlsl`, "the foam's draw"; the block under `HD_WATER_FOAM`)
and is drawn in its own pass, compiled from the same function with `HD_WATER_FOAM`
(`hd_room_water_foam_ps.inc`, `hd_room_water_foam_depth_ps.inc`), over every range of a
body whose bank foam or whitecap strength is above 0, from above, on the unmarked pixels
alone where the creatures' mark split the frame (`hd_render.cpp`, `draw_water_sheet`);
the sheet's own draw needs no split any more (its marked pixels drew without foam, and
it has none now). The only difference is the rounding of the first draw's result to the
render target's bits under the foam. RoomProbe's depth views draw no foam pass. The
mark's `WATERLOG` line ends `foam=` (the foam draws); RoomProbe prints `foam draw(s),
GPU <ms>`, which the sheet line does not count.

The pieces (`hd_room.hlsl` `CrestEnv`, `WaveSum8`; `hd_render.cpp` "the crests" over
`kWaterFan`). Every row's height runs along its own crest under an envelope (1 - C) +
2C g, g Wave2's curve of the place along the crest: a crest is a piece about two of the
row's wavelengths long - at most `kCrestReach`, 1,536 units, so a sea's 1,500- and
1,025-unit rows do not lay pieces longer than the pond is wide -, 1 + C high in its
middle and 1 - C between two, C the class's depth 0.8. The envelope's phase starts at
the golden angle times the row, so no two rows' pieces line up, and drifts along the
crest by 0.05 turns a second, the even rows one way and the odd the other. The slope
takes the envelope's rise along the crest as well, exact for the curve (24 C u (1 - |u|)
turns a unit times the step): it reaches 0.38 of a row's own slope at a piece's end
(0.8 x 0.955 / 2), too much to leave out. `WaterVS`'s swell takes the same envelope on
all eight rows, so the drawn crest and the lit one are one; `RiverPS`'s relief and the
foam's draw read the same sum. The constants are seven registers per sheet draw, pixel
c149 - c155 and vertex c168 - c174: per four rows the step along x and z in turns a unit
and the phase now, then 1 - C, 2C, 24C and the second bend's push.

The fan. The rows ranked by wavelength, longest first, lie at 0, 0.25, -0.375, 0.5,
-0.625, 0.75, -0.875 and 1.0 times the class's width round the body's own direction - a
channel's long axis, a river's flow, else the class's - the negative side half a step
further out, so no two rows are mirror images (their angles' sum stays an eighth of the
width off 0) and no two lie within a quarter of it, both also modulo pi, a crest's line
having no way. Basin width 1.5 (crest lines round 171 of 180 degrees - ripples from all
round a fountain): 260 at 0, 197 at 0.38, 150 at -0.56, 113 at 0.75, 85 at -0.94,
63 at 1.125, 47 at -1.31, 29 at 1.5 radians. Channel, sea and river 1.2 (crests mostly
across a canal, the wind's waves and a river's pieces across and askew to its current):
the longest at 0, then 0.3, -0.45, 0.6, -0.75, 0.9, -1.05, 1.2 - the channel's 420, 311,
230, 166, 120, 88, 64, 41, the sea's 1,500, 1,025, 700, 481, 330, 222, 150, 98, the

pieces slide downstream with the current; `RiverPS`'s relief light now draws pieces, and

RoomVS moves the remaster's marked water art with the first four of those, as before -

The bend and the glints. `WaveBend` gains a second push under the slow one: a pattern of

**The crests up close: no glints, pieces at no fixed step.** Asked for after the eleventh
play test (reference pictures supplied for this project, not in the repository): close
to the water it had become worse - the surface covered with a dense pattern of dots -,
from afar better, and the fountain had turned into a pattern of squares. The pictures:
ANDREA2's sewer canal from the walkway's edge, about 45 degrees down, its lit water under
a dense regular grid of small bright dots; the same canal from afar at eye level, fine;
the canal from above, the dot grid again; the fountain hall with the two waterfalls'
white feet, a fine square pattern on the water. What the tenth part was asked for stands
(short crest pieces in varying directions, fitting the current), and so does the far
look; the near look must lose every regular grid.

The cause, two parts. The glints: `WaterPS` multiplied the highlight by Wave2 along world
x times Wave2 along world z - a chequerboard aligned to the world's axes, its cell 1 /
(0.7 k) of the shortest row (58.6 units in a channel, 41 in a basin, 140 in a sea);
from afar a cell falls under a pixel, close by it is a grid of dots. Counted on the
pictures (each scaled to 1920 wide, the strongest bins of a 256-pixel tile's spectrum, at
three places on the canal): the owner's dots 19.1, 22.9 and 15.5 pixels apart at 117,
117 and 115 degrees, RoomProbe's view of that place (ANDREA2 19 "1900 3300 1000 15 50",
field of view 80) with the glints 16.8, 21.2 and 13.9 at 113, 114 and 112 - the same
with the waves' heights at 0, the glints alone - and the water of `2d48e83` none of
them. The pieces: each row's envelope was periodic along its crest, every piece of a row
of one length and the pieces of neighbouring crests in line, a fine grid of dashes of its
own where the rows are short. And the measure of the tenth part was blind to most of
the glints: it subtracts the picture with `waves 0` from the one with `bend 0`, and the
cells stand in both - on the canal close the glints' own picture holds 38.4 % of its
power in six bins (12.9 % without them), the measure read 9.7.

What changed (`hd_room.hlsl`). The glints are gone; the highlight is Blinn-Phong over
the waves' normal and nothing else. `CrestEnv` bends the place along each crest by two
slow curves of Wave2's kind fixed in the world: 0.15 of a turn deep at 0.37 of the
piece's frequency along the crest, 0.3 deep at 0.61 across it (`HD_CREST_ALONG`,
`HD_CREST_ACROSS`, `HD_CREST_WARP_A`, `HD_CREST_WARP_B`, starts in steps of 0.618 of a
turn). Along, a piece runs from 0.75 to 1.5 times its mean length and never folds back
(the bend moves the place by at most a third of its own rate); across, the next
crests' pieces stand up to 0.6 of a piece out of line. The envelope's rise is exact
with both curves (`growX`, `growZ`, the rise per turn times the gradient of the bent
place); at most 1.73 times the straight envelope's 0.38 of a row's slope. `WaterVS`'s
swell, the foam's draw and `RiverPS` read the same `WaveSum8`. The engine keeps every
number; its comment over `kWaterFan` names the curves and drops the glints from what
`crest` scales. The far look is kept (the canal at eye level from afar measures 17.6
against 16.4 and looks the same). Tried and dropped: 0.3 along (pieces up to three
times their mean, long streaks on ANDY3's pond, the bridge's view 23.0 against 18.5);
the four shortest rows straight (the lattice back: the canal close 15.1 against 11.1).
At the canal at eye level no lit lines return without the glints (11.5 against 11.3),
so nothing else was added. The fountain's basin needs no narrower fan: from above it
reads as ripples crossing from several places (D2 below), no cell repeats.

**The deck's plates, after the tenth play test.** The build of `2d48e83` was played
(reference pictures supplied for this project, not in the repository). On JOBY5's deck in
room 4 two of the five dry squares, 3,2 and 5,2, showed the void, nothing drawn; the other
three, 3,3, 4,3 and 5,3, showed their plates. The classic level lays faces with its water
texture on those squares, the Remaster deck plates on all five; the look wanted is the
plates on every square, with no stripes and no waves on the land.

The cause (`hd_render.cpp`, step 8 of `HDRenderSetWaterSheets`, "the art over a sheet"
:12077). The deck lies at the water's own height, 256, and its classic corners border the
water, so they carry the classic surface mark (`hd_level.cpp` `BuildWaterMarks`), and the
HD vertices at them and in their plane's flood are marked: every flat triangle of the
deck's plates counts as the Remaster's water art (`HDRange::artTris`). The plates of 3,2
and 5,2 are one draw call - part 0, material 0, page 537, 36 triangles, its box x 3,072 to
6,144 and z 2,048 to 3,072 at y 256 - and the hide asked whether the call's box reaches a
square whose sheet draws. It does: square 4,2 between the two plates is the notch of
water over room 144, where a sheet draws, and no triangle of the call lies over it
(`TrgProbe -squares 4 150 400 3 5 2 2`: 64 of 64 points at y 256 on 3,2 and on 5,2, none
on 4,2). So the whole call was hidden, and with the restored classic faces left out by
the sixth play test's dry-copy rule (the plates cover all five squares, so the faces
are a second copy of the floor) nothing drew there. The calls of 3,3 and 5,3 (page 538)
and of 4,3 (page 544) reach no sheet square and stayed. The hide came with the second
play test's part; until the sixth, the restored faces covered the hole with their
stripes.

The fix. A range keeps the floor squares its art triangles cover (`HDRange::artCells`
:1355, filled where `artTris` is counted :6439: the squares of each triangle's own box,
an edge on a square's line not counted, the rule of the flats), and the hide takes a
square only when it is one of them; the box stays as the first test (:12127). The deck's
call is kept: the five squares show the Remaster's plates, the dry faces stay left out,
and the flood's gate is unchanged, so no wave runs on the land. A call the box reaches
over a square none of its art triangles lies over is counted (`HDRange::artSpared`,
:12168).

The probe's marks. RoomProbe had no classic water marks: only `-plane` and `-roomplane`
hand it four, so every `-hdwater 1` picture so far counted only material 16 as water art
and in JOBY5 hid 36 triangles fewer than the game (15,906 against 15,942) - the probe
could not show the hole. `-watermarks` (with `-roombox`) builds the marks out of the
classic `.TRC` with a twin of `BuildWaterMarks` and of `drawroom.cpp`'s
`aRoomVertexWaterMarks` (the engine's functions walk `ROOM_INFO` and its globals and
cannot be linked into a tool) and prints the engine's `water marks=<n> rooms=<n>`. Held
against the owner's logs: JOBY5 1,531 marks in 15 rooms, 11,447 stamped and 8,358 flooded
vertices and 15 planes dropped, as in the game; ANDREA1, ANDY1, ANDY2, ANDY3, JOBY2, JOBY4

**The crests placed by a hash, after the twelfth play test.** Asked for after the
twelfth play test, with a picture of Lara swimming on ANDREA2's sewer canal seen from
above and behind her, about 55 degrees down, a crop of it and four photographs of real
water (reference pictures supplied for this project, not in the repository): the waves
keep to a square of their own, a constant pattern over the water, very noticeable; the
pattern is made of many quadrilaterals broken by squeezes; the photographs are the kind
of look wanted. In the picture the water round a walkway's corner is covered with knots
standing in quadrilaterals about a tenth of the picture wide, swirled together in
places. The photographs, in words: a field of wind ripples - countless short crests one
to three wavelengths long, nearly parallel within a patch, staggered like bricks, the
patches turned a little against each other, no line longer than a few wavelengths;
chop with sharp irregular crests, no two alike, its highlights broken into short
streaks; dark water with soft criss-crossing ripples, scaly, never a straight line and
never one cell twice; fine scaly chop. The far look of the canal at eye level stays as
accepted, and the crests are still to come from varying directions, fitting the current.

The cause. The quadrilaterals are not a square of the level's grid: seen from 2400 units
above, the canal's light repeats at no 1024-unit step. They are the beat of the long
rows: where two straight rows a few tens of degrees apart cross, their crests coincide
along a lattice whose cell is the difference of their wave vectors - for the channel's
rows 851 units (420 and 311), 411 (420 and 230) and 337 (311 and 230) -, and the
highlight and the reflection's lobe light those coincidences as knots. Counted in the
owner's picture (the band-passed brightness of the water left of Lara, its
autocorrelation): cells 188 and 160 pixels of 1600, about 330 and 280 units at his
distance - the 337 and 411 beats, the 851 one twice that, his square. The pieces of the
eleventh part did not break it: every piece kept its row's exact direction and phase, so
the knots stood where the straight rows put them. The squeezes are `WaveBend`'s two
periodic pushes: RoomProbe at the owner's view (ANDREA2 19 "2452 3514 2240 -6 52",
field of view 80) with `crest 0` shows the straight rows' lattice at its clearest, as
drawn it shows the knots swirled, and a probe build with both pushes out shows the pieces
standing in rows of dashes - the lattice without its squeezes; with the reflection's
stand-in pattern held at its mean nothing changes.

What changed (`hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_render.cpp`). Randomness comes from a hash of whole
cell numbers, never from a curve: `CellHash` takes the fractional parts of two sums of
products of two indices with multipliers n / 4096 - exact in single precision, so it
repeats after exactly 4096 cells and nowhere before, and precise anywhere in a level
because it is given cell numbers, not places. Each row of a sheet's eight is cut into
cells: across, three crests from trough to trough, numbered by the crests' own count -
the processor wraps a row's phase to three turns and hands the shader the whole cells
it has run (`kCrestAcross`, kept modulo 4096, `kCrestOffset` 977 apart from row to
row), so a crest keeps its cell while it travels; along, three of the row's wavelengths
(`crestLen` 3, at most `kCrestReach`), every other cell across moved along by half a
cell, so the cells stand like bricks. The hash of a cell gives its piece, a short train
of crests: a height of 0.4 to 1 times `kCrestGain` (6), a length of 1.5 to 3
wavelengths at a place in the cell, a lean of up to about 15 degrees (0.8 of a turn over
the cell, `HD_CREST_LEAN`) and a shift of up to 0.1 of a turn. The piece is the row's own
curve under two windows - along the piece and across the cell, each the smoothstep of a
tent, both 0 with their slopes at the cell's edges -, the lean and shift a shear of the
phase under the same windows (`CrestRows`); across, the middle crest weighs fully and
its two neighbours a quarter. No sine is evaluated beyond the row's own curve, and the
slope is exact for the pieces as drawn (checked against the numerical gradient on a
1024-square grid in a script: largest difference 0.002 against slopes up to 0.19). The
squeeze is one push along a value noise of the same hash (`WaveBend`): cells 1.5 of the
longest wavelength wide, along that row's direction, by up to 0.3 of its wavelength
(`kBendPush`), drifting 0.031 and -0.023 cells a second. With `crest 0` the pieces and
the squeeze are gone: the straight rows, unbent. The two slow curves over the pieces,
their drift along the crest and both periodic pushes are gone; the fan stays. The rows'
phases and heights go to the shaders four to a register (c156 - c159, vertex c175 -
c178), which spares gathering them. Where the slots or the time do not stretch, the
pieces keep no lean and shift: `RiverPS` (which also takes no squeeze), the underside's
and the views' variants and the foam's draw (0.02 ms dearer with the lean over a screen
of sea). `WaterVS`'s swell takes the same pieces at a gain of 1 (`kCrestSwellGain`):
at 6 a long row's trough sank ANDY3's pond under the ground beside the island.

The numbers and their reasons. The cell three crests across: one crest a cell drew every
piece as a round bump, the sheet pitted from above (the owner's view and a numerical
model of the sum). No cell left empty: with a sixth empty the water showed flat
stretches with single dimples. The gain: 4.49 keeps a row's mean square (0.52 the
heights', 0.258 and 0.371 the two windows'); at 4.49 the pieces read faint against the
floor seen through the water, 6 by eye. The lengths, the lean, the shift, the bricks'
half cell, the squeeze's cell, push and drift are free choices, set by eye on the
round's RoomProbe pictures. The hash's constants passed a count on 128 x 128 cells at
three places up to (4000, 6000): even over 64 bins (chi square 41 to 82 on 63 degrees
of freedom), neighbours correlated by under 0.03, the spectrum flat (its largest bin 8
to 14 times the mean); a sine hash of the same cells kept an eighth of its values
distinct.

**The splash and the tank, the water's own.** Asked for: an HD splash where Lara dives
(a short burst of cards on the remaster's spray pages and one large ring on the sheet,
the answer chosen for the dive splash, 2026-10-10), and of RICH2's fish tanks, with a
video of the room (supplied for this project, not in the repository): the water that
comes out - can it be HD like our water? It was still the classic look.

What was classic. A dive into water (`Splash`, game\effects.cpp; Lara wading in,
`WadeSplash`; an explosion under water, game\lara1gun.cpp) calls `SetupSplash`
(game\effect2.cpp), whose struct `UpdateSplashes` grows tick by tick - three rings of a
radius and a size, an inner and a middle column that rise and fall, a life of 62 that
runs out two a tick once the inner column is back at the surface - and
`S_DrawSplashes` (specificfx.cpp) draws as additive sprite rings at twice the struct's
radius and an eighth of its height. A fish tank (FISHTANK, slot 413), once broken, runs
`ControlFishtank` (game\tower.cpp): every tick 5 or 4 points of `SplashOffsets` along
the tank's front, through joint 0, each one spark of `TriggerFishtankSpray` - grey,
additive, 14 to 17 ticks, rising 8 to 15 units a tick (its gravity is negative), a
radius growing from 64..95 to 256..380 units - while `item_flags[1]` falls from 4096 by
a 64th a tick: 105 ticks, 3.5 s, then `KillItem`. The floor lasers of its room
(FLOOR_LASERS, slot 392) hold `trigger_flags` at 64 while it runs (`GetFishTank`) and
count it down to 0 after it (2.13 s); `S_DrawFloorLasers` draws them as red quads only,
random while that count runs - the lasers shorting in the water, not a wet floor.
RICH2 holds two tanks: item 33 in room 23 over floor lasers (item 34, 4 x 4 squares)
and item 182 in room 122, which has none. The tank's mesh itself, scaled in height by
`item_flags[1]` (`DrawScaledSpike`, game\traps.cpp), is the large dome of water in the
video; it is not part of this round.

What it is now, with `tomb5.hd_water` on (`hd_render.cpp`, "the cards" and "the tank's
film"; the arithmetic in `hd_splash_math.h`, all of it a function of the age alone).
The splash and the spray ask for `tomb5.hd_motion` as well: without it `HDWaterSplash`
and `HDWaterSpray` (hd_level.cpp) return false at their first test and the classic
sprites draw, as with `hd_water` 0; the film needs `hd_water` alone. A splash over a
drawing sheet (the ripples' test: a sheet under it within 256 units of
height) is taken by `HDWaterSplash` from `SetupSplash`, which marks the struct with bit
0x10; `S_DrawSplashes` then leaves its sprites out. The struct runs on as before -
nothing reads it but the classic draw. The HD form steps the struct's own numbers
(`HDSplashAt`, line for line `UpdateSplashes`, drawn on linearly between ticks): two
rings on the sheet, through the sheets' own rings (`gather_rings`), their fronts the
classic middle and outer rings' outer edges and their strengths 1.0 and 0.6 of the
classic life - a free choice, set by eye on the round's RoomProbe pictures, twice the
0.5 a wading Lara's ring starts with; a crown of 12 cards on the inner ring and 16 on
the middle one, each at its column's height times 0.7 to 1.0 and read at 0.85 to 1.15 of
the splash's time from its own seed, as wide as the two rings' widths over two (24 to
160 units) and as tall as its column, at least half as tall as wide - a low haze once
the column is back -, leaning up to 0.3 radians, its share the classic life; and 24
drops thrown from the inner ring with 0.5 to 1.1 times the column's first speed and 0.5
to 1.5 times the ring's speed outward, under the column's own gravity (`InnerYVel`
grows by 0x400 a tick and moves the struct by a 16th, drawn an 8th: 8 units a tick
squared, 7200 units/s^2), gone when they are back at the surface. Counts, shares,
widths and lean are free choices, set by eye on the round's RoomProbe pictures. Lara's
dive at a fall speed of 128 lives 1.5 s; a faster fall a longer one, a wading splash a
smaller one, as with the classic struct.

A spark of a tank's spray is taken by `HDWaterSpray` from `TriggerFishtankSpray`,
after the classic spark is made, which marks it `SF_UNUSED2` (set by nothing else);
`S_DrawSparks` leaves it out. Its card moves as the classic spark does - the same
recurrences (`HDTankPuff`) with this file's hash where the game rolls
`GetRandomControl`, so the game's random stream is untouched - and its share is 0.35
times the strength over 64 (a free choice, by eye). The spray points stand on the floor
(joint 0 lies at the item's height less 1 unit), so nothing falls from them: the cards
rise as the classic mist does.

The film. The floor the tank floods gets a thin sheet of this water: per FLOOR_LASERS
item sharing its room with a FISHTANK, its box as `InitialiseFloorLasers` lays it, a
basin body of its own, at rest 8 units over the lasers' floor (`kFilmHair`, about 2 cm
at 2.3 mm a unit, a free choice under the lasers' 128), 5 x 5 vertices a square, the
shore the distance to the box's edge, in the group of the room and of its flipmap
partner (RICH2 room 23 and 32). Its depth byte, in the sheets' 32-unit steps, is 0 (8
over 32, rounded down); only the variant without the depth texture reads that byte,
and to it the film has no depth. It is built after the level's own bodies and is no
water square for anything else: not counted, not in the WATERLOG lines, no ring
source, no ripple gate, no hidden art, no eye under it, no caustic (a room's caustic
lights its whole floor at every moment). Its strength a frame (`HDFilmStrength`, read
off the items by `FeedWaterFilms`, hd_level.cpp): while the tank runs (4096 -
`item_flags[1]`) / 1024, at most 1 - up over 19 ticks, 0.63 s, as the water pours out;
after it the lasers' own count over 64, dry with them; 0 before. The strength sets
three things. The blend factor (SRCBLEND BLENDFACTOR, DESTBLEND INVBLENDFACTOR): with
the frame's copy bound, `WaterPS` writes the water and the floor behind it whole, alpha
1, so that blend is an exact cross-fade between the film and the floor; without the
copy the film is not drawn, and a dry film asks for no copy. The height: the surface
stands 16 units (`kFilmRise`, about 4 cm, a free choice, set by eye on the round's
RoomProbe pictures) times the strength over its rest, through `WaterVS`'s crest lift
(`gSwell` z, with w so low that every vertex takes all of it), tapering in from the
edge over the basin's 512 units and still while `tomb5.hd_motion` is off - deepest
while the tank pours, sinking as the lasers' count runs down; a deeper film bends and
darkens the floor seen through it more. The rim: the film's edge takes a channel's bank
foam (`kWaterClass`'s channel row, strength 0.7 and band 300 units), its strength times
the film's, in the foam's own draw - a density, so the rim thins as the film fades. No
shader changes for either: both are the sheets' constants. The film's clip is 0, not
the bodies' 8: at 8, its own rest height, it lost a band in front of the tank's plinth
where the frame lies less than 8 units under its surface (RoomProbe `-tank 33 1.5` at
960 x 540, the film at rest: 73,132 pixels differ from the dry view with the clip 8,
84,559 with 0). The lasers' red draw is not touched - it is the lasers', and the film
lies under it. The tank in room 122 gets the spray and no film: it has no floor lasers.

The cards (`CardVS`, `CardPS` in `hd_room.hlsl` under `HD_CARD`, which alone declares

eye, projected alone; a window of a remaster page - spray 3242 and 3243, drops 3160,

cut round (one less the squared radius, squared), faded over 64 units against the

for the light spray catches in the air, a free choice by eye - the page gives the
shape, the water its colour. At most 512 cards a frame: four splashes at their peak
are 208, a tank's spray at most 85 cards (4.5 sparks a tick for 17 ticks). Drawn once

**What the prover found.** Five findings, each answered. The film's 41 to 63 ms
bracket, left unexplained (medium): measured to its cause, a one-time wait of the
process's first sheet draw that is older than this round (Measured); no code change.
The film's height did not follow the tank and its edge had no foam (medium): the
height now rises with the strength, the rim takes a channel's bank foam, and the
film's clip is 0 (the film, above) - the clip's band was found while measuring the
height. The film's "8 deep" never reached the shader (low): its depth byte is 0, and
the comment, this entry and the ledger say so. The spray in the tank view barely shows
(low): the owner's to judge (Left). The switch named only `hd_water` where the splash
and the spray need `hd_motion` too (low): this entry and the manual name both. The
diff reaches past the files the round was given (low): `specificfx.cpp` (the classic
draws the two gates skip), `hd_level.cpp` and `hd_level.h` (the hooks in
`BuildWaterSheets` and `HDFrameDrawGlow`), the new `hd_splash_math.h`, and thirteen
`.inc` files whose stamp line alone changed - the places a merge with the other rounds
of the night meets first (Left). After the fix the classic path 3 of 3, `-hdwater 0`
15 of 15, `-hdwater 1` without splash or tank 15 of 15 and the dry tank view 1 of 1
identical as before, all 209 WATERLOG lines of the fifteen levels identical to

**Round 2: the shot, the spray, the dome, the warm-up.** Asked for after the play test of
the evening of 2026-10-11 (the build of `4f725a8`): all in all a result to be very pleased
with - but the splash when the tank is shot is still SD, while the water that comes out at
the lasers in RICH2 is HD already and looks good. Answered that evening: the spray
stronger, yes; the dome in HD next, yes; a warm-up draw at the load against the first
water frame's hitch, yes.

What the shot is. His pictures show the tank of RICH2 room 122 (item 182, the one without
floor lasers), seen from in front of its glass; the log's tank shots (`SMASH_GLASS` and
`EXPLOSION1` on one tick, at 606609, 655000 and 669406) put the first at that tank, its
`SPLASHLOG` lines then `tank=-1:0.00` (no film). Lara's shot (`FireWeapon` ->
`GetTargetOnLOS`, game\control.cpp) only shatters the glass, a shatter static (slot 50;
RoomProbe `-statictable`: RICH2 room 23 mesh 0 and room 122 mesh 0): glass debris, two
ricochet sparks, and the next tick the trigger under the glass starts the FISHTANK. The
white cloud in front of the glass is the FISHTANK's own mesh, drawn by `DrawScaledSpike`
(game\traps.cpp) and scaled in height by `item_flags[1]` / 4096 - the dome the previous
part left: one mesh of 69 vertices and 104 quads (MeshDump, a script of this round, on the
classic rich2.trc), texture 52 scrolled by `AnimateWaterfalls`, half of its quads
additive; a flat top 1,276 over the floor behind the glass (local z -1540 to -516) and a
curved apron from the glass's top edge down to the floor 866 units in front of it (profile
z, y: -516, -1276; -286, -1236; -57, -1118; 115, -930; 233, -685; 307, -382; 350, 6),
2,140 wide at the top and 3,186 at the floor - Lara, in front of the glass in his picture,
stands inside it. Whole on the first tick, 0.198 of its height at the 105th, gone on the
106th (3.53 s): two pops. It is not the spray: the spray is `TriggerFishtankSpray`'s
sparks, cards since the previous part, rising from the apron's foot (`SplashOffsets` local
z 52 to 324, under the foot at 350). So the shot's SD look and the dome are one thing;
this part builds the dome's HD form and adds the burst at the break the classic has none
of.

The shot, the burst (`HDTankBurst`, hd_splash_math.h). On the tank's first ticks its water
is thrown out of the opened glass: 40 spray cards and 24 drops, each leaving the glass
(`glassZ`) at a height spread evenly over the opening and a place across the top's width,
at its own moment within 0.2 s (6 ticks), out of the glass at the speed water leaves an
opening under a column of its own depth, sqrt(2 g (height - h0)) (Torricelli) times 0.6 to
1.0, up or down by up to 400 units/s, under g = 4300 units/s^2 (9.81 m/s^2 at 2.3 mm a
unit); gone back on the floor or after 1 s. From RICH2's 1,276 the fastest leave at 3,310
units/s and land at most 1,276 units out (2 sqrt(d h) at d = h), the apron's own reach. A
spray card widens to 2.5 times its size as it flies and fades with the share of its flight
left; a drop stays whole. The counts, the time, the lift, the life and the sizes are free
choices, set by eye on the round's RoomProbe pictures. The tank's shape comes from its
classic mesh (`HDTankShapeOf`: the top and the floor, the glass as the furthest z within
32 units of the top - `kTankBand`, which takes RICH2's top vertices at -1276 and -1277 and
its floor ones at 6 and none of the next rows at -1239 and -382 -, the foot's reach, the
widths), handed to the renderer at load by the engine (`TankMeshToRenderer`, hd_level.cpp,
out of `mesh_vtxbuf`) and by RoomProbe (out of the .TRC's bytes) alike. The tank is handed
in each frame by the classic draw (`DrawScaledSpike` -> `HDWaterTank`), so the HD form
draws exactly when the classic one does; its age is its ticks out of `item_flags[1]`
(`HDTankTicksOf`, the first step count at or under it), run on smoothly by the frame's
clock and held within the tick the game is in. A film for the laser-less tank of room 122
out of the apron's footprint (2 x 4 squares before its glass) was built and dropped: in
his view at 2560 x 1440 it cost 0.20 ms over `4f725a8` (sheet 0.098, copy 0.017, foam
0.063), more than the round's bound of 0.15 (Left).

The spray. In his view the spray touched 14.9 % of the picture at 1 s, the brightness of
those pixels up by 24; in the view of room 23's tank 1 % (RoomProbe `-tank` with and
without `-tankleave spray`, 1920 x 1080). Why so little: a card stood round its spark's
point, and the spark starts on the floor (joint 0 lies 1 unit over the item), so half of
each card lay under the floor and the rest within the soft edge's 64 units of it - and
room 23's spray points lie inside the 256 high step before its glass; the share was 0.35,
times the page's alpha (mean 0.40, DdsProbe) and the round cut (mean 0.26 over the quad):
about 0.036. Now the card stands on its point, its lower edge there, at a share of 0.8
(`kTankSprayShare`), the dive splash's middle crown ring's: the spray is the same water
thrown up. The film's rise and rim are as they were.

The dome (`HDTankDomeAt`, `HDTankDomePoint`, `HDTankDomeShare`; hd_render.cpp, "the tank's
water"). The HD path draws the mesh itself and `DrawScaledSpike` leaves the classic one
out (`if (item->object_number == FISHTANK && HDWaterTank(item)) return;`, game\traps.cpp;
`item_flags[1]` runs on as before, nothing of the game changes): every quad as two
triangles, every vertex scaled in y as the classic scales it, by the tank's own ticks run
on linearly between them (1.0 down to 0.198); the apron drawn out of the glass over 0.25 s
(866 units at 3,460 units/s, the 3,310 the burst leaves at); the whole in over 2 ticks and
out over the 0.5 s before KillItem's tick, so it neither pops in nor out (both free
choices). It goes through the cards' shaders as they are - no shader changes: `CardVS` 9
slots, `CardPS` 35, every `.inc` as at `4f725a8` - with the corner at 0, so the round cut
is whole: a see-through sheet whose share is 0.15 where the eye looks through it and up to
0.65 where it looks along it, (1 - |cos|)^2 between, the angle out of the mean of its
quads' normals in view space taken across their diagonals (a quad's winding does not
matter); the remaster's spray page 3243 stretched 384 units across and 2,048 down, so its
blotches draw out into streaks, running down the water at 1,660 units/s, half the speed of
a fall of the dome's height (sqrt(2 g 1,282) / 2); tinted as the cards of that tank are,
premultiplied, soft against the frame's depth, before the cards. The first look, 0.3 and a
page every 512 units both ways, stood as a blotched cloud over the room. Shares, lengths
and fades are free choices, set by eye on the round's RoomProbe pictures.

The warm-up (`HDRenderWaterWarmUp`, hd_render.cpp, "the warm-up"). The first draw of a
water sheet in a process waits about 42 ms (the previous part). Measured with scratch
timers round each draw, to the GPU's end (never committed; RICH2's tank view, 2560 x
1440): the first sheet draw 41.9, 42.7 and 43.9 ms, the next 0.36 to 0.49 and 0.10; the
first frame copy 0.8 to 1.1, the first card draw 2.6 to 3.1. Drawn first with the rooms'
vertex shader, the sheet's pixel shaders took 0.41 to 0.72 ms (`WaterDepthPS`) and 0.05 to
0.16 (`WaterPS`); then the first draw with `WaterVS` 60 to 73 ms; the sheet buffers'
upload (`PreLoad`) 0.37 to 0.91 ms. So the wait is the driver readying the water's vertex
shader (386 slots) on its first use. Now, once a level, after the sheets are built and the
depth texture is bound (one call in `BuildWaterSheets`, the only touch of the sheets'
path), each of the water's seven pixel shaders draws one triangle of the level's first
sheet range with `WaterVS` - declaration and textures as the frame binds them - and the
cards' pair one card, into a 16 x 16 target of their own without a depth buffer, the queue
drained after each, the device's state put back; nothing reaches the frame. A new line
with `-log`: `HDLOG level=<stem> water warm-up <ms> ms: sheet <ms>, depth <ms>, under
<ms>, foot <ms>, river <ms>, foam <ms>, foam depth <ms>, cards <ms>`. RoomProbe warms the
same way after its own depth bind (`-nowarm` leaves it out) and prints its frame's time on
the processor from BeginScene to the GPU's end.

`SPLASHLOG` gains `tanks=<n>` at its end, the breaking tanks whose water the frame drew,
and is written while one draws. RoomProbe: `-tank` draws the tank's water while the tank
runs, `-tankleave spray|water` leaves a part out.

RoomProbe's frame also holds the rooms' own first draw (29 to 44 ms, the rooms' vertex

**Round 3: the wet floor and the barrel's rings.** Asked for, put into English: an idea
for the aquariums - room 23's lowered area and rooms 122, 121, 45 and 46: after the shot
the floor gets a gloss, to show that it is wet (proposed on 2026-10-11, ordered on
2026-10-13: the wet gloss, yes, let us do it). And after the play test of 2026-10-13: the
barrel's rings are barely visible; he had to look from very close, at one angle, to see
that they had arrived at all.

What the classic game does to those floors. Nothing: `ControlFishtank` sprays for 105
ticks and `KillItem` takes the tank (`IFL_CLEARBODY`, its status left `ITEM_ACTIVE`); a
loaded game kills a shot tank with `ITEM_DEACTIVATED`. The floors (`SectorCheck` on the
classic `rich2.trc`): room 122 has a 2 x 2 floor at y 0 between doors, its east column the
tank's own room 22 at -256; rooms 121 and 45 have y 0 squares beside raised blocks at -768
and stairs at -256 and -512; room 46 is a corridor of 2 x 18 squares at y 0 (a drop of
1,536 into room 42 in its south wall row), room 113 two squares off it at y 0. Room 23 has
its lowered area at -2560 (the 4 x 4 middle and two more squares), the plinth step at
-2816 before the glass and -2816 doors and steps round it; its flipmap twin 32 opens the
tank's side. The dome's apron (the previous part) lands on the floor in the tank's frame
between the glass and its foot: at tank 182 world x 48,290 to 49,156 and z 67,014 to
70,200, four squares at y 0 of rooms 122, 45 and 121.

Which floor gets wet (`hd_render.cpp`, "the wet floor", `build_wet_floors`). The squares
under the apron's foot, and from there every flat square at the same height or one click
lower, across rooms by world square - water runs level and down a step, never up one,
never down a drop into another room, never behind the glass into the tank. So a room with
a higher dry part keeps it dry. RICH2: tank 182 wets 50 squares at y 0 of rooms 122, 121,
45, 46 and 113 (the raised blocks and stairs of 121 and 45 stay dry; the `rooms=` list of
the load line also names the rooms whose door squares lie there), tank 33 its plinth and
the lowered area of room 23, 14 squares at two heights.

When. A grid of points every 256 units over those squares (25 a square, shared), each with
its way from the glass - the shortest run over the grid, diagonals at their length, a step
down at no cost - pushed back by up to 384 units out of a hash of its place, so the front
is ragged; a second hash sets how much of the mirror the water's depth there gives (0.5 to
1). The front (`HDWetFront`, hd_splash_math.h) comes out with the apron (866 units in 0.25
s) and runs on at 321 units/s, sqrt(g h) at the tank's film's 24 units (8 at rest and 16
of rise) - the speed a wave runs in water that shallow, 0.74 m/s; a point is wet a quarter
square behind it (`HDWetAt`). Tank 182's furthest point lies 19,749 units along the way:
the corridor's far end is wet after about a minute. The state each frame (`FeedWaterWet`,
hd_level.cpp, as the films read the tank): 1 while `ControlFishtank` runs it, its age out
of `item_flags[1]`; 2 once `KillItem` took it - the floor stays wet; a tank first seen
shot, as a loaded game has it, is wet all over at once. 0 whole. It does not dry (a
question for the owner, under Left). With `tomb5.hd_motion` 0 nothing runs: the front
stands past every point and the floor is wet all over from the frame the tank breaks. The
run is motion, the wet floor is the game's state - the tank is shot - as the film's
strength is, which with motion off keeps following the tank and its lasers while only its
rise stands still; the dome is the classic one then, and the floor under it is wet.

How it is drawn. Once a frame in `HDFrameDrawGlow`, over the opaque frame and before the
sheets' copy, a layer 4 units over the floor (about 1 cm; the depth buffer resolves 1.2
units at 20,000) through the cards' vertex shader and a pixel shader of its own
(`hd_wet.hlsl`, `WetPS`, 178 slots, `hd_wet_ps.inc`), premultiplied: the floor behind kept
by one less 0.3 times the wet, and a mirror weighted by Schlick's Fresnel at water's F0 of
0.02. The mirror is the frame itself where a ray reflected in the floor, marched in screen
space (12 steps from 32 units, each 1.5 times the last, about 8,200 units), finds what the
frame drew - the copy of the opaque frame the sheets read, taken here, its clip at 1
undone as Reinhard's curve x / (1 - x) held at 8, since a mirror of a few hundredths shows
a bright source and little else -, else the light field's colour times the polished walls'
0.35; over both the lamps as the field's Blinn-Phong highlight at exponent 128 with the
textbook normalisation (n + 8) / 8, all held softly under the walls' cap of 0.75, and the
distance fog as the cards take it. Where the frame lies more than 32 units under the layer
(a drain, a gap of the art) it fades out over the next 32. A floor wholly out of the view
is left out, its copy with it. The first look without the mirror only darkened the floor:
in his view the field's highlight is nothing, the lamps overhead and his eye 25 to 38
degrees over the floor put the half vector 26 to 32 degrees off its normal ((cos)^128
about 1e-6); with the mirror and the clip kept, the vending machines' reflection changed
the floor by 8 levels at most; undone, by up to 66.

Why not the gloss variant. Measured: the floors' pages (1047, 1049, 1053, 1079, 1029) name
no sheen (`TrgProbe -gloss`), 1047 is a clear page and room 46's floor is a clear floor of
the blend phase, which the gloss variant never draws; a wet strength there needed the room
build's ranges split by face, two more slots for the darkening (507 to 509), a whole
range's strength at once (no front), and its sheen is held under 2.5 times the surface's
own lit colour - a dark marble floor cannot take a water mirror that way. The tank's film
over the same floor cost 0.20 ms in his view (the previous part).

`SPLASHLOG` gains `floor=<item>:<wet>` at its end (the first tank whose floor is wet, the
mean wet of its points), and the line comes once a second while that water still runs out;
the load writes one `SPLASHLOG level=<stem> wet tank=<item> squares=<n> rooms=<list>
heights=<n> points=<n> tris=<n> reach=<units> far=<units>` line a tank. RoomProbe draws
the wet floor with `-tank` and holds it at a strength with `-tankwet <0..1>`. With
`tomb5.hd_water` 0 nothing of it is built.

The barrel's rings (`hd_render.cpp`, "the rings", `kRingBody`; `HDRingStrength`,
hd_splash_math.h). Measured first with RoomProbe `-life 1 -liferings game` at ANDY3's lake
at night, a barrel's ring of 249 seen from the bank at 700, 1,500 and 3,000 units and 450
to 1,600 over the water, 960 x 540, 0.1 to 2 s after it starts: 0 to 3,074 pixels changed
by more than 4 of 255, against 0 to 2,575 for a wading Lara's ring of 120 at the same
place and age. Why so faint: a ring is a slope, and at night the water mirrors a dark sky
nearly alike at every slope - the ring showed only where its slope turned the mirror to
the brighter horizon; its strength was capped at a size of 128 (240 to 255 counted as 128)
and falls with the square of its life (0.51 of it at 1 s), where a wading Lara's ring is
started again every 0.6 s and stays young. Now a ring that starts over 128 - only the
water's life's floats start one - counts its size past 128 and is 4 times stronger; at 2
the ring did not read from Lara's camera, at 4 it does at 1.5 and 2 s. At the ring's start
its slope stands far steeper than a real wave's, so near the barrel it reads as an
outline. A ring that starts at 128 or less keeps its strength to the bit; nothing of the
water's life changes, and no shader.

**Measured.** His view (RICH2 room 122, the eye of pictures 137 and 138, `-tank 182`),
2560 x 1440, five runs, the water's phases and the wet floor summed: at 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 s
0.075, 0.073, 0.069 and 0 ms at `ba89a58f`, 0.137, 0.137, 0.140 and 0.070 after (+0.062 to
+0.071; the floor 0.044 to 0.055 of it, the copy 0.017). The room 23 tank's view: at 1.5
and 10 s 0.227 and 0 ms at `ba89a58f`, 0.67 to 1.49 and 0.30 to 0.80 after, the floor's
bracket 0.27 to 1.26. A scratch timer round the floor's draw call alone (never committed):
its first draw of the frame 0.33 to 0.78 ms there, the same draw again right after it
0.031 ms; in his view 0.035 to 0.044 ms the first time. Not the copy (the first draw with
no copy bound as slow), not the shader's first use alone (a warm-up draw with the march
running cut it to 0.20 to 0.33); without the march (`-nocopy`) 0.027 ms. Pixels at 960 x
540, the lower half: his view at 10 s 124,231 changed by more than 4 (116,686 darker,
7,545 brighter, up to +63), its luma 52.2 to 46.4; the room 23 view at 10 s 77,350 (70,969
darker, 6,381 brighter); at 1 and 3 s there the tank's film still covers the floor. The
barrel's ring after: 242 to 20,334 pixels over 4 (lake, the six views), the wading Lara's
ring's 30 counts identical. Slots: `WetPS` 178 (8 texture, 170 arithmetic); every other
`.inc` byte-identical; `RoomPS` and its gloss variant 510 and 507 as they were.

**Checked.** The classic path 6 of 6 md5-identical to `8691e82` (ANDREA2 19 and 231, JOBY2
42 and 66, ANDY3 17 and 34, `-classicroom` and `-classiconly`). With `-hdwater 0` the
fifteen cameras 15 of 15 identical to the fix round's parity set. With `-hdwater 1`
against a RoomProbe built from `ba89a58f`: the fifteen cameras 15 of 15, the pond's twelve
views at 1, 3 and 5 s 36 of 36, the canal dive 4 of 4, the tank views without `-tank` and
his view before the break 3 of 3, the sweep's 209 WATERLOG lines; with `-life 1 -liferings
game` at 9 s the pond's twelve views 5 identical and 7 changed where a barrel's ring is.
ModernTest grows by 11 checks (the front, the wet, the corridor's minute; Lara's ring as
before, the barrel's past 128 and four times); the suites 0 failed; the engine and every
tool build. The motion rule, his view and the room 23 view at 0, 1, 3 and 10 s: with
motion on 8 of 8 pictures md5-identical to the build before it; with `-nomotion` 8 of 8
identical to the same build held at `-tankwet 1`, and against the build before it his
