seconds there before), at 10 s identical.

**Left.** The look and the timing in the game - nobody in this round could play it. The
floor does not dry: whether it should, over minutes, is the owner's to say. The room 23
view's first floor draw of a frame took 0.3 to 0.8 ms in RoomProbe, a second one 0.03;
the cost is not the same in every process: in five fresh RoomProbe runs at 2560 x 1440
the room 23 view at 10 s drew its floor in 0.631, 0.467, 0.384, 0.062 and 0.437 ms, the
corridor of room 46 at 120 s in 0.496, 0.084, 0.328, 0.084 and 0.427 - a cost of the
process's first use or the card's clock rather than of each frame, which only the game's
FPSLOG in rooms 23 and 46 after the shot can settle; if the game pays it every frame, the
march can be cut to the pixels it can change. The mirror shows only what the frame shows:
what stands off the screen does not mirror, and toward the screen's edge it fades. A
tank's film over the floor reads the copy taken before the floor was drawn wet, and so
shows the floor under it dry while it lasts. The barrel's ring at 3,000 units stays small;
its strength and the outline near the barrel are the owner's to judge. For the water's
life: the comment over the barrel's ring in `hd_life_rules.h` (at line 1867 to 1871) still
says its strength on the sheet is that of a wading Lara's ring of 128; since `kRingBody` a
ring of 240 to 255 draws 7.5 to 8 times that (`HDRingStrength` 3.75 against 0.5 for a
ring of 240 at its start). The file is that part's, so its comment is left to it.

**Commits.** `4d8b54ce`, `95bf8151`, `584642bd` (the wet floor with `hd_motion` off),
`bf7d5a30` (a shader comment, the bytecode unchanged).

**The water's life.** Asked for on 2026-10-09: a little more life in the water - now and
then small fish that flee from Lara, oil drifting through the sewers at random, and
whatever else comes to mind. Two reference pictures supplied for this project (not in
the repository) show what floating things mean here: JOBY5's flooded galley with small
objects on the surface, slightly bobbing, and ANDY1's planks, which the level already
has as HD models. The first round of it was built on 2026-10-11 beside the water
sheets, which another round changed at the same time; nothing of the sheets' look,
tables or draw changed here.

*The thirteen questions of the design round, with the choices this round built on - to
be confirmed or changed by the owner:*

- D1 where: only dirty water - ANDREA2's sewer canal, ANDY3's river and ponds, ANDY1's
  pools (a), with the sets chosen per section (c).
- D2 how many: counts fixed in a table, places rolled at level load with
  `GetRandomDraw`, no save (c).
- D3 the bob: a float drifts with the current and bobs on a curve of its own (b); the
  exact bob on the sheet's eight rows (a) needs their sum on the processor and is left.
- D4 the gathering: floats collect at banks and grates on a canal or a basin (a), and
  ride a river's conveyor from its upstream row to its end (c).
- D5 the fish: a school of 4 to 8 `FISH2`, rigid, with a yaw wobble, fleeing Lara (a).
- D6 oil and D7 fireflies and midges: not this round.
- D8 the drips: rolled ceiling points that ring the sheet (a).
- D9 the pieces: whole models only (a); the crate of ANDREA2 and the cans cut out of
  JOBY5's shelf art are left.
- D10 the pool: item-less, drawn through the HD objects' list (b).
- D11 light shafts and D12 the dive's splash: another round.
- D13 the first round: the pool with the floats, the fish and the drips in the three
  levels (a).

How. `specific/hd/hd_life_rules.h` holds the tables and every rule as pure functions,
which the engine, RoomProbe and ModernTest share; `specific/hd/hd_life.cpp` is the
engine's side; the water module hands a body's squares out through one read-only getter.

- *The models* (`kHDLifeKinds`, `hd_life_rules.h:62`): `BOTTLE`, `WET_CLOTH`,
  `CLOTH_RICH2_RICH1`, `ANIMATING3_ANDY1` from `5\ITEM` and `FISH2` from `4\ITEM`,
  found by name through the model resolver into synthetic slots `0x7800` and up, put
  into the level's one model list after Lara's wardrobe (`HDLifeModelPlan`,
  `hd_life.cpp:133`, called at `hd_object.cpp:1998`), preloaded with every other model.
  Their boxes give the floating heights 80 (a bottle on its side), 16 (the cloths), 326
  (a barrel on its side) and 70 (the fish) and the reach across the water, half the
  box's diagonal seen from above (`HDLifeReach`, 242 for the barrel). `FISH2`'s head
  points toward +x: `ModelProbe -name FISH2` from the side and from above (`-yaw 0`,
  `-pitch 0` and `90`, +x to the right) shows the eye on that end.
- *Where* (`kHDLifeLevels`, `:97`; `HDLifeTakes`): ANDREA2 the channel bodies of 16
  squares or more (the canal, 44 squares; its fountain basins stay clean), weights
  bottle 4, green cloth 3, ochre cloth 3, barrel 1, no fish; ANDY3 every river of three
  squares or more and its bodies of eight squares or more, ANDY1 its bodies of eight or
  more, both ochre cloth (a dead leaf) 4, green cloth 1, barrel 1, and a school. One
  float for three of a body's squares with water under them (a floor at the surface
  counts none), twelve a body (`HDLifeCount`): twelve keeps three bodies inside the 32
  HD entries the life draws a frame at most, a quarter of the frame's 128
  (`HD_OBJ_ITEMS`), of which Lara takes 6 to 10; two barrels a body at most. Places a
  quarter square inside a square deep enough for the kind (*the depth*), so a quarter
  square from any bank.
- *The drift* (`HDLifeFloatTick`, `:1071`): the body's current (the sheets' `flow` and
  `speed`) plus a wander of 60 units a second, its way a hash of the float and the
  clock's 4-second step blended over the step (never a random per frame); the yaw turns
  toward the way at 40 degrees a second. A step that would bring the float nearer to a
  bank, or to water too shallow for it, than its reach (128 at least) is refused, the x
  or z part alone is tried - so a float slides along a bank (`HDLifeStep`, `:369`) - and
  a float a bank holds tries again after 6 to 9 seconds. On a river a float a quarter
  square past the middle of the last row downstream, or held by a bank, comes back
  with a kind rolled again on an upstream square deep enough for that kind
  (`HDLifeUpstreamSquare`, `:507`; any square of the body that is when none upstream
  is).
- *The bob* (`HDLifeBobAmp`, `:568`; `HDLifeFits`, `:558`): a sine of the clock, 2.5
  to 4 seconds and a phase of its own, a quarter of the floating height but never more
  than the body's sheet rises and never more than the draft leaves over that rise;
  tilts of 3 and 2 degrees on the same curve. A kind floats on a body only where its
  draft (bottle 0.5, cloth 0.7, barrel 0.45 of the height) reaches deeper than the
  sheet falls. The rise comes from the getter: the class's swell share times its eight
  rows' heights (their envelope is at most one), a quarter more where the class has
  whitecaps - 0 in a basin, 5.9 units in a channel, 3.0 in a river, 121.3 in a sea. So
  a basin's floats lie still and only tilt, and on a sea only the barrel stays in the
  water. All of this holds for a float held level: the tilt is left out of the
  waterline, and on a sea, where the barrel's bottom at the top of its bob clears the
  sheet's lowest point by exactly 0 units, the tilt lifts a corner up to its reach x 3
  degrees, 12.7 units (the bound `HDLifeTiltDrop`, `:595`; the two tilts' sum peaks
  at 10.6 for the barrel's 163 and 179 half-widths), over it.
- *The depth* (`HDLifeNeed`, `:851`; `HDLifeOpen`, `:335`): a float needs water at
  least as deep as its lowest point - its draft, its bob up to the top and the drop
  its tilt gives a corner: about 184 units for a barrel on a sea, 162 on a river, 159
  in a basin, 18 for a cloth on the canal, 50 for the canal's bottle. A square
  whose floor lies at the surface is water to none (the sheets' `depth`, the walk down
  to the first floor that is no further water portal). The rule holds where a float is
  rolled (a kind is offered only where the body has such a square, and the float is
  placed on one, by the same draw as before, so a body whose squares are all deep
  enough rolls as it did), where it drifts (shallow water stops it like a bank) and
  where a river float comes back.
- *The school* (`HDLifeSchoolTick`, `:1129`): 4 to 8 `FISH2` on a ring of 150 to 300
  units, half as wide as long, half a square down, rising and sinking 64 units, a 6
  degree yaw wobble at 1.5 hertz, at half the body's light; its middle cruises at 150
  units a second to a deep square it picks again every 6 seconds and keeps 387 units
  (the ring's 300 and half the fish's 173) from water less than 768 deep (the fish's
  lowest point lies 611 under the surface); a body needs six such squares. Lara within
  1024 units sends it to the deep square farthest from her at 300 units a second for 4
  seconds, renewed while she stays near.
- *The drips* (`HDLifeTick`, `:1162`; `put_ripple`, `hd_life.cpp:69`): a body with four
  or more squares whose room is not open air gets one drip for eight, two to six, each
  at a period of 3 to 9 seconds; a drip rings only within six squares of Lara and at
  most once in two seconds a body, so the eight rings a sheet draw shows are not
  crowded. The ring goes into a free slot of the game's `ripples[]` with the fields
  `SetupRipple` writes (flags 0x10 and 1, size 32 and up to 7 more as the engine's own
  drip in `game\joby.cpp`, life 48 and up to 15 more, init 1) - not through
  `SetupRipple`, which draws the life from `GetRandomControl`: the game's own random
  sequence must not depend on what is drawn. `UpdateSplashes` ages it like any other,
  and the sheets take it as a ring (flag 0x10).
- *The frame* (`HDLifeFrame`, `hd_life.cpp:305`, called at the top of `HDFrameDraw`,
  `hd_level.cpp:6884`, not in the inventory ring's frames): the tick at the drawn clock
  of the frame before (one frame's lag), then the entries nearest the eye first, at most
  32, each pushed through `HDObjectPush` with the matrix the stack's base gives its
  point (as Lara's braid takes it) and its body's light as the ambient. The pool is
  built at `hd_level.cpp:5410`, after the objects and the sheets - so at every level
  load, and again when the HD level is rebuilt after the device was recreated, which
  rolls the places anew - and freed with the level (`:5582`); nothing of it runs or
  allocates without the sheets (`hd_water` 0, `hd_enable` 0), and no savegame field
  exists.
- *The getter* (`HDRenderWaterBodySquares`, `hd_render.cpp:13853`, at the end of the
  water block's public functions): a body's squares each place once - corner, surface,
  depth, room, sheet, open air - and its sheet's rise. Read only.
- *`LIFELOG`* with `-log`: a level line, a line per body and a line a second of the
  clock (the manual has the legend). RoomProbe draws the same with `-life <seed>`,
  `-lifelara x,z[,t]` and `-lifebench` (the tools' README).

**Measured.** RoomProbe `-hdwater 1 -life 1` at every level with sheets: ANDREA2 one body
(the canal, class channel, 44 squares, rise 5.9, no current: no sink names its
squares), 12 floats, 0 fish, 5 drips, 0 skipped; ANDY1 two bodies (14 squares each,
class sea, rise 121.3), 4 floats (barrels; 6 lighter floats skipped), 13 fish in two
schools, 0 drips (open air); ANDY3 seven bodies (rivers of 10, 3, 4 and 10 squares, the
lake 42, the shallows 24, the pond of room 145 11), 18 floats, 8 fish in two schools,
2 drips, 10 skipped. ANDREA1, ANDREA3, ANDY2, JOBY2 to JOBY5, RICH1 to RICH3: no life.
The pool takes 1,756, 1,776 and 3,848 bytes; the four models' pages add 5.33 MiB to the
page cache in each of the three levels (4 pages). At most 26 entries drawn in a frame of
the probe, never above 32. The waterline at 1, 3 and 5 seconds (`under=` the surface,
`over=` it, units): the canal's bottle 34.5 to 46.0 under and 34.3 to 45.8 over against
a rise of 5.9, its cloths 7.2 to 15.0 under and 0.9 to 8.7 over (a crest may run over a
cloth, which is what a cloth awash does); the river's barrel 145.0 to 149.4 under
against 3.0, its leaves 8.2 to 14.1; ANDY1's barrels 122.4 to 171.1 under and from 154.4
to 203.2 over against 121.3, ANDY3's sea barrels 121.4 to 170.2 under; the pond's barrel
and cloths lie still, 146.5 and 11.1 under. The floor, against each square's depth (a
copy of RoomProbe that prints every life square's depth): at 3, 20, 60 and 120 seconds
every float's lowest point (draft, bob, tilt) clears the floor of every square its reach
touches, by 71.4 units at the least (the shallows' one barrel on the one square 256
deep; the 23 squares whose floor is the surface take none). Over 20 seconds the canal's
12 floats wander and none reaches a bank (no current); ANDY3's rivers send 11 floats
back upstream by 10 seconds, 19 by 20, 65 by 60 and 131 by 120. The pond's school calm
at 1.9 seconds and fleeing at 2.5, 7 and 12 with Lara standing at its middle (52450,
82300) from 2 seconds. The canal's drips with Lara near: 4 rings written in 12 seconds,
the other falls held by the two-second gap. The cost at 2560 x 1440, `-lifebench`, two
runs: the canal along its length, 9 drawn, GPU 0.0199 to 0.0207 ms, the poses and
matrices 0.005 to 0.006 ms, the draws' submission 0.031 to 0.033 ms; ANDY3's river, 9
drawn, GPU 0.0080 ms; ANDY3's pond, 8 drawn, GPU 0.0209 ms; a step of the pool takes
from 0.0010 to 0.0044 ms. A first draw of the models in a fresh process costs the probe
up to 225 ms of GPU time on some views; the engine preloads its models and pages at
level load (`specific\file.cpp`), the probe its buffers only.

**Checked.** The classic path, 6 of 6 md5-identical to `8691e82` (ANDREA2 231, JOBY2
66, ANDY3 34, with and without the depth texture bound); the fifteen cameras with
`-hdwater 0`, 15 of 15 identical to the water round's parity set, and with `-hdwater
1` and no `-life`, 15 of 15 identical to `aed63ba`; no shader and no `.inc` changed;
the suites (ModernTest 14753 with 32 new checks of the life, MenuTest 42627,
InterpTest 729, LipsTest 270 and 243) 0 failed; the engine and every tool build. The
canal's pictures at 1 and 5 seconds are md5-identical before and after the depth rule
(every canal square is 1024 deep or more), and 5 seconds twice gives the same picture.

**Left.** The look in the game: nobody in this round could play it. The exact bob on
the sheet's rows (D3 a), so that floats ride a sea's waves; until then ANDY1's pools,
class sea, carry barrels only, and ANDY3's lake and shallows too. ANDREA2's canal has
no current, so its floats wander and do not collect at the grate; a `flow` row would
give it one. Floats drift under the piers and decks that stand over sheet squares
(ANDY1). No falling drop is drawn, only its ring. The spring of ANDREA2 room 194 is in
since the night's lows (`dd35bc6`): a default ring source in the engine's own row for
the room, and a current away from it for the body's floats (`HDLifeSpringPush`,
`hd_life_rules.h` :444; 40 units a second at the spring, nothing 1536 out); the basin
takes no floats under ANDREA2's life row, so in the game the current waits for them.
Oil (D6), fireflies and midges (D7), the cans of JOBY5's shelf art (D9 c), light
shafts (D11), the dive's splash (D12). No picture draws through the game's own path
(`view_at`, `HDObjectPush`): RoomProbe `-life` draws its twin with `HDModelDraw`, and
the engine's matrices were checked by reading only. The tilt lifts a sea barrel's
corner up to 12.7 units over the sheet's lowest point (*the bob*); counting it in the
fit and the bob's height would halve the sea barrel's bob (25 to 12.7) and the canal
cloths' (4 to 2.4) and is the owner's to judge. A device reset in the middle of a level
rebuilds the HD level and rolls the places anew, so floats and schools jump after an
alt-tab or a lost device; keeping them needs the pool compared against the rebuilt
bodies. A drip's ring takes a free slot of the game's 128 ripples, and `SetupRipple`
returns before its `GetRandomControl` calls when all are taken, so a full table would
let the game's random sequence depend on what is drawn; a life ring lives about 1.2
seconds, one per body in two seconds at most. With Lara standing at the pond's middle
its school stays in flight.

**What the review found.** A float had no depth rule, and both barrels of ANDY3's
shallows stood in the floor (medium): fixed by *the depth*. No picture draws through
the game's own path: left, for the play test. The tilt lifts a corner over the sheet:
the claim is narrowed to a float held level and the number given, the rest left. The
record and the ledger put a river's sink a quarter square past the end: corrected to
past the last row's middle. Stale comments (the bank's margin, the build's parameters,
the kinds ANDY1's pools take) and numbers without a reason (the light's 128 and 255,
the sun's 0.75, the hash's constants): rewritten. The re-roll after a device reset:
named here and in the manual, the rest left. A full ripple table: left. The fish's
facing: measured with ModelProbe, +x is right.

**Commits.** `9c1381a`, `0e1ea4b`, `e4f4251`, `1fc81d3`, `2a36718`, `ac81bfd`, `05a0502`,

**Round 2, after the owner's play test.** The owner played the first round on
2026-10-11 and was content with it as a whole; for the life he asked for seven things,
here in his words put into English. The river floats pop up in the middle of the
water and vanish at the end with a pop; every river has a slot 256 high where the
water comes from and goes to - the floats should come out of the hole, surface, drift
on the surface and at the end go down into the drain and fade away, which masks it a
little. The fish do not flee from Lara, they only hang about in their school. The
drips from the ceiling stone: where are they - he saw none. The barrel is fine; big
things in the water should make the round rings Lara makes when she swims. The canal
of ANDREA2 should carry its floats to the grate (his "yes, with small extra
adjustments" - the adjustments are his to come; this round built the plain current).
The floats jump to new places after alt-enter; fix it if that is simple. And there
are no fish in RICH2's aquarium yet. The thirteen questions above stay as built.

How. All of it in `hd_life_rules.h` as pure functions with the engine's side in
`hd_life.cpp`; the canal's current is a row of the water module's compiled river
table.

- *The river's ends* (`HDLifeRiverEnds`, `HDLifeDiveShare`, `HDLifeOnRun`,
  `HDLifeComeBack`). Measured first, with SectorCheck on the classic `ANDY3.TRC`: past
  the last sheet row of each of the four rivers, along the flow, lies a dry floor 256
  to 768 units over the surface or a wall, and at six of the eight ends the water goes
  on under it - 256 high at four (the sink river's inlet, the 640-river's outlet, the
  two streams' slots over rooms 70 and 66), 1024 at two; the stream over room 70 is fed
  from the side (a wall along its flow), the one over room 66 ends in water closed by
  its height byte. Today's float came back on the first square and left a quarter
  square past the last row's middle, both over the sheet. Now a float comes back at the
  inlet's slot point, 384 units past the first row's edge (more than the 242 a barrel
  reaches across the water, so all of it is under the block), its top 64 under the
  surface; over the first square it rises to its floating place and over the last
  square it dives, both on a smooth step, riding straight with the current there (no
  wander, no bank test); it comes back only once past the outlet's slot point, as far
  past the last row's edge. A model's push takes no alpha (`HDObjectPush`), so the
  light and the sun of a diving float fall to a quarter over the dive - the water's own
  absorption does the same - and the geometry hides the rest. The body's `LIFELOG` line
  ends in `in=` and `out=`, the slot points.
- *The flight* (`HDLifeDartSpeed`, `HDLifeDartWay`, `HDLifeSchoolTick`). Measured
  first with RoomProbe `-lifelara`: the fleeing school swam straight at the deep square
  farthest from Lara at 300 units a second and stopped for good at the first place its
  3x3 test left deep water - 110 units in the two seconds after she came, in ANDY3's
  pond and lake alike; its ring also jumped when the flight doubled its turn. In the
  owner's log the school that fled from second 90 to 103 of ANDY3 was the lake's (Lara
  swam in room 3; she came no nearer than 34,508 units to the pond). Now Lara within a
  square of any fish, or a live splash of the game on the body's water (`splashes[]`,
  read only), sends every fish on a dart of its own: away from the scare, turned by up
  to 25 degrees by a hash so the school breaks up a little, 2,800 units a second
  falling off with a time of 1.5 seconds - 3,093 units, three squares, in the first
  two, a dart a swimmer sees; sliding along the deep water's edge (128 units off it,
  more than `FISH2`'s 87 reach). After 4 seconds the centre goes where the fish are
  (or to the nearest square that holds a school) and they swim back to the ring at 600
  units a second; a new scare 1.5 seconds after the last starts a new dart. Each fish
  turns to its way at 720 degrees a second (`HDLifeFishTurn`) and its school's tail
  beat has a clock of its own, three times as fast in a flight, so neither a dart's
  start nor its end turns a fish or jumps its wobble in one frame.
- *The drips one can see* (`HDLifeDropTicks`, `HDLifeDropFall`, `draw_drops`). The
  ring was the engine's drip size, 32 to 39 - a ring's strength on the sheet is its
  size over 128 times a half, so a quarter of a wading Lara's (112 to 127). The card
  path has callers for a splash and a tank's spray only, so the drop is drawn the
  classic way: as `DrawDrips` draws the game's drips (`Drips[]`), a line of the sort
  list from its head to half a tick's move over it, the tail at half the head's colour
  (120, 160, 208, about one and a half times the middle of a wet Lara's drips). The
  pool holds its drops itself (`HDLifePool::falling`, at most 32) and puts none into
  `Drips[]`: `GetFreeDrip` hands out the first free slot from `next_drip` on, so a
  held slot would move a wet Lara's next drip to another one, and a drip of an even
  slot that lands calls `TriggerDripSplash` and its random draws. It leaves the
  ceiling over the drip point (the
  classic sector's ceiling byte, through the rooms above), falls from rest by 153 a tick
  (the project's 4,300 units a second squared at 30 ticks) as `UpdateDrips` moves it,
  and its ring of 96 to 111 - three quarters of a wading Lara's or more - starts when it
  arrives: 27 ticks from the canal's ceiling at 3,072, 45 from the pond's sky room at
  6,144. The reach of six squares round Lara and the two seconds a body stay; the
  body's line ends in `drips_at=`. ANDY3's drips rang 0 times in the owner's 111
  seconds because Lara never came near the pond.
- *The rings round the barrels* (`HDLifeFloatRings`). A float 160 units high or more -
  the barrel, 326; a bottle is 80, a cloth 16 - writes a ring into the ripples every
  1 to 2 seconds (a hash of the float), 88 and up to 16 more at the top of its bob,
  through the life's own slot fill; a diving river float rings no more.
- *The canal's current* (`kWaterFlow`, a `cls` column). The canal's rows run along its
  longer side, 15 squares along z against 7 along x, toward +z (`water_look`; a crest
  of `WaveSum8` moves along its row's way), its bank foam drifts the same way, and past
  its +z end wall the water goes on under it (water room 133): the drain. A compiled
  river row with class -1 (keep) gives the canal +z at 90 units a second - half its
  rows' 180, one and a half times the floats' wander, a slow sewer of 0.2 m/s; a
  channel's look reads no flow, so only the floats and the `flow=` fields change.
  Floats now keep apart (`HDLifeClear`, 0.75 of their two reaches), so the current lays
  them side by side along the wall. Where the current holds a float square-on against
  a bank - the side arm five squares west of the main channel, its rows z 43,008 and
  44,032 - the float turns along the bank toward the nearest square of its row with a
  way on, at the current's speed (`HDLifeWayOn`), as water a wall stops runs along
  it; the end wall has no way on, so the floats lie along it.
- *The pool kept through a rebuild* (`HDLifeSameBodies`). `HDLevelUnload` alone ends a
  level, so a begin for the same stem with a pool standing is a rebuild after a lost
  device; when the bodies the water module hands out are the same, the pool is kept
  with the models' sizes as loaded now. The level line ends in `kept=`.
- *The fish tank* (`kHDLifeTanks`, `HDLifeAddTank`). RICH2 room 23's tank is an
  alcove behind glass, x 33,792 to 34,816, z 67,584 to 69,632, y -3,840 to -2,816 -
  the only squares where room 23 and its flip 32 differ - with the FISHTANK item 33 in
  front of it. It gets a body of its two squares (class `tank`, `water=-1`) and a school
  of 8 by the pond's rules, half a square under its top; RICH2 gets a life row that
  offers no floats. Whole while the item has not been set off (inactive, its water at
  the 4,096 `InitialiseFishtank` gives it); the shot sets it off, the room flips to the
  empty alcove, and the fish go at once - the classic state has no water level in the
  alcove to fall with, only the spray and the dome over the floor.

**Measured.** RoomProbe `-life 1`, the slot points: ANDY3's sink river in at 43,392
and out at 32,384 (z 19,968), the 640-river 35,456 and 46,464 (z 36,352), the streams
over room 70 48,512 and 44,672 (z 23,040) and over room 66 z 35,200 and 30,336 (x
45,568). Over 30 seconds at one-second steps, 341 river samples: 33 past an edge, every
one with its top 41 units or more under the surface, 26 come-backs, no jump. The
pond's school with Lara at its middle: spread 223 calm, 1,299 half a second after her,
2,900 by three seconds; with a splash at one second it is back together (spread 228)
by twelve. The canal: 0 of 12 floats in the last row at 0 seconds, 5 by 60, 8 by 120,
all 12 by 170, side by side along the wall. The drips: 5 in the canal under ceilings
at 3,072 and 2,304, 2 in the pond from 6,144; a canal drop the pool holds from 8.53
seconds to its ring at 9.43 (27 ticks), its head at 3,108, 3,362, 4,003 and 4,645 at
8.6, 8.9, 9.2 and 9.4 seconds over the surface at 4,864. Over 60 seconds ANDY3's rings
(barrels and the pond's drips) hold 9 of the 128 ripple slots at once at the most,
ANDREA2's 1, ANDY1's 5; at most 5, 2 and 7 rings lie
within 1,024 units of a ring as it starts, of the eight a sheet draw takes. RICH2: 8
fish, the pool 876 bytes (860 before the pool held its drops), one model page. The
cost at 2,560 x 1,440 (`-lifebench`, two runs, against `4f725a8`): the canal 9 drawn,
GPU 0.0016 to 0.0018 ms before and 0.0018 to 0.0020 after; the pond 8 drawn, 0.0048 to
0.0052 either way; a step of ANDY3's pool 0.0061 ms (0.0036 before the floats kept
apart). After the fix pass, against `440be1b`: the canal 0.0017 to 0.0018 ms on the GPU
(0.0020 to 0.0021 before), the pond 0.0052 (0.0053), a step of ANDY3's pool 0.0055 ms;
the drops' lines are the sort list's and not in these figures.

**Checked.** The classic path 6 of 6 md5-identical to `8691e82`; the fifteen cameras
with `-hdwater 0` 15 of 15 identical to the water round's parity set and with
`-hdwater 1` and no `-life` 15 of 15 identical to `4f725a8`; ModernTest's life groups
grown (the river's ends, the drops, the rings, keeping apart, the way on, the keep, the
tank, the flight, the turn), the suites 0 failed; the engine and the tools build.

**Left.** The look in the game - nobody in this round could play it: how dark a
diving float should get, whether 2,800 units a second reads as a fish's dart, whether
the drop's streak is seen at the canal's light. The stream over room 70 is fed from
the side, so its floats come back inside the wall past its upper end. RoomProbe draws
no classic line, so no picture shows the falling drop - only its numbers and its
ring; and it builds its water once, so the rebuild is proven by ModernTest alone. A
flight that its 8-second cap ends with a fish still away from its ring puts that fish

**The fix pass.** The prover found that the life's drop, held in a free odd slot of
`Drips[]`, still moved the game's random sequence: `GetFreeDrip` takes the first free
slot from `next_drip` on, so with a life drop in slot 1 a wet Lara's next drip went to
slot 2 instead of 1, and an even slot's drip that lands calls `TriggerDripSplash` (a
re-statement of `GetFreeDrip` shows it). The pool now holds and draws its drops itself
(above). He also found three of the canal's twelve floats on the side arm's bank still
at 300 seconds, the wander (60 units a second) losing to the current (90): the way on
along a bank (above). And a fish's yaw snapped to its dart's way and its wobble's phase
jumped when the beat tripled: the turn and the beat's own clock (above). The ledger's
entry 169 now says which of its two sentences holds when.

How. All of it in `hd_life_rules.h`; `hd_life.cpp` builds it unchanged.

- *The edge in a flight* (`HDLifeEdgeDistance`, `HDLifeEdgeWay`, `HDLifeTurnWay`). At d
  units from the edge the share of a dart's way that points away from it is at least
  (384 - d) / 512: any way from 896 units off, along the edge at 384, half away from it at
  the stop's 128, so a dart square on to a wall bends along it over its last square and a
  fish the edge holds turns out of it. Along which way: the side its way leans to by more
  than the sine of the dart's 25-degree scatter, square on the side of a hash of the fish
  and the dart (1201). The way turns at the fish's own 720 degrees a second: a first build
  that set it at once turned 95 degrees in one tick in a corner, where the nearest edge
  goes from one wall to the other. A fish whose way back to its ring the edge refuses
  rounds it the same way. 384 is `FISH2`'s 173-unit length and more off the stop.
- *The regroup.* The school regroups where its whole ring keeps the stop, 428 off the edge
  (its widest ring, 300, and the stop), else at the nearest deep square's middle, 512 off
  any edge. The rejoin runs at 600 units a second or faster where a place lies farther
  than that reaches in the time left, and the flight ends within 10 seconds of its last
  dart (6 seconds of rejoin, 8 before): two halves of a school that fled both ways along
  the basin's arm stood 5,300 units apart, the 8 seconds ran out and the last fish jumped
  660 units to its place. After a flight the heading turns to its cruise at 45 degrees a
  second (`HDLifeSchool::steady`): a fish on the widest ring runs 236 units a second more
  as it turns, less than the rejoin's 600.
- *A Lara who stands still* (`HDLifeSchool::seen`). With the edge turn the fish of a pool
  a square or two wide stay in the water's middle, within a square of a bank Lara stands
  on, and darted on without end (7 and 12 darts in 30 seconds on ANDY1's banks in a first
  build): a school she scared is not scared by her again until she has moved 256 units, a
  quarter square, from where she stood at that dart, and once she has, that place is
  forgotten: back at it after she swam off, she scares them again. A swimmer who follows
  keeps them darting; a splash scares them wherever she stands.
- *The tank* (`HDLifeTankBox`, `HDLifeTankAt`). A tank's school never flees. Each fish
  swims a line of its own along the tank's long side: the eight lines set evenly over the
  tank's width less the stop each side, 96 apart (`FISH2` is 26 wide), in the order of a
  hash of the fish (1301), so no two share one; along it a cosine from 215 off one end -
  the stop and `FISH2`'s reach, so the nose stays off the end as it turns - to as far off
  the other, there and back in 20 to 30 seconds by the hash (1303), from a phase of its
  own (1307): 108 to 162 units a second on the mean, the school's cruise of 150 at the
  quickest. It slows to its turn at each end and turns about at its own rate; its depth
  keeps the band's rise and sink.
- *The roam* (`HDLifeRoams`, `HDLifeRoamSteps`, `HDLifeRoamNext`, `HDLifeRoamPick`,
  `HDLifeRoamStep`). A school whose body's deep squares span more than 8 squares roams: it
  keeps for each square of its body when its centre last came to it
  (`HDLifeSchool::been`, counted in squares come to), and picks as its waypoint the deep
  square's middle, 3 steps off at least, whose way runs over the most squares it never
  came to, then over those it came to longest ago; the hash of the school and its count
  of legs (1311) decides between ways that tie. The first square it comes to picks the
  first waypoint, so it starts with the longest way, to the body's far end. It swims
  there square by square on the shortest way over deep squares - a diagonal step
  only where both squares beside it are deep, so every step keeps 512 off the edge - at
  one `FISH2` length a second (175, the pond's cruise of 150 at one length a second), its
  heading turned to its way at 45 degrees a second; the ring and the depth's rise stay
  round it. ANDY3's pond (4 squares), ANDY1's pools (6 and 7), whose schools saw 54 to 64
  percent of their squares in a minute, and the tank keep their cruise. The body's
  `LIFELOG` line ends with `roam=1` or `roam=0`.

(the end of the walkway north of channel 61's mouth, from above), a view from over the
walkway and one along the canal at eye level; the water's pixels split by the path
behind the sheet (`-waterdepthview 1`). The highlight makes the yellow, not the

floor within a square and a half, so its waves stand at their whole height over a
dark body and every slope that faces the highlight's light lights. The channel's
highlight is now 0.4, the river's: the opaque water's median 45 and brightest 2 % 69,
the water a floor shows through 43 to 42, the view at eye level unchanged (no
highlight reaches it). ANDY2's three channel bodies and JOBY5's three take the same.

*The eye at the surface* (`hd_room.hlsl` `WaterVS` "round the eye", `WaterPS` "the
side"; `hd_render.cpp` c148). The play test's log holds the eye at 3258, 28380 in
JOBY2's rain basin for fourteen seconds, from 10 units under the surface at rest to
42 over it, its room flipping between 13 (the water) and 7 (the air). RoomProbe swept
that eye from 96 under to 96 over in steps of 8 at four clock times; scratch probes
painted one branch each. Three states, three causes: the near-white plane over the
surface - 45 to 85 % of the water's pixels had N.V under 0, a slope turned away from
the eye, which made the Fresnel term 1 and laid the sky's horizon colour flat over
them; the flat blue plane - the sheet seen from above, steeply, over 3,584 units of

### The spring (#200)
2026-10-14

**What.** Asked for on 2026-10-09: "In ANDREA2 we have an underwater spring, I find
that quite nice. Could we have, under the spring, a kind of visible rising current, and
build a few small bubbles into the jet? Then the spring would be complete, and we could
scatter it sporadically under water in all levels where it would fit." The spring is
the ring source of ANDREA2 room 194's fountain basin over water room 120 (the middle of
its six water squares, x 54,272 to 57,344, z 31,744 to 33,792): the game itself makes
no ripple there and no item stands there. Since this round a spring is the engine's
own: a point under water with its own hashed clock that rings the sheet over it, sends
a few small bubbles up its jet and bends what stands behind its rising current; the
fountain is the first entry of a compiled table, `hd_water.txt` can change, add or take
away springs, and a hashed rule places a spring now and then in the levels' other
water.

**Why.** Before it the place rang through the ripple field of the compiled override
row for ANDREA2 194 (`kWaterOverride`, put there by the water's life, `dd35bc62`), a
ring of size 80 every 0.7 s with no current and no bubbles; the owner's tuning file
carries the same ring as a `ripple` row. Rings alone read as rain on a pond, not as a
jet.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_spring.h` holds the rules as pure functions, without the
engine and Direct3D (ModernTest includes it); `hd_spring.cpp` builds a level's
springs, hands their rings to the sheets and draws them - its first part reads the
level only through `hd_render.h` and is linked by RoomProbe (`/D HD_SPRING_TOOL`), its
last part is the engine's. `hd_shader/hd_spring.hlsl` holds two pixel shaders,
`ColumnPS` and `BubblePS`, drawn with the cards' vertex shader (`CardVS`'s bytecode,
`hd_room_card_vs.inc`). Every random choice is a hash of the spring's level and place
(the life's mixer), never a generator's draw: the same level and clock give the same
picture.

- *The rings.* One a period, each up to a fifth of a period early or late by hash, so
  the train does not tick; size 80 times the strength (at least 16), the size and the
  period 0.7 s tuned by the owner with his file row - a ring's slope is its size over
  128, so a jet's landing stays under a wading Lara's 112 to 127. They go into the
  sheets' live rings as they are (`HDRenderWaterRingAdd`, without the merge a game
  ripple goes through), from `FeedWaterRipples` once a frame, only for springs within
  6,144 units of the eye (the drips' reach), so far springs do not crowd the 64 kept
  rings; at a spring's first frame or after a jump of the clock the rings of the last
  four seconds go in at their own ages (a ring lives 3.5 s). A `ripple` row of the
  file within a quarter of a square of a spring rings that place already: the spring
  then rings no more, so his present file does not ring twice.
- *The bubbles.* Three a second at strength 1 (the request said two to four: the
  middle), each born at a hashed moment in its slot, over the jet's core within 0.4 of
  the column's half-width. They rise at 200 to 300 units a second by hash: a few
  millimetres of air rise at about 0.25 m/s in still water (110 units at 2.3 mm a
  unit), and the jet carries them faster. The classic bubble (`game/tomb4fx.cpp`,
  `UpdateBubbles`) speeds up a tick at a time without a cap - 883 units a second after
  the basin's 2,304 units, 5.1 s for the rise -, which a bubble in a steady jet does
  not, so its law is not used. They sway in the classic bubble's form (measured there:
  about 20 units one way and 7 the other at 1.42 s), here 8 to 20 units and a third of
  it across at 1.0 to 1.8 s by hash; radius 5 to 12 units, the classic breath bubble's
  drawn size over its rise (`DrawBubbles`: 4 to 7.5 at birth, growing). One in three
  by hash leaves a small ring where it reaches the sheet, 48 to 63 like the classic
  bubble's (`SetupRipple`, flags 2). A bubble is a card facing the eye, premultiplied
  (`BubblePS`: a bright rim from 0.55 to 0.9 of its radius, a faint body, a small
  highlight), soft against the depth texture over 32 units, the cards' distance fog,
  under the water the frame's extinction, from over the water the water's own
  absorption per channel along the eye's path under the surface; its colour the body's
  spray colour as the cards wear it. Both looks were drawn at the fountain's two eyes
  with the same places, sizes and fades: the own card, and the classic sprite
  (`DEFAULT_SPRITES` + 13, sprite 17 of ANDREA2's classic `.TRC`, a 32 x 32 window of
  its page 10 - a dark disc with a bright crescent - times the classic shade 144,
  additive) through the same card path in a probe built for the comparison. They cover
  the same pixels (under the water 368 and 375 at 1 s); the own rim reads brighter
  (the mean change in those pixels 28.4 and 29.3 at 1 and 2 s against 19.5 and 21.2;
  from over the water 22.0 and 20.7 against 19.7 and 17.3) and it takes the body's
  colour and the water's absorption as the cards do, without a classic page in the HD
  path - so the own card stays.
- *The rising current.* A quad on the jet's line from the floor to the sheet, turned to
  the eye in eight rows, half as wide at the floor as 32 units and 96 per step of
  strength (128 at 1) and widening by a tenth of its height as a round jet does. It is
  drawn after the sheets, with the cards, as a multiply: the blend `DESTCOLOR` /
  `INVSRCALPHA` with rgb `a r` and alpha `a`, `r` the ratio of the frame's copy at the
  bent place to the copy at the pixel (floor 0.02, at most 2), `a` the share, whole from
  half the column's weight up - the target becomes `target (1 + a (r - 1))`. Under the
  water, where the target is the
  copy, that is the copy at the bent place: the refraction itself. From over the water
  the sheet writes its pixel whole from the copy (`a = 1`), so a column drawn before it
  would be hidden and one drawn after it in the usual way would paint the floor without
  its water; the multiply moves the floor's pattern inside the sheet's colour and keeps
  its tint and mirror, and adds no light (no milk, no beam). It reuses the copy the
  frame took for the sheets - no second copy. The bend: two octaves of value noise
  (cells 24 units across the line and 96 along it, and half that), rising at 400 units
  a second, at most 96 units of view space at strength 1, strongest on the line and gone
  at the edge as `(1 - u^2)^2`, falling with height as 1,200 over 1,200 plus the height,
  faded over the last eighth at each end; the weight scales the bend, the share follows
  it. A bent place nearer than the column keeps the pixel's own. It fades as the eye
  looks along its line and as its half-width at mid height falls from 16 to 6 pixels.
  The noise's lattice values are a table of 64 by 64 texels the processor fills with the
  life's mixer (`HDSpringNoiseTexel`, a salt per channel; means 127.0 and 128.1, spread
  73.9 and 73.6, neighbours and channels uncorrelated under 0.03), bound with wrap and a
  linear filter, so the shader reads each octave in one fetch at the cell's corner plus
  its smoothed fraction; the rise wraps at 64 cells along, where the table repeats, so
  the pattern never jumps. The first column took its lattice values from a published
  third-party shader hash, uncredited, and took its weight on the bend and on the share
  both, each held under 0.5, at a bend of 32 on square cells of 48: under the water it
  changed 276 to 370 pixels by 8 levels or more and could not be told from the water
  without it. The streaks and the bend of 96 make a band that wavers; 128 on cells of 32
  by 128 smeared the wall. From over the water the column stays faint: it moves the
  floor's pattern inside the sheet's colour, and the basin's floor behind it is dark and
  flat (luminance 20.9, spread 7.9 levels without the water); a bend of the floor as the
  sheet sees it would need a second copy or the sheet's own shader (its depth variant at
  512 slots), and light of its own would be milk. From above the jet shows by its rings
  and its bubbles. With `hd_motion` 0 the bubbles and the column stand at the clock
  motion last had, and the sheets draw no ring, as for every ring.
- *The table.* `kHDSprings`: ANDREA2, room 194, x 55,808, z 32,768, floor y 2,560 (the
  six squares are 2,304 deep under the sheet at 256, RoomProbe `-life` LIFESQUARES),
  strength 1, period 0.7 s. The compiled override row for room 194 keeps its class and
  no longer carries the ripple; a spring marks its body's spring
  (`HDRenderWaterBodySpring`) unless a ripple row marked it, so the life's floats still
  drift away from the fountain.
- *The file row.* `<LEVEL> <room> - spring <x> <z> <strength> [<seconds>]` in
  `hd_water.txt` (`ParseWaterLine`, the numbers read by `HDSpringParseKey`). A row for
  the level and room of a spring of the table changes it - place, strength, and the
  period where it gives one -, strength 0 takes it away; any other row adds a spring,
  whose period is 0.7 s over its strength without seconds. A row whose one key is
  `spring`, with class `-`, tunes no body, so it cannot reset a compiled row's foam.
  Where two sheets lie over one place (the fountain over the sewer), the spring takes
  the one in the row's room, else the highest. The owner's `ripple` row keeps its
  meaning; to have the spring ring his line becomes `ANDREA2 194 - spring 55808 32768
  1.0 0.7`, or goes.
- *The placement rule* (`HDSpringRulePick`). A candidate square draws a sheet over 768
  units of water or more (the life's deep water), lies three squares or more from
  Lara's start and from every opening of its water - a portal through a wall that
  reaches into the water and leads out of the body; a portal with the body's squares
  on both sides only parts two rooms of one water (JOBY2's sea over rooms 42 and 76) -
  and under no static. A body that is no river, has no current, holds no spring of the
  table or the file and has six candidates or more (the life's school size) holds one
  spring in two, by the hash of its level and its first square (least z, then least
  x), at the middle of a candidate the hash picks, strength 0.5 to 1 by hash. One in
  three placed one spring in the fifteen levels, one in two places three in three
  levels - a spring found now and then, not one per pond. The level's facts come from
  the engine as loaded (the build runs before a saved game is restored, so Lara's item
  stands at the level's start) and in RoomProbe from the classic `.TRC`.
- *The key.* `hd_springs`, a DWORD beside the options, read at the level's build with
  `REG_PeekLong` and never written: absent the rule as built, `0` no spring of the
  rule (the table's and the file's stay), `n` one body in two times n.
- *The seam.* `SPRINGLOG` behind `-log` at the level's build, nothing per frame: one
  line for the level (`springs=`, `table=`, `file=`, `rows=` the file's spring rows,
  `dropped=` springs with no sheet over them, `rule=`, `bodies=`, `fit=`,
  `candidates=`, `key=`) and one per spring (`room=`, `x=`, `z=`, `floor=`,
  `surface=`, `strength=`, `period=`, `body=`, `how=table|file|rule`,
  `rings=own|row`). WATERLOG's `spring=` is written before the springs mark theirs.
- *RoomProbe.* With `-hdwater 1` the springs are built and drawn as the engine does
  (`-spring x,z,s` adds one, `-nospring` none, `-springparts 1|2` the columns or the
  bubbles alone); `-springs` prints the SPRINGLOG lines and a SPRINGRULE line per body,
  `-springkey <n>` the key.

### The level load on several cores
2026-10-11

**What.** The HD part of a level load runs on the machine's cores and says in the log
where its time goes. The rooms' build - the vertex buffer, every room's triangles sorted
into draw calls and tagged, the mirror search - runs one room at a time on a pool of
threads and is put together in room order afterwards, so the buffers come out the same on
one thread as on sixteen; the models' texture pages, which decoded on one thread, decode
on the same pool as the rooms' pages. One new registry value, `tomb5.hd_threads` (`0` the
machine's count, the default; never above 16), and new fields at the end of three log
lines and one new line: the `built` line ends in `phases=`, `threads=`, `hash=` and
`hash_ms=`, the `trg=` line in `scan_ms=`, the `models` line in `hash=` and `hash_ms=`,
and `HDLOG level=<L> hd_share ms=` sums the level's whole HD share. The two fingerprints'
time is in their own `hash_ms` and in no other number of the lines.

**Why.** Collected under #199, opened on 2026-10-09 with the loading bar as its first
entry. The owner's log of the build of 2026-10-09 18:38 put the HD share of a level load
at 1.2 to 3.9 s (TITLE 3.9, RICH2 3.7, ANDREA2 3.5, JOBY2 2.8, ANDY3 2.6, JOBY5 2.6, ANDY1
2.4, ANDREA1 2.4, JOBY4 1.2), the room build at 0.7 to 3.0 s on one core (TITLE 3.0, RICH2
2.5, ANDREA2 2.5, JOBY2 1.8, ANDY3 1.5, ANDY1 1.3, ANDREA1 1.3, JOBY5 1.1, JOBY4 0.7), the
models at 0.4 to 1.2 s (their `build_ms` 519 to 1176, `page_ms` 393 to 870), the page
decoding at 0.14 to 0.55 s on sixteen threads. The levers he named: the room build on
several cores or cached, the model builds, the TITLE level (1.85 million vertices). The
night of 2026-10-11 took them in parallel rounds; this is the loading bar's.

**How.** First the measurement, then each lever, each proved by the hash below.

*The phases* (`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp` `HDRenderLevelBegin`; `hd_render.h`
`HDBeginPhase`, `HDRenderBeginPhaseName` :4756): a lap after each part books its time -
`prep` (the sheen field, the gloss seed), `pages` (`HDPageCacheCreate`), `owners` (which
group owns a water mark, the wind, the falls), `verts` (the vertex buffer), `setup` (the
glow parts, the stand holders), `fill` (every group's triangles), `index` (mirrors, sheen,
windows, the index buffer). `hd_level.cpp` (`LoadPhase` :1382) times its own steps before
the build (marks, boxes, gloss, intr, air, pairs, cuts, stand, places) and after it
(tables, statics, sheets, surfaces, frames, objects) with the performance counter, and
`HDLevelLoad` times the `.TRG` scan on the loading thread (`scan_ms` :5005). The built
line (:5722) carries the steps before the build, the read and the build's own parts; the
`hd_share` line (:5861) the scan, the build as one part and every step after it.

*The fingerprint* (`hd_render.cpp` `BuildHash` :4658, `hd_model.cpp` :1852): FNV-1a 64
(`HDFnv64`, `hd_pagecache.h` :436) over the vertex buffer in blocks of 65,536 vertices
(each vertex as `ComposeVertex` :4497 puts it together out of the `.TRG` and its three
mark bits), then every group in group order (each draw call's fields and the index
buffer's bytes it names, the group's cells, flats, pieces, stand ranges and samples), then
the level tables the index fill writes (destructibles, stand covers and their face flags,
stand triangles, book parts and runs, static pieces, clear pages, hits, air pairs, the
counts). The block and group answers are fed in as 8 bytes each. On with `-log` in the
engine, always in RoomProbe and ModelProbe; taken after the build's last lap and reported
apart (`hash_ms`); the models' over each model's vertex and index bytes and its draw
calls' start, count, page slot and node, in build order, timed per model into a running
total (`HDModelHashMs`, `hd_model.cpp` :4185) and reported apart as well. Neither time is
in any other number: `built ms=` and the `begin` step lose `stats.hashMs` (`hd_level.cpp`
:5261), the `objects` step loses the models' share (:5834), and the `models` line's `ms=`,
`build_ms=` and `buf_ms=` lose theirs (`hd_model.cpp` :4129, `hd_object.cpp` :2025).

*The pool* (`hd_pagecache.h` `HDPoolThreads` :354, `HDPoolRun` :370), header-only so that
the suite tests it as the engine runs it: items handed out in index order from an atomic
counter, the calling thread one of the workers, no thread outliving the call, the first
exception thrown again on the caller. The thread count is `tomb5.hd_threads` through
`HDPoolThreads` (1 to 16 kept, above 16 is 16, 0 or less `hardware_concurrency`) -
`DecodeThreads` (`hd_level.cpp` :1403) for the rooms, the same for the models
(`hd_object.cpp` :2005). Sixteen is the page decode's old ceiling, which keeps its batches
of two pages per thread inside the 32-bit address space. Each lever and what it races on:

- The page decode (`hd_pagecache.cpp` :1226) runs its batches on the pool instead of its
own thread loop: a page decodes into its own slot of the batch, the uploads stay on the
calling thread. The models' pages took one thread since the seam for objects - no reason
was written down - and now take the pool's count.
- The vertex buffer (`hd_render.cpp` :5402) in blocks of 65,536 vertices: a vertex reads
the `.TRG` and the mark tables, which nothing writes then, and writes its own slot of the
buffer, of the shimmer marks and of the hash's bits; each block counts into its own row.
The loop wrote every field into the locked WRITEONLY buffer and read three back for its
counters - a read of write-combined memory per vertex; a vertex is now put together on the
stack and stored whole, which alone took TITLE's `verts` from 402 to 33 ms on one thread.
- The index fill (`fill_group` :5721, `FillOut` :5565): a group writes its own slot of
`g_groups` and its own `FillOut` - its index run (with `range.start` and a static piece's
index its own until the join moves them by the run's place), its destructibles, book
parts, stand covers and face flags, stand triangles and static pieces (ids and first flags
moved at the join), its hits and counts (added at the join; the smallest span, the ripple
cap and the add weight folded there), the wind-weighted corners it names and the clear
pages it sees first (counted at the join for the first group, as the one loop's seen flags
did). Two tables the fill used to make on first use are made before it in its own order:
the book runs (`MaterialBookSlots` over group, pass, part; the fill asks
`MaterialBookSlotsMade` :1118, which writes nothing) and every page's plain sheen
(`PageGloss`; the fill asks `PageGlossKnown` :3363). Everything else it reads - the
`.TRG`, the boxes, the intrusion, pair-face, cut, stand, air and place tables, the page
cache - is handed in before the build and written by nobody during it. The groups are
handed out biggest first; the join (after :7561) is in group order.
- The sort of a pass's triangles (:6834) runs stably over their numbers with the same key
and lays the 33-word records out in place, one cycle of the permutation at a time - the
order a stable sort of the records gives.
- The mirror search (`FindMirrors` :2998) one room at a time on the pool, each room's
mirrors in its own row, joined in room order; the other rooms' cells are a sorted list
searched by binary search instead of a hashed set built one insert per triangle.
- The memory of the fill (`kFillBudget` :7561): a group starts when the groups running and
it hold under 96 MiB of triangle records and sort lists, or when nothing else runs - the
page decode's batch budget. Without it RoomProbe's peak commit on sixteen threads stood
160 MiB over one thread's on TITLE. A group holds its share as an `HDByteGate::Share`
(`hd_pagecache.h` :440, taken at `hd_render.cpp` :7600), whose destructor gives the
bytes back and wakes the waiters however the fill ends: a fill that throws
(`std::bad_alloc` in the 32-bit process) reaches `HDPoolRun`'s caller and leaves no
thread waiting for room. ModernTest's `load_pool` checks it on 1, 4 and 16 threads with
an item that throws while it holds its share (30 checks); the build's hash of the
fifteen levels on one thread and sixteen is unchanged by it.

Not a lever: overlapping the page decode with the fill. The fill asks each triangle's page
whether it is part-way clear (`HDPageCacheSlotClear`), which the decode measures; the
device is not created multithreaded, so the uploads stay on the calling thread; and the
decode's batches are budgeted for the 32-bit address space. Batches of four pages per
thread instead of two under the same 96 MiB gave 7 % on TITLE and ANDREA1 and nothing on
JOBY4 and were not kept: the decode is not held up by its batch tails but by its own
throughput, 2,193 ms of TITLE's pages on one thread against 554 on sixteen. The cache of
the built buffers (L3 of the order) was not built - see *Left*.

## 2.5 Sixty frames a second

The engine presents up to sixty pictures a second while its simulation keeps the thirty
logic steps a second it has always had. Nothing of the game's arithmetic moved: what a
frame that carries no logic tick shows is interpolated from the two ticks around it, and
every counter that used to measure time in drawn frames was put on the logic tick
instead. The setting is `tomb5.fps_mode`, default 1 (sixty); `fps_mode 0` is the engine
as it was, and every rule below is guarded so that at that setting no line of it is
reached. Engine paths are relative to `TOMB5 Code/TOMB5`; the design is written out in
the 60 fps plan (not part of the repository). Where TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931 - solves the same problem differently, its idea was
re-derived and credited in the header rather than taken, and nothing of it is copied;
nothing here comes from the Remaster's programs.

### The frame rate option and the clock
2026-09-06 - 2026-09-07

**What.** `tomb5.fps_mode` is a `ulong` in `tomb5_options` (`global/types.h`), read and
written under the registry name `fps_mode`: `0` is thirty presents a second, `1` is
sixty and is the default, `2` hands the pacing to the display. A value above 2 is
clamped back to 1 (`tomb5/tomb5.cpp`). The option is the *Frame rate* row and prints
`30`, `60` or `Display`. The simulation runs thirty logic steps a second in every mode.
The modal screens that stop the world - the pause menu, the load and save screens, the
death menu, the special features, the F4 outfit screen and the loading fade - keep their
two-tick present; the inventory ring and the title screen have since been given the
frame rate by rules of their own.

**Why.** The thirty hertz cap was a single busy wait and nothing else. `Sync()`
(`specific/time.cpp`) counts whole sixtieths of a second (`frequency = pfq / 60`) and
`S_DumpScreen()` (`specific/output.cpp`) waited for two of those ticks before it
presented, while everything downstream was already built for a 60 Hz tick:
`ControlPhase()` (`game/control.cpp`) runs `for (framecount += nframes; framecount > 0;
framecount -= 2)`, where `nframes` is how many sixtieths the frame really took and a
logic step costs two of them. Feeding one tick per present therefore yields sixty
presents and thirty logic steps with no line of the simulation touched. A modal loop
steps its own animation counters once per present and those counters were written for a
thirty hertz present, which is why two ticks is what leaves them alone.

**How.** `gPresentMinTicks` (`specific/output.cpp`, declared in `specific/output.h`)
replaces the constant `2` in `S_DumpScreen`'s wait. `DrawPhaseGame()` (`game/draw.cpp`)
sets it to `GameFrameMinTicks()` around its own present and puts it back to `2` after
`ProfileFrameEnd`, so a frame is judged against the slot it really waited for.
`GameFrameMinTicks()` returns 2 at `fps_mode 0` and while `InventoryActive`, 0 when the
present itself blocks (`fps_mode 2`) and 1 otherwise; `ActiveFpsMode()` reports the mode
the device really got and `TargetPresentHz()` is the same decision as a rate (30 or 60).
The blend factor is `InterpAlphaNow()` (`game/interpolate.cpp`): at `fps_mode 2` it is
the clock (`InterpTickFraction()`), otherwise 1 for any mode but 1, and 1 again for any
frame whose present waits two ticks (`GameFrameMinTicks() >= 2`) - the same test the
display-bound branch makes, so a modal frame is never drawn between two ticks. `DoTitle`
clears `framecount` as `DoLevel` has always done (`game/gameflow.cpp`): the accumulator
survives a level change and the two-ticks-a-present loop returns it to where it started,
so a title entered on the -1 parity read a factor of 0.5 on every frame, every frame
counted as an in-between frame, every counter guarded on the logic tick stood still -
among them `DoScreenFade`, the only thing that sets `DoFade` to 2 - and the fade-in from
black never advanced, leaving a black quad over the menu that swallowed every key. The
clearing costs at most half a logic tick at the moment the title is entered and runs at
`fps_mode 0` too. The *Frame rate* row stands on the *Display* tab of the table-driven
options frame (`game/menu_frame.cpp`) that replaced the tomb5 options pages
(`tomb5/troyestuff.cpp`). At `fps_mode 0` every branch is inert: `gPresentMinTicks` is
2, `S_DumpScreen` reads `while (n < 2)`, `TargetPresentHz()` is 30 and the frame budget
constants are the old ones to the bit. `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/InterpTest.cpp`
carries a `title_cadence` section that runs the title's two-ticks-a-present accumulator
from both parities and checks that no frame of either is a tween frame and that the
logic tick count is unchanged.

### VSync and the rate the monitor sets
2026-09-07

**What.** `tomb5.vsync` (on by default) switches on the vertical sync the port never
had, and `fps_mode 2` waits for nothing of its own and lets `Present` wait for the
panel. The two rows stand together on the *Display* tab; the *Display* row reads
`Display (60)` when VSync is off, because the blocking present is what paces that mode,
and the VSync row reads `on (restart)`, being a device-creation parameter and the one
setting in the build that is not instant. There is no uncapped mode and no path to one:
without a blocking present `ActiveFpsMode()` reports 1 and the sixty hertz spin is back.

**Why.** With the panel pacing the frames the blend factor can no longer come from the
parity of the loop, and two further rules break with it. "`alpha < 1`" is only the same
thing as "this frame carries no logic tick" while the cadence is two frames to a tick;
at 144 Hz it is true on four frames out of five, and every fade, raindrop, corpse and
caption would have stopped. The clock also has to be read on the other side of the flip:
every other present reads `Sync()` first and flips afterwards because there the wait is
the read, but here the wait is inside `Present`, and a `Sync()` taken before it lands
the waiting ticks in the next frame's count - the factor would ask for a state the logic
has not reached and the picture would stand still for a frame at every logic step. A
driver can also lie: a control panel forcing vsync off leaves the device claiming the
interval while `Present` returns at once, and then nothing bounds the loop at all.

**How.** `PresentationInterval` is part of `D3DPRESENT_PARAMETERS`, so the option is
read in `DXCreate` (`specific/dxshell.cpp`) at startup, on Alt+Enter and on a resolution
change, and the device-lost path in `DXShowFrame` resets from the same `PresentParams`.
`DXCreateD3DDevice` checks `caps.PresentationIntervals` first and drops back to
`IMMEDIATE` with a log line rather than failing to create a device; `DXVSyncActive()`
afterwards answers what the device really got. Because `init_tomb5_stuff` runs on the
game thread that `WinMain` starts after the first `DXCreate`,
`load_tomb5_present_settings()` (`tomb5/tomb5.cpp`) reads that one value ahead of time
through the read-only registry helper `REG_PeekLong` - `OpenRegistry` uses
`RegCreateKeyEx` and `init_tomb5_stuff` decides from `REG_KeyWasCreated()` whether to
write the whole set of defaults, so a second reader opening the key early would have
taken a first run's defaults away. `GameFrameMinTicks()` returns 0 for a display-bound
game frame, so the spin is never entered; at 144 Hz two frames out of three come back
from `Sync()` with no whole tick, `ControlPhase(0)` runs no logic step and the frame is
drawn from the clock. `specific/time.cpp` gained `TIME_SubTick()`, how far past the last
tick the clock stands, read without consuming it and deliberately not capped at one;
`InterpRefreshAlpha` (`game/interpolate_math.h`) is `(framecount + subTick + 1) / 2`,
the only mapping that never has to be clamped - the loop spends two ticks per step but
runs one as soon as the accumulator is positive, so the newest state is the world at `S
= 2k+1` and the factor walks 0 to 1 across every logic step at any refresh rate with no
accumulator of its own. The clamp is for hitches and for the early returns inside
`ControlPhase`, both of which draw the newest state, which is what thirty hertz shows on
a slow frame. Logic ticks are counted rather than inferred (`g_tickSerial`, stepped in
`InterpCapturePrev`), and the drawn frame that finds a new one claims the per-tick
counters, so exactly one frame per logic tick steps them whatever the panel does.
`S_DumpScreen` flips first and reads the clock afterwards in this one mode, which leaves
`PROF_SPIN` empty and `PROF_FLIP` carrying the wait. `NoteDisplayBoundPresent` is the
watchdog: six hundred display-bound presents in a row under half the panel's period is
an overridden interval, and the frame rate falls back to the sixty hertz spin for the
session with one line in the log; an iconic window is not counted, because `Present` on
a minimised window can return at once and coming back from the taskbar must not cost the
player the setting. The mode costs one 1/60 s tick more display latency than `fps_mode
1`, which is why 60 remains the default; in exchange the busy wait is gone and the core
that spun inside `while (!Sync());` waits inside the driver. Options rows in
`game/menu_frame.cpp`.

**Commits.** `a785a50`

### The in-between frame: the root snapshot
2026-09-07 - 2026-09-20

**What.** A drawn frame that carries no logic tick shows the midpoint between the two
ticks around it instead of a duplicate of the frame before it. New files
`game/interpolate.cpp`, `game/interpolate.h` and `game/interpolate_math.h` (the
arithmetic alone, so that an offline test can include it). Three call sites are the
whole seam: `InterpCapturePrev()` as the first statement inside `ControlPhase`'s tick
body, before `GlobalCounter++` (`game/control.cpp`);
`InterpBeginFrame(InterpAlphaNow())` as the first line of `DrawPhaseGame` after
`ProfileFrameBegin`; and `InterpEndFrame()` after `S_AnimateTextures`, before
`ProfileFrameEnd` (`game/draw.cpp`). The snapshot holds `items[512]` (position, three
rotations, room, object, anim, frame, valid), `effects[24]`, `hairs[2][7]`, the camera
and Lara's nine aim angles (the torso twist, the head turn and the two arms, eighteen
shorts) - 15.0 KB, beside 10.7 KB for the live values a frame overwrites and 1.1 KB of
touched-index lists, 27 KB of statics before the particle movers join them, with no
allocation and no pointer into the `game_malloc` pool. Only slots that moved in the tick
are touched. A node whose y angle differs by exactly 32768 between two ticks keeps the
live rotation instead of blending it; its position still blends.

**Why.** `InterpCapturePrev` is the first statement of the tick body because when one
`ControlPhase` runs several ticks - a hitch, the two priming ticks of a level start -
each overwrites the last, and what stands at draw time is the state before the final
tick, the only neighbour the drawn state has. `room`, `object`, `anim` and `frame` are
stored so that a slot handed to a different object can be told apart, otherwise a dead
enemy's slot reused by a spawn would be drawn sliding from the grave to the spawn point.
The braid is in the snapshot because `HairControl` derives every link from the head, and
a head that moves half a step while the braid does not is a plait hanging in the air.
Cut scenes are snapped whole as a correctness requirement: their camera is decoded from
a frame index (`game/deltapak.cpp`) and `frigup_lara()` moves Lara from inside
`DrawPhaseGame` itself, so blending the first would fight a decoder and restoring after
the second would undo what it did (the entry *The cut scenes at the frame rate* below
finds otherwise and blends them). The simulation's own generator had to be protected:
the draw path calls `GetRandomControl` in five places and the star twinkle alone takes
four thousand draws out of the logic stream on every drawn frame, so without a restore
two runs of the same level with the same inputs would drift apart between the frame
rates. The half-turn rule answers `turn180_effect` (`game/effects.cpp`), which does
`x_rot = -x_rot; y_rot -= 0x8000` on an animation command - Lara's roll, its second
half, the water roll and four more, seven over her slot in a level and six of them in
every level: on that tick the animation's own root bone turns the other half, so at
thirty the picture is continuous, but the interpolator blends root and pose apart,
`InterpLerpAngle` took exactly half a turn the arbitrary anticlockwise way while the
pose blend was refused on that same tick, and Lara was drawn sideways for one tween
frame. The braid's own flips are the same case: a segment hanging straight down has an
undefined yaw that flips by exactly half a turn from tick to tick, five or six times a
second while she stands still.

**How.** At `fps_mode 1` the blend factor needs no clock: after `ControlPhase` returns,
`framecount` is `-1` when a tick ran and `0` when none did, so the drawn states are `T1,
(T1+T2)/2, T2, ...`. The frame is drawn live instead of blended when there is no
previous state, when `object_number` changed, on a teleport (`abs(dx)+abs(dy)+abs(dz) >
512` in one tick - nothing in TR5 crosses half a sector under its own power in 33 ms, a
terminal fall is about 130 units), on the same test across a room boundary, on a camera
cut, and while `GLOBAL_playing_cutseq` is set, in which case `InterpBeginFrame` returns
before it writes anything. `InterpInvalidate(why)` drops the previous state at a level
and a title start (`game/gameflow.cpp`), in `FreeLevel` (`specific/file.cpp`), when a
savegame is read (`game/savegame.cpp`, beside `JustLoaded = 1`) and on the return from
the inventory, the save screen, the load screen and the pause menu. `InterpBeginFrame`
remembers `rand_1` on an in-between frame and `InterpEndFrame` puts it back
(`GetRandomControlSeed()`, `specific/function_stubs.cpp`), so the consumption per logic
tick is what it is at thirty whatever the drawing code does; the star twinkle
(`DrawStars`, `specific/specificfx.cpp`) and the floor lasers' water pulse are guarded
on top because both write their result back into persistent state. Angles blend the
short way round; Lara's nine aim angles are blended here rather than by the pose machine
because they are per-tick values that come from the player, written by `LookLeftRight`
and the weapon code and read by both halves of `CalcLaraMatrices` through `phd_RotYXZ`.
The half-turn case is named by `InterpHalfTurn` (`game/interpolate_math.h`) - a y
difference of exactly 32768 - and `ApplyNode` (`game/interpolate.cpp`) then leaves the
whole rotation at the live value, the effect negating `x_rot` in the same breath so that
the rotation goes as one; on such a tick the previous animation root offset is also
turned by the same flip before the root-offset blend of the next entry runs
(`InterpRootFlip`, `game/interpolate.h`/`.cpp`, `game/interpolate_math.h`), because the
underwater roll's animation change flips `y_rot` while the two offsets are the same
world point one turn apart and would otherwise drag her through her own pivot by about
140 units - two sign changes are the whole correction, since `Rx(a) * Ry(180) * Rx(a) =
diag(-1, 1, -1)` for every `a`. Of the seven `turn180_effect` animations three reach
that rule on the flip tick, whose tween is refused: the roll 147 fires on its first
frame, so the change 146 to 147 is the flip tick (the owner's `-log` prints `INTERPLOG
root lara anim 146->147 ... flip=1 turned=(9,-376,4) ... kept=(0,0,5)`, and RootProbe
`-grab 146 147 0 0 -51` over ANDREA1 prints the same numbers); the underwater roll 205
fires on a key its rate 1 far-pose rule refuses the tween across; and the tightrope turn
451 fires on the second key of its held far pair. The other four, 48, 207, 210 and 212,
fire on their last frame and step the frame by one on the flip tick, so the pose is
accepted there; that frame belongs to the old yaw and is drawn from turned copies (see
*Lara facing the wrong way for one tick in the jump twists*), and the change that
follows it turns the previous offset the same way (`g_rootTurned`, `game/interpolate.cpp`).
Nothing downstream knows about any of it: `DrawRooms`, `InsertRoom`, `phd_PutPolygons`,
the bucket sorter, the shadows, the lighting, `HDFrameRoom`, `HDObjectNode` and
`HDLaraDraw` read the same globals and get the interpolated ones - not one line of
`specific/hd/` changed, because the HD seam takes its matrices off the engine's own
stack; `HDLOG frame lara` gained `interp=`, what the frame was drawn at, and `INTERPLOG`
gains `halfturn=N` per second (the braid's flips show as `HAIRLOG dyaw 180` on the same
seconds). Nothing of TROne's blend was taken: TROne
records a tick's finished view-space node matrices and replays them blended, in which an
item's half turn and the animation's opposite half have already cancelled, so it needs
no such rule; two larger ways were priced and set aside - blending the composite yaw of
item and root bone, which buys one frame of facing smoothness in a somersault at the
price of a gimbal case where the root bone is pitched, and blending per-node matrices as
TROne does, which is a rewrite of the pose path. Checked by
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/InterpTest.cpp`, sections `angles` (exactly half a turn
either way, and `turn180_effect` from every angle on the 512-unit lattice, is a half
turn; one unit short of it is not) and `root_flip`. At `fps_mode 0` `InterpAlphaNow`
returns 1 and both frame functions return before writing a byte.
